chs.tz: 使用 SQL 管理数据

cards.en:
A database is a collection of structured data in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data. It is designed so that a large amount of data can be stored efficiently. A database does not have to be digital: a waiter's notebook recording seats and orders is a paper database.

Database management includes three tasks:
  • Retrieval of information from a database;
  • Modification, deletion and insertion of data in a database; and
  • Modification of the database structure to meet changing needs.
Everyday applications include ordering systems, automatic teller machines (ATM) and flight reservation systems. Online shops store products, social media store posts and photos, banks store accounts: all are databases. In the exam, when asked to state a database management task, use the three phrases above word for word.
cards.zh:
Database is a collection of structured data in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data. 数据库是电脑系统中一批有结构的数据，方便储存和读取，设计目的是有效率地储存大量数据。数据库不一定是电子的：餐厅侍应用笔记本记下座位和点餐，也是纸本数据库。

数据库管理（database management）包括三项工作：
  • Retrieval of information：从数据库读取资料；
  • Modification, deletion and insertion of data：修改、删除、插入数据；
  • Modification on database structure：修改数据库结构，以配合需要的变化。
日常例子：点餐系统（ordering system）、自动柜员机（ATM）、机票订位系统（flight reservation system）。网店的货品、社交平台的帖子、银行户口都存放在数据库里。考试问“数据库管理工作”时，直接写上面三句英文。

ex.q: A cinema adds a new column to store whether a seat is wheelchair-accessible. Which database management task is this? What about a customer checking which seats are free?
ex.a:
Adding a column changes the table design, so it is modification of the database structure.
Checking free seats only reads data, so it is retrieval of information.
ex.az: 加一个栏位 = 修改数据库结构；查空位 = 读取资料（retrieval）。

cards.t: Paper database vs digital database (library example)
cards.tz: 纸本数据库 vs 数码数据库（图书馆例子）
cards.en:
Activity 1.1 compares a traditional library with an online library management system. In the past, a checkout card under the book cover recorded the borrower, checkout date and due date, and librarians copied this by hand into a log book. This needed a massive amount of effort and was extremely cumbersome.
Traditional methodOnline library management system
Data is recorded on checkout cards and log booksData is stored in the online system
Data must be searched manually from a physical copyData can be searched by the system in a relatively short time
Other advantages you can quote: the computer copy is easy to update and back up, many users can access it at the same time, and searching/sorting is automatic. This is why we now use a DBMS instead of pencil and paper.
cards.zh:
Activity 1.1 比较传统图书馆和网上图书馆管理系统（library management system）。以前书本封底有借书卡（checkout card），记下借书人、借出日期和到期日，图书馆员还要人手抄进记录簿（log book），非常费力和麻烦。
传统方法网上系统
数据写在借书卡和记录簿上Data is stored in the online system
要人手在实体纸本中搜寻Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time
其他可写的优点：容易更新和备份、多人可同时使用、自动搜寻和排序。所以现在用 DBMS 代替纸笔。

ex.q: Give two advantages of an online library system over checkout cards.
ex.a:
1. Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time, instead of manually.
2. Data is stored in the online system, so it is easier to update / back up and can be accessed by several staff at once.
ex.az: 1. 系统可快速搜寻；2. 数据存于系统，容易更新、备份及多人同时使用。

cards.tz: 数据库结构：栏位、记录、数据表
cards.en:
A database organises data as fields, records and tables.
  • Field: a single piece of information (one column, e.g. NAME);
  • Record: a complete set of fields (one row, e.g. all data of one student);
  • Table: a collection of records.
A database can contain many tables, and a DBMS can hold many databases (Fig. 1.8 data hierarchy: DBMS → databases School A, School B … → tables Classroom, Teacher, Student → records → fields). Keep the levels in order: database > table > record > field. In table drawings, the header row lists the field names; each later row is a record.
cards.zh:
A database organises data as fields, records and tables.
  • Field（栏位）：a single piece of information，即一栏，例如 NAME；
  • Record（记录）：a complete set of fields，即一行，例如一个学生的全部资料；
  • Table（数据表）：a collection of records。
一个数据库可有多个数据表，一个 DBMS 可有多个数据库（Fig. 1.8 数据层级：DBMS → School A、School B 等数据库 → Classroom、Teacher、Student 表 → 记录 → 栏位）。层级次序：database > table > record > field。画表时，表头列出栏位名称，下面每一行是一条记录。

ex.q: Table STUDENT has columns SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO and 7 rows of students. How many fields and records does it have? What is '1A' in Ada's row?
ex.a: 4 fields (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) and 7 records. '1A' is the value of the field CLASS in Ada's record.
ex.az: 4 个栏位，7 条记录；'1A' 是 Ada 那条记录中 CLASS 栏位的值。

cards.tz: 设计数据库（DVD 租赁活动）
cards.en:
Activity 1.2 asks you to design three log sheets for a DVD rental store in the early 2000s:
  • DVDs: DVD ID, DVD name, price, age restriction, etc.
  • Members: member ID, name, contact, age, etc.
  • Renting records: member ID, DVD ID, rent date, due date, payable amount, etc.
Notice how the renting sheet uses the IDs to link to the other two sheets instead of copying names. This is the idea behind keys later in the chapter. Aims of the activity: understand the purpose of database design, see why a good design matters for effective management, and identify factors to consider.
A poor database design may lead to problems such as causing data to become unreliable or inaccurate; the performance of the database may be degraded, and its flexibility may also be lost.
cards.zh:
Activity 1.2 要求为 2000 年代初的 DVD 租赁店设计三张记录表：
  • DVD 表：DVD ID、名称、价钱、年龄限制等；
  • 会员表：会员 ID、姓名、联络方法、年龄等；
  • 租借记录表：会员 ID、DVD ID、租借日期、到期日、应付金额等。
留意租借表用 ID 连接另外两张表，而不是重复写名字，这就是本章后面“键（key）”的概念。活动目的：明白数据库设计的目的、好设计对有效管理的重要性、设计时要考虑的因素。
A poor database design may lead to problems such as causing data to become unreliable or inaccurate. The performance of the database may be degraded, and its flexibility may also be lost.（设计差会令数据不可靠、不准确，效能下降，失去弹性。）

ex.q: Why should the renting record sheet store the member ID rather than the member's name and phone number?
ex.a: The member ID identifies one member uniquely (two members may share a name). Storing only the ID avoids copying the phone number into every renting record, so if the phone number changes it is updated in one place, keeping data accurate and reliable.
ex.az: ID 唯一；只存 ID 可避免重复资料，电话改变时只需改一处，数据保持准确。

cards.en:
We often use a database management system (DBMS) to help us manage databases. A DBMS is software that stores the databases and lets us create tables, insert, update, delete and retrieve data.
  • Microsoft Access is a DBMS with a graphical user interface (GUI).
  • MySQL is a DBMS which allows us to manage databases without a GUI (commands typed in a console). Tools such as MySQL Workbench let us use MySQL with a GUI.
This book uses MySQL. (The practice exercises on this site run SQLite in the browser; the basic statements are the same, and differences are noted where they matter.)
cards.zh:
We often use a database management system (DBMS) to help us manage databases. DBMS 是用来储存数据库、建立数据表及插入、更新、删除、读取数据的软件。
  • Microsoft Access：有图形用户界面（GUI）的 DBMS。
  • MySQL：不用 GUI 也可管理数据库（在命令行输入指令）；MySQL Workbench 等工具可让我们以 GUI 使用 MySQL。
课本用 MySQL。本站练习在浏览器运行 SQLite，基本语句相同，有差异的地方会注明。

ex.q: Name a DBMS with a GUI and one usually used without a GUI.
ex.a: Microsoft Access (GUI); MySQL (no GUI, typed commands).
ex.az: Access 有 GUI；MySQL 通常无 GUI。

cards.en:
We use queries to filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data in a DBMS. These queries are written in Structured Query Language (SQL). With a GUI (Fig. 1.7) we can form a query without knowing SQL syntax, but in the exam you must write SQL from scratch.
Keywords from the Compulsory Part (Table 1.1):
FunctionKeywords
RetrievalSELECT FROM
SummarisationGROUP BY
FilteringWHERE / HAVING
SortingORDER BY
Remember: WHERE filters records, HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.
cards.zh:
We use queries to filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data in a DBMS. These queries are written in Structured Query Language (SQL). 查询（query）用来筛选、排序、汇总、更新或删除数据，以 SQL（结构化查询语言） 编写。用 GUI（Fig. 1.7）可以不懂语法也建立查询，但考试要自己写 SQL。
必修部分学过的关键字（Table 1.1）：
功能关键字
读取 RetrievalSELECT FROM
汇总 SummarisationGROUP BY
筛选 FilteringWHERE / HAVING
排序 SortingORDER BY
WHERE 筛选记录；HAVING 在 GROUP BY 之后筛选组别。

ex.q: Which keyword is used for each: (i) count students per class, (ii) list only class 1B, (iii) list by class number?
ex.a:
(i) GROUP BY (summarisation)
(ii) WHERE (filtering)
(iii) ORDER BY (sorting)
SELECT CLASS, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS
ex.az: (i) GROUP BY；(ii) WHERE；(iii) ORDER BY。

cards.t: SHOW DATABASES and the data hierarchy
cards.en:
In a DBMS, there can be multiple databases, e.g. one database for each of School A, B, C and D, each with tables Classroom, Teacher and Student (Fig. 1.8). Because of this, we must know which databases exist and specify which one to use.
SHOW DATABASES gets a list of the databases in MySQL.
SHOW DATABASES;
Result: a one-column list such as SCHOOLA, SCHOOLB, SCHOOLC, SCHOOLD. Note the keyword is plural: SHOW DATABASE is an error. (SQLite has one database per file, so SHOW DATABASES does not exist there.)
cards.zh:
In a DBMS, there can be multiple databases. 一个 DBMS 可以有多个数据库，例如 School A、B、C、D 各一个，每个都有 Classroom、Teacher、Student 表（Fig. 1.8）。所以要先知道有哪些数据库，再指定使用哪一个。
SHOW DATABASES gets a list of the databases in MySQL.
SHOW DATABASES;
结果是一栏清单，例如 SCHOOLA、SCHOOLB、SCHOOLC、SCHOOLD。注意关键字是复数：SHOW DATABASE 会出错。（SQLite 一个档案一个数据库，没有 SHOW DATABASES。）

ex.q: Which statement runs without error: A. SHOW DATABASE  B. show databases ?
ex.a: B. The keyword must be DATABASES (plural). Lower case is fine because MySQL commands are case insensitive.
ex.az: B。要用复数 DATABASES；小写没问题。

cards.en:
If we do not want to use any existing databases, we may create a new database:
CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE;
After this, SHOW DATABASES lists SCHOOLA … SCHOOLE.
Whenever we start MySQL, we must specify which database to use before manipulating any data from tables:
USE SCHOOLE;
Every later CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT … then works on tables inside SCHOOLE. A database name should not contain spaces: CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRE fails, CREATE DATABASE TOWNCENTRE works.
cards.zh:
建立新数据库：
CREATE DATABASE SCHOOLE;
之后 SHOW DATABASES 会列出 SCHOOLA 至 SCHOOLE。
Whenever we start MySQL, we must specify which database to use before manipulating any data from tables. 每次启动 MySQL，处理数据表前都要先指定数据库：
USE SCHOOLE;
之后的 CREATE TABLE、INSERT、SELECT 等都作用于 SCHOOLE 内的表。数据库名称不应有空格：CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRE 出错，CREATE DATABASE TOWNCENTRE 可以。

ex.q: Write the statements to create a database LIBRARY and start working in it.
ex.a:
CREATE DATABASE LIBRARY;
USE LIBRARY;
ex.az: 先 CREATE DATABASE，再 USE。

cards.en:
To store data, we should create a table inside the database first. General form:
CREATE TABLE table (field1 data_type1, field2 data_type2, ...)
Example: a table STUDENT with four fields SID (student identity number), NAME, CLASS and CNO (class number):
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME CHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT)
CHAR(5) means a string of 5 characters at most and INT means an integer. You may define any number of fields, and each field may have a different data type. Every field must have a data type: create table shop (id, name, location) is wrong in MySQL. Fields are separated by commas and the list is wrapped in one pair of brackets; a missing closing bracket is a common error.
cards.zh:
To store data, we should create a table inside the newly created database first. 格式：
CREATE TABLE 表名 (栏位1 数据类型1, 栏位2 数据类型2, ...)
例子：建立 STUDENT 表，有 SID（学生编号）、NAME、CLASS、CNO（学号）四个栏位：
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME CHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT)
CHAR(5) means a string of 5 characters at most and INT means an integer. 栏位数目不限，每个栏位可以有不同数据类型。在 MySQL 中每个栏位必须写数据类型：create table shop (id, name, location) 是错的。栏位之间用逗号分隔，整组用一对括号包住；漏了右括号是常见错误。

ex.q: Write a statement to create table TEACHER with TID (4 characters), NAME (up to 16 characters) and CLASS (2 characters).
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE TEACHER (
  TID CHAR(4),
  NAME CHAR(16),
  CLASS CHAR(2)
);
A statement may be split across lines; it ends at the semicolon.
ex.az: 每个栏位写名称和类型，逗号分隔，最后加分号。

cards.en:
SHOW TABLES gets a list of the tables in the current database. If the current database has STUDENT, TEACHER and CLASSROOM, then
SHOW TABLES;
returns a one-column result listing STUDENT, TEACHER, CLASSROOM. It only lists tables of the database chosen by USE. Related: SHOW CREATE TABLE table shows the full SQL statement to recreate a table (used in 1.7 to find constraint names). In SQLite the equivalent is SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'.
cards.zh:
SHOW TABLES gets a list of the tables in the current database. 如果当前数据库有 STUDENT、TEACHER、CLASSROOM，
SHOW TABLES;
会列出这三个表名。只列出用 USE 选定的数据库内的表。相关指令：SHOW CREATE TABLE 表名 显示重建该表的完整 SQL（1.7 用来找约束名称）。SQLite 对应写法：SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'。

ex.q: A user runs USE SCHOOLA; then SHOW TABLES; Which tables are listed?
ex.a: Only the tables inside database SCHOOLA (e.g. Classroom, Teacher, Student of School A), not tables of other databases.
ex.az: 只列出 SCHOOLA 内的表。

cards.en:
Lab 1.1 shows that typing SHOW DATABASES and pressing Enter gives no response; typing ; afterwards makes MySQL run it; typing SHOW DATABASES; responds at once.
Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. MySQL will not respond until it sees a semicolon. You may type a SQL statement in multiple lines as long as these lines are not separated by a semicolon, e.g.
CREATE TABLE TEACHER (
  TID CHAR(4),
  NAME CHAR(16),
  CLASS CHAR(2)
);
In exam answers the final semicolon is often omitted, as in the textbook solutions; in the console it is required.
cards.zh:
Lab 1.1：输入 SHOW DATABASES 按 Enter，没有反应；再输入 ; 才执行；输入 SHOW DATABASES; 立即有反应。
Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. MySQL will not respond until it sees a semicolon. 分号表示语句结束。一条语句可以分多行输入，只要中间没有分号，例如上面的 CREATE TABLE TEACHER。考试答案可以省略最后的分号（课本答案亦如此），但在命令行必须有。

ex.q: A student types CREATE TABLE T (A INT) and presses Enter. Nothing happens. Why, and how to fix?
ex.a: MySQL has not seen a semicolon, so it is waiting for the statement to end. Type ; and press Enter.
ex.az: 没有分号，MySQL 仍在等待；补上 ; 即可。

cards.en:
MySQL is case insensitive most of the time. Its commands can be written in upper case or lower case. These three are the same:
sHoW dATaBaSes;
SHOW DATABASES;
show databases;
However, it is a good practice that we write our SQL in a consistent way, e.g. keywords in capitals. Be careful: the data values inside quotes are data, so 'Ada' and 'ADA' are different strings (whether they compare equal depends on the DBMS collation; MySQL's default ignores case, SQLite's '=' does not). Write values exactly as stored.
cards.zh: MySQL is case insensitive most of the time. MySQL 大部分情况不分大小写，指令可用大写或小写，上面三句效果相同。不过 it is a good practice that we write our SQL in a consistent way，例如关键字一律大写。注意：引号内的数据值是数据，'Ada' 与 'ADA' 是不同字符串（比较时是否相等取决于 DBMS：MySQL 默认不分大小写，SQLite 的 = 会分）。值要照储存时的写法。

ex.q: Are select * from student and SELECT * FROM STUDENT the same in MySQL?
ex.a: Yes: commands are case insensitive. Use one style consistently.
ex.az: 相同；但应保持一致风格。

cards.en:
We had better not use any symbols, digits and whitespaces in database names, table names and field names. Different DBMS handle them differently. Though not recommended, we may enclose names containing symbols, digits and whitespaces with a backquote (`) to prevent errors:
CREATE TABLE `STUDENT ALT` (
  SID CHAR(5),
  NAME CHAR(16),
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  `CLASS NO` INT
);
Backquotes (`) are not the same as quotation marks ('), which are used to enclose strings and dates. So `CLASS NO` is a field name while 'CLASS NO' is a string value.
cards.zh:
名称（数据库、表、栏位）最好不要用符号、数字和空格，不同 DBMS 处理方式不同。虽不建议，但可以用反引号 (`) 包住含符号、数字、空格的名称以免出错，例如 `STUDENT ALT`、`CLASS NO`。
Backquotes (`) are not the same as quotation marks (')：单引号用来包住字符串和日期。所以 `CLASS NO` 是栏位名，'CLASS NO' 是字符串值。

ex.q: Fix: CREATE TABLE MY SHOP (ID INT)
ex.a: Either remove the space: CREATE TABLE MYSHOP (ID INT) (recommended), or use backquotes: CREATE TABLE `MY SHOP` (ID INT).
ex.az: 去掉空格（建议）或用反引号。

cards.en:
Activity 1.3 trains you to spot statements that cannot run. The correct choices and the reasons:
WrongCorrectReason
SHOW DATABASEshow databaseskeyword is plural
CREATE DATABASE CITY CENTRECREATE DATABASE TOWNCENTREno spaces in names
create table shop (id, name, location)create table shop (id int, name char(30))every field needs a data type
CREATE TABLE HOTEL (HID INT, HNAME CHAR(40), HADDRESS CHAR(40)CREATE TABLE HOTEL (hid INT, hname CHAR(40), address CHAR(40))missing closing bracket
Mixed case in field names (hid) is fine. Checklist: plural keywords, no spaces, data types, matching brackets, commas between fields, quotes around strings.
cards.zh:
Activity 1.3 训练找出不能执行的语句。正确答案和原因：
  • show databases（SHOW DATABASE 少了 S）
  • CREATE DATABASE TOWNCENTRE（名称不能有空格）
  • create table shop (id int, name char(30))（每个栏位要有数据类型）
  • CREATE TABLE HOTEL (hid INT, hname CHAR(40), address CHAR(40))（另一句缺右括号）
栏位名大小写混用没问题。检查清单：复数关键字、无空格、有数据类型、括号配对、栏位间逗号、字符串加引号。

ex.q: Find the error: CREATE TABLE CAR (PLATE CHAR(8) MODEL VARCHAR(30))
ex.a:
A comma is missing between the two field definitions.
CREATE TABLE CAR (PLATE CHAR(8), MODEL VARCHAR(30))
ex.az: 两个栏位之间缺逗号。

cards.en:
When creating a table, we have to define the data type of each field.
Data typeKeywordSizeExample
IntegerINT / INTEGER4 bytes0, 283, -19
Real: floating pointFLOAT / DOUBLE4 / 8 bytes569.1, -27.382
Real: fixed pointDECIMALvariesmoney
Character: fixed lengthCHAR(n)varies'1B 23'
Character: variable lengthVARCHAR(n)varies'rA9@Us'
BooleanBOOL / BOOLEAN1 byte0 (FALSE), 1 (TRUE)
DateDATE3 bytes'2025-12-31'
TimeTIME> 3 bytes'11:30:00'
DatetimeDATETIME> 5 bytes'2025-12-31 11:30:00'
Real numbers are usually stored as floating point numbers. Dates use the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', times 'HH:MM:SS'.
cards.zh:
When creating a table, we have to define the data type of each field. 建表时每个栏位都要定义数据类型（见左表）：整数 INT/INTEGER（4 bytes）；实数 FLOAT（4 bytes）/DOUBLE（8 bytes）浮点、DECIMAL 定点；字符 CHAR(n) 定长、VARCHAR(n) 变长；布尔 BOOL/BOOLEAN（1 byte，0 = FALSE、1 = TRUE）；日期 DATE（3 bytes）、时间 TIME、日期时间 DATETIME。
Real numbers are usually stored as floating point numbers. 日期格式 'YYYY-MM-DD'，时间 'HH:MM:SS'。（SQLite 接受这些类型名称，但内部只有 INTEGER、REAL、TEXT 等几种储存类别。）

ex.q: Choose data types: (i) number of pages, (ii) price 15.50, (iii) whether a book is in stock, (iv) the exact time a notice expires.
ex.a: (i) INT (ii) FLOAT (or DECIMAL) (iii) BOOL (iv) DATETIME
ex.az: (i) INT (ii) FLOAT (iii) BOOL (iv) DATETIME

cards.en:
When character strings, date and time are input into tables, they should be enclosed in single or double quotation marks. Numbers (INT, FLOAT) and Booleans are written without quotes.
INSERT INTO EVENT VALUES (83313, 'History Tour', '2036-04-15', 40, 1)
Common errors: writing a date unquoted (2036-04-15 would be read as the subtraction 2036−4−15 = 2017), writing a currency sign ($14.5) in a number, or writing a date as '24/11/2042' instead of '2042-11-24'. Booleans may be written as TRUE/FALSE or 1/0.
cards.zh: When character strings, date and time are input into tables, they should be enclosed in single or double quotation marks. 字符串、日期、时间要加单引号或双引号；数字（INT、FLOAT）和布尔值不加引号。常见错误：日期不加引号（2036-04-15 会被当作减法 2036−4−15 = 2017）、数字加 $ 符号、日期写成 '24/11/2042'（应为 '2042-11-24'）。布尔值可写 TRUE/FALSE 或 1/0。

ex.q: What is wrong with VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 138, $14.5, 24/11/2042)?
ex.a:
$ must not appear in a number, and the date must be quoted in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format:
VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 138, 14.5, '2042-11-24')
ex.az: 去掉 $；日期加引号并用 YYYY-MM-DD。

cards.tz: CHAR(n) 与 VARCHAR(n) 比较（增润）
cards.en:
CHAR() occupies a fixed size of storage space. A CHAR(100) field stores at most 100 characters, and storing a 5-character string takes the same space as a 100-character string.
VARCHAR() occupies a varied size of storage space. A 5-character string in VARCHAR(100) takes less space than a 100-character one. However, a VARCHAR() field spends extra storage space for the length information and has a slightly worse performance than CHAR().
Rule of thumb:
  • Strings usually of a certain length → CHAR(), e.g. class names '1A', '2C', 8-digit phone numbers.
  • Strings of varied length → VARCHAR(), e.g. student names 'Ben Bu' vs 'Benedict Timothy Carlton Cumberbatch'.
cards.zh:
CHAR() occupies a fixed size of storage space. CHAR(100) 最多 100 个字符，存 5 个字符也占用与 100 个字符相同的空间。
VARCHAR() occupies a varied size of storage space. 在 VARCHAR(100) 存 5 个字符比存 100 个占用较少空间。但 VARCHAR() 要额外空间记录长度，效能比 CHAR() 稍差。
原则：
  • 长度固定 → CHAR()，如班名 '1A'、8 位电话号码；
  • 长度不一 → VARCHAR()，如学生姓名。

ex.q: Choose CHAR or VARCHAR: (i) HKID-like 8-character code, (ii) book title up to 200 characters.
ex.a:
(i) CHAR(8): always the same length, no length overhead, better performance.
(ii) VARCHAR(200): titles vary a lot in length, so it saves space.
ex.az: (i) CHAR(8)；(ii) VARCHAR(200)。

cards.en:
If numbers with leading zeros, such as '000123' and '034930', are stored as numeric values, i.e. INT or FLOAT, the leading zeros will be removed, giving 123 and 34930. We should store such numbers as character strings, i.e. CHAR() or VARCHAR() instead.
Decide by reading the field description: 'a 4-digit identity code which may begin with zeros' → CHAR(4); 'an identity number ranging from 0 to 999,999' → INT (no leading zeros, smaller storage). Phone numbers, student IDs like '03493' and HKID numbers are codes, not quantities: you never add them, so store them as strings.
cards.zh:
If numbers with leading zeros are stored as numeric values (INT or FLOAT), the leading zeros will be removed. 例如 '000123' 存成 INT 会变成 123。We should store such numbers as character string, i.e. CHAR() or VARCHAR() instead.
看栏位描述决定：“4 位编号，可能以 0 开头” → CHAR(4)；“编号范围 0 至 999,999” → INT（没有前导零，占用空间较少）。电话号码、学生编号 '03493' 这类是代码，不会拿来做加减，应存成字符串。

ex.q: SID values look like 03493, 03496. A student defines SID INT. What happens when '03493' is inserted?
ex.a: It is stored as 3493; the leading zero is lost and the SID no longer matches the real ID. Use SID CHAR(5).
ex.az: 会存成 3493，前导零消失；应用 CHAR(5)。

cards.t: Choosing data types to minimise storage (Example 1.1)
cards.tz: 选择数据类型以减少储存（Example 1.1）
cards.en:
Template: CREATE TABLE [table] ([field1] [type1], [field2] [type2], ...). Table names and field names are given; decide each type from the description and sample data.
Example 1.1, table EVENT:
  • EID: unique ID from 0 to 999,999 → no letters or leading zeros → INT (smaller than a string).
  • ENAME: maximum length 255 → VARCHAR(255).
  • EDATE → DATE.
  • FEE: sample 10.5, 59.9 has a decimal part → FLOAT (or DECIMAL), not INT.
  • FINISHED: only 0 or 1 → BOOL.
Accept INTEGER for INT, BOOLEAN for BOOL, CHAR(255) for ENAME.
cards.zh:
格式：CREATE TABLE [表] ([栏位1] [类型1], ...)。表名和栏位名已给出，要从描述和样本数据决定类型。
Example 1.1 EVENT 表：
  • EID：0 至 999,999 的唯一编号，没有字母和前导零 → INT（比字符串省空间）；
  • ENAME：最长 255 → VARCHAR(255)；
  • EDATE → DATE；
  • FEE：样本有 10.5、59.9 等小数 → FLOAT（或 DECIMAL）；
  • FINISHED：只有 0 或 1 → BOOL。
INT 可写 INTEGER，BOOL 可写 BOOLEAN，ENAME 可用 CHAR(255)。

ex.q: Write the CREATE TABLE statement for EVENT described above.
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE EVENT (
  EID INT,
  ENAME VARCHAR(255),
  EDATE DATE,
  FEE FLOAT,
  FINISHED BOOL
)
ex.az: 按以上分析逐个栏位写类型。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.1 Q2: MEMBER has MID (a 5-digit ID), MNAME (max 40), VIP (yes/no), AGE, CREDIT (e.g. 6000, 9500). Write the CREATE TABLE statement.
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE MEMBER (MID CHAR(5), MNAME VARCHAR(40), VIP BOOL, AGE INT, CREDIT FLOAT)
A '5-digit ID' is a code, so CHAR(5); CREDIT is money and may have decimals, so FLOAT.
ex.az: 5 位编号用 CHAR(5)；金额用 FLOAT。

cards.tz: INSERT INTO ... VALUES 插入记录
cards.en:
INSERT INTO stores a new record in a table.
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) VALUES ('03493', 'Ada', '1A', 1)
Parts: table name, the field list in brackets, then VALUES with the values in the same order as the listed fields.
  • If you arrange the values in the same order as the fields in the table, you do not have to specify the fields:
    INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03496', 'Clem', '1B', 15)
  • If you specify the fields, you can arrange the values in any order:
    INSERT INTO STUDENT (CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28, 'Eva', '03505', '1B')
Without a field list you must give a value for every field, in table order.
cards.zh:
INSERT INTO 把新记录加进表中：
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) VALUES ('03493', 'Ada', '1A', 1)
依次是表名、括号内的栏位清单、VALUES 及与栏位次序对应的值。
  • 值的次序与表中栏位次序相同时，可以不写栏位清单：INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03496', 'Clem', '1B', 15)
  • 写明栏位时，值可以任何次序排列：INSERT INTO STUDENT (CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28, 'Eva', '03505', '1B')
不写栏位清单时，每个栏位都要按表中次序给值。

ex.q: Table BOOK(BID, BOOKNAME, AUTHOR, PUBDATE, NUMPAGE, PRICE). Insert: name '2012', author Arthur White, code 2012, price $201.2, published 20 Dec 2012, 2012 pages. (Checkpoint 1.3 Q1(b))
ex.a:
INSERT INTO BOOK VALUES
  ('2012', '2012', 'Arthur White', '2012-12-20', 2012, 201.2)
BID and BOOKNAME are strings (quoted) even though they look like numbers; NUMPAGE and PRICE are numbers; no $ sign; date in 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
ex.az: BID、书名是字符串要加引号；页数、价钱是数字；日期用 YYYY-MM-DD。

cards.en:
We may leave a field empty during insertion. In such a case, this field will have a NULL value, i.e. a lack of value.
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS) VALUES ('03506', 'Gabe', '1C')
CNO is not listed, so Gabe's CNO is NULL (unless the field has a DEFAULT value). Beware that not all fields are allowed to have a NULL value; this property (NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY) is defined during table creation.
Testing for NULL uses IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, not = NULL. NULL is ignored by COUNT(field), SUM, AVG.
cards.zh:
We may leave a field empty during insertion. In such a case, this field will have a NULL value, i.e. a lack of value. 插入时没有给某栏位值，该栏位就是 NULL（“没有值”），除非该栏位有 DEFAULT 值。上例 Gabe 的 CNO 为 NULL。Beware that not all fields are allowed to have a NULL value：NOT NULL、PRIMARY KEY 栏位不可为 NULL，在建表时设定。
判断 NULL 要用 IS NULL / IS NOT NULL，不能用 = NULL。COUNT(栏位)、SUM、AVG 会忽略 NULL。

ex.q: Example 1.2(a): EVENT(EID, ENAME, PIC, EDATE, FEE, FINISHED). Insert (83313, 'History Tour', PIC NULL, 2036-04-15, 40, 1) and (83315, 'Swimming Gala', PIC NULL, 2036-06-08, 0, 0).
ex.a:
Since PIC is NULL for both, omit it from the field list:
INSERT INTO EVENT (EID, ENAME, EDATE, FEE, FINISHED) VALUES
  (83313, 'History Tour', '2036-04-15', 40, 1),
  (83315, 'Swimming Gala', '2036-06-08', 0, 0)
ex.az: PIC 都是 NULL，在栏位清单中省略即可。

cards.en:
Misconception: 'When the field value is 0, it is NULL.'
Correct: When the field value is 0, it is not NULL. It has a data type, number. NULL has no data type.
0 is a real value (e.g. a free event has FEE = 0, a product out of stock has STOCK = 0), while NULL means the value is unknown or missing (e.g. a student whose class number has not been assigned). Likewise an empty string '' is not NULL. Consequences: WHERE FEE = 0 finds free events but not events with NULL fee; COUNT(FEE) counts 0 values but skips NULLs.
cards.zh:
误解：“栏位值是 0 就是 NULL。”
正确：When the field value is 0, it is not NULL. It has a data type, number. NULL has no data type.
0 是真实的值（免费活动 FEE = 0、缺货 STOCK = 0），NULL 表示值未知或缺失（例如未编学号）。空字符串 '' 也不是 NULL。后果：WHERE FEE = 0 找到免费活动，但找不到 FEE 为 NULL 的；COUNT(FEE) 会计算 0，但跳过 NULL。

ex.q: Table P has STOCK values 0, NULL, 5. What do SELECT COUNT(STOCK) FROM P and SELECT COUNT(*) FROM P WHERE STOCK = 0 return?
ex.a:
COUNT(STOCK) = 2 (0 and 5; NULL skipped).
WHERE STOCK = 0 → 1 record. The NULL row is not equal to 0.
ex.az: COUNT(STOCK)=2；STOCK=0 的只有 1 条。

cards.en:
We may insert more than one record at a time. Use comma to separate the records.
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) VALUES
  ('03510', 'Finn', '1B', 7),
  ('03513', 'Dio', '1C', 13),
  ('03517', 'Ben', '1A', 9)
Each record is in its own brackets; the brackets are separated by commas, with no comma after the last record. The statement can also be written in one line. If one record violates a constraint (e.g. duplicate primary key), the whole statement fails and no record is inserted.
cards.zh: We may insert more than one record at a time. Use comma to separate the records. 每条记录用一对括号，括号之间用逗号分隔，最后一条后面不加逗号。整句也可写在一行。若其中一条违反约束（例如主键重复），整句失败，一条也不会插入。

ex.q: Insert two members into MEMBER(MID, MNAME, MTYPE, AGE, CREDIT): 25908 Ada Chan Bronze 26 472.5 and 72330 Eva Wong Gold 23 203.7 (Checkpoint 1.2 Q1(a)).
ex.a:
INSERT INTO MEMBER (MID, MNAME, MTYPE, AGE, CREDIT) VALUES
  (25908, 'Ada Chan', 'Bronze', 26, 472.5),
  (72330, 'Eva Wong', 'Gold', 23, 203.7)
MID ranges 0 to 99,999 so it is an integer (no quotes).
ex.az: 两条记录各一对括号，逗号分隔。

cards.en:
After insertion, we may retrieve the data from specific fields of a table using SELECT FROM.
SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT
returns only the NAME and CNO columns of every record (Gabe's CNO shows NULL).
Note that the SQL result is not the table STUDENT. Using SELECT FROM to retrieve data never changes the data in the actual table. The non-selected fields SID and CLASS are still intact.
We may also retrieve the data from all fields of a table using a wildcard *:
SELECT * FROM STUDENT
cards.zh:
After insertion, we may retrieve the data from specific fields of a table using SELECT FROM. SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT 只显示每条记录的 NAME 和 CNO（Gabe 的 CNO 显示 NULL）。
SQL 结果不是 STUDENT 表本身。SELECT 读取数据永远不会改变表中的数据，没被选的 SID、CLASS 仍然完好。
用通配符 * 读取所有栏位：SELECT * FROM STUDENT。

ex.q: Write a statement to show the member type of the member named Ivy Chau (Checkpoint 1.2 Q1(b)).
ex.a:
SELECT MTYPE FROM MEMBER WHERE MNAME = 'Ivy Chau'
Only MTYPE is asked for, so do not use *.
ex.az: 只要会员类型，不要用 *。

cards.en:
When retrieving data, we may set criteria to filter records.
SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B'
returns Clem 15, Eva 28, Finn 7. The criterion compares a field with a value; strings and dates need quotes. Other comparison operators: <> (or !=), >, <, >=, <=, combined with AND / OR / NOT (explored in later chapters). For a Boolean field, WHERE FINISHED = 1 and WHERE FINISHED = TRUE are the same.
cards.zh: When retrieving data, we may set criteria to filter records. SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' 得到 Clem 15、Eva 28、Finn 7。条件把栏位与值比较，字符串和日期要加引号。其他比较运算符：<>、>、<、>=、<=，可配合 AND / OR / NOT（后面章节）。布尔栏位：WHERE FINISHED = 1 与 = TRUE 相同。

ex.q: Example 1.2(b): show the data of finished events in EVENT.
ex.a:
SELECT * FROM EVENT WHERE FINISHED = 1
'Data' means all fields, so use *. FINISHED = TRUE also works.
ex.az: “data” 指所有栏位，用 *；FINISHED = 1 或 TRUE。

cards.tz: ORDER BY、ASC 与 DESC 排序
cards.en:
When retrieving data, we may also set criteria to sort records.
SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' ORDER BY CNO
→ Finn 7, Clem 15, Eva 28. ORDER BY comes after WHERE.
Data can be sorted in either ascending order (ASC) or descending order (DESC). Since the default sorting order is ascending, adding ASC changes nothing. ORDER BY CNO DESC → Eva 28, Clem 15, Finn 7.
We may sort by more than one field: ORDER BY CLASS, CNO sorts by CLASS first, then by CNO within the same class. Character strings are sorted in alphabetical order (character by character), so '11' comes before '7' if stored as strings.
cards.zh:
When retrieving data, we may also set criteria to sort records. ORDER BY 放在 WHERE 之后。
Data can be sorted in either ascending order (ASC) or descending order (DESC). 默认是升序，加 ASC 结果一样；ORDER BY CNO DESC 为降序。
可按多个栏位排序：ORDER BY CLASS, CNO 先按 CLASS，同班再按 CNO。字符串按字母次序逐个字符比较，所以以字符串储存时 '11' 排在 '7' 之前。

ex.q: Example 1.2(c): show the names of the events sorted by fee in descending order.
ex.a:
SELECT ENAME FROM EVENT ORDER BY FEE DESC
Only ENAME is shown; sorting can use a field that is not displayed.
ex.az: 只显示 ENAME；排序栏位不一定要显示。

ex.q: Show the data of Gold members sorted by age in ascending order (Checkpoint 1.2 Q1(c)).
ex.a:
SELECT * FROM MEMBER WHERE MTYPE = 'Gold' ORDER BY AGE
ASC is optional.
ex.az: ASC 可省略。

cards.en:
We may filter duplicated results by using DISTINCT.
SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT
STUDENT's CLASS column is 1A, 1B, 1B, 1C, 1B, 1C, 1A; the result is just 1A, 1B, 1C. DISTINCT goes right after SELECT and applies to the whole selected row: SELECT DISTINCT CLASS, CNO removes rows only when both CLASS and CNO are the same. It does not change the table.
cards.zh: We may filter duplicated results by using DISTINCT. SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT：原来 CLASS 栏是 1A、1B、1B、1C、1B、1C、1A，结果只有 1A、1B、1C。DISTINCT 紧接 SELECT，作用于整行选出的结果：SELECT DISTINCT CLASS, CNO 要 CLASS 和 CNO 都相同才算重复。不会改变表。

ex.q: Show all existing member types without duplication (Checkpoint 1.2 Q1(d)).
ex.a: SELECT DISTINCT MTYPE FROM MEMBER
ex.az: SELECT DISTINCT MTYPE FROM MEMBER

cards.t: Learning SQL step by step (The Secret of Learning SQL)
cards.tz: 学好 SQL 的步骤（The Secret of Learning SQL）
cards.en:
The textbook's 'Secret of Learning SQL' page sets out three levels:
  1. Beginner: facing a new SQL statement: run the code on a computer and compare the result with the statement and table; study the textbook examples.
  2. Exam-style questions: Level 1, answer questions one by one and check each by trial and error; Level 2, answer a group first, then check them all and tick the correct ones. Start with questions that include sample data; for questions without sample data, create your own sample data and work out the query.
  3. Advanced exam practice: three common types: state the purpose of a given SQL statement; write the output of a statement on given data; write an alternative SQL that gives the same output (e.g. rewrite without joining tables).
The practical exercises on this site follow the same idea: write, run, compare.
cards.zh:
课本“The Secret of Learning SQL”分三级：
  1. 初学：在电脑运行 SQL，对照语句和表看结果；参考课本例子。
  2. 考试题型：第一级逐题作答、在电脑试错；第二级先做一组题，再一次过检查、剔出正确的。先做有样本数据的题；没有样本数据时自己造样本数据来推算查询。
  3. 进阶：三种常见题型：说出 SQL 的目的（purpose）；写出 SQL 的输出（output）；写出得到相同结果的另一个 SQL（例如改写成不用 JOIN）。
本站的实作练习也是：写、运行、对照。

ex.q: A question gives the table PLAYER and asks 'What is the output of SELECT * FROM PLAYER WHERE PID = '001'?'. Which question type is this and how do you answer?
ex.a: It is a write the output question. Draw the result as a table with the header row (field names) and every matching record, showing NULL or default values exactly as stored.
ex.az: 属“写出输出”题：画出含栏位名的结果表及所有符合的记录。

cards.en:
UPDATE changes data in existing records.
UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' WHERE SID = '03517'
Parts: table, SET field = new value, WHERE criterion. Only records matching the criterion change; here Ben becomes Bob.
Updating multiple fields: separate the assignments with commas.
UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Buzz', CLASS = '1B' WHERE SID = '03517'
A new value can also be calculated from the old one, e.g. SET PRICE = PRICE * 0.9. Do not write SET twice or use AND between assignments (SET NAME='Buzz' AND CLASS='1B' is wrong).
cards.zh:
UPDATE 修改已有记录的数据：
UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' WHERE SID = '03517'
依次是表名、SET 栏位 = 新值、WHERE 条件。只有符合条件的记录被修改。
同时更新多个栏位：用逗号分隔：UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Buzz', CLASS = '1B' WHERE SID = '03517'。新值可由旧值计算，例如 SET PRICE = PRICE * 0.9。不要写两次 SET，也不要在赋值之间用 AND。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.3 Q1(c): All books written by Sela Brooks are now $12.4. Update BOOK.
ex.a: UPDATE BOOK SET PRICE = 12.4 WHERE AUTHOR = 'Sela Brooks'
ex.az: 按作者筛选，价钱不加 $。

cards.t: Use a unique field as the criterion
cards.en:
Think About: why use SID = '03517' rather than NAME = 'Ben' to update Ben's record?
SID is an identity number, which is supposed to be unique for each student. Different students may share the same name. We risk updating the wrong student if we use NAME in the criterion.
So when updating or deleting one specific record, put the primary key (or another unique field) in the WHERE clause. When the task really targets a group (all books by one author, all class 1B students), use the group's field.
cards.zh:
Think About：为何用 SID = '03517' 而不用 NAME = 'Ben'？
SID is an identity number, which is supposed to be unique for each student. Different students may share the same name. We risk updating the wrong student if we use NAME in the criterion.
所以更新或删除某一条记录时，WHERE 应使用主键（或其他唯一栏位）。若题目针对一组记录（某作者所有书、1B 班全部学生），才用该组的栏位。

ex.q: Example 1.3(d): Product BA1100 is out of stock. Update PRODUCT.
ex.a:
UPDATE PRODUCT SET STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'
PID is the unique product ID; out of stock means STOCK = 0 (not NULL).
ex.az: 用唯一的 PID；缺货设 STOCK = 0。

cards.t: Danger: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
cards.tz: 危险：UPDATE / DELETE 没有 WHERE
cards.en:
UPDATE usually comes with a WHERE clause, otherwise it will update the whole table.
UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob'
turns every student's name into Bob. 'It would be rare to have a full house of students named Bob', so think twice before executing an UPDATE statement without a WHERE clause.
Similarly, using DELETE without a WHERE clause simply deletes all records from the table:
DELETE FROM STUDENT
The table still exists, but it is empty. Before running UPDATE/DELETE, you can first run a SELECT with the same WHERE to see which records will be affected.
cards.zh:
UPDATE usually comes with a WHERE clause, otherwise it will update the whole table. UPDATE STUDENT SET NAME = 'Bob' 会把全部学生改名 Bob。所以 think twice before executing an UPDATE statement without a WHERE clause.
同样，DELETE 没有 WHERE 会删除表中所有记录：DELETE FROM STUDENT 之后表仍存在，但是空的。执行前可先用相同 WHERE 的 SELECT 看看会影响哪些记录。

ex.q: STUDENT has 7 records. What does UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '2A' do?
ex.a: All 7 records get CLASS = '2A', because there is no WHERE clause.
ex.az: 7 条记录全部改为 2A。

cards.en:
DELETE FROM removes whole records that match a criterion.
DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B'
Clem, Eva, Finn and Buzz (all class 1B) are removed; Ada, Gabe and Dio remain. DELETE removes records, never a single field value: to clear one value use UPDATE ... SET field = NULL. No field list is written (DELETE NAME FROM ... is wrong). Deletion can be blocked by a FOREIGN KEY if other tables still refer to the record (1.6).
cards.zh: DELETE FROM 删除符合条件的整条记录：DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' 删除所有 1B 学生，剩下 Ada、Gabe、Dio。DELETE 删除的是记录，不能只删一个栏位值：要清空某个值用 UPDATE ... SET 栏位 = NULL。DELETE 不写栏位清单。若其他表的外键仍引用该记录，删除会被阻止（1.6）。

ex.q: Delete all products that expired before 2024-01-01 from PRODUCT.
ex.a:
DELETE FROM PRODUCT WHERE EXPIRY < '2024-01-01'
Dates compare correctly in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Products with NULL expiry are not deleted.
ex.az: 日期比较；EXPIRY 为 NULL 的不会被删。

cards.en:
Since one careless mistake is capable of wiping out or drastically changing a table, it is important to make a backup from time to time so that we may roll back the database to its previous state.
Typical careless mistakes: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE, a wrong criterion (NAME instead of SID), DROP TABLE on the wrong table, or ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY that trims leading zeros. A backup is a copy of the database kept somewhere else; restoring it returns the data to the time of the backup (changes after it are lost).
cards.zh:
Since one careless mistake is capable to wipe out or drastically change a table, it is important to make a backup from time to time so that we may roll back the database to its previous state. 一个疏忽就可能清空或大幅改动数据表，所以要定期备份，必要时把数据库还原（roll back）到之前的状态。
常见疏忽：UPDATE/DELETE 漏了 WHERE、条件用错（用 NAME 而非 SID）、DROP 错表、MODIFY 令前导零消失。备份是另存的副本；还原后备份之后的改动会失去。

ex.q: Why should a school make regular backups of its student database? Give one example of a mistake it protects against.
ex.a: Because one careless statement such as DELETE FROM STUDENT (no WHERE) could delete every record. With a recent backup, the database can be rolled back to its previous state.
ex.az: 例如漏写 WHERE 删光记录，可从备份还原。

cards.tz: DROP TABLE 与 DELETE FROM 比较
cards.en:
DROP TABLE deletes the whole table from the database:
DROP TABLE STUDENT
Once a table is deleted, all its records, if any, will be deleted as well.
DELETE FROM STUDENTDROP TABLE STUDENT
Recordsremoved (all, or those matching WHERE)all removed
Table structurekept (empty table remains, can insert again)removed (must CREATE TABLE again)
WHERE allowed?yesno
Statement typedata manipulationstructure (definition)
cards.zh:
DROP TABLE 把整个表从数据库删除：DROP TABLE STUDENT。Once a table is deleted, all its records, if any, will be deleted as well.
比较：DELETE FROM 删除记录（全部或符合 WHERE 的），保留表结构，之后仍可插入；DROP TABLE 删除所有记录和表结构，要重新 CREATE TABLE 才能再用，也不能加 WHERE。

ex.q: After DELETE FROM STUDENT, can you run INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES (...)? After DROP TABLE STUDENT?
ex.a:
After DELETE FROM: yes, the empty table still exists.
After DROP TABLE: no, error 'table does not exist'; the table must be created again.
ex.az: DELETE 后可以；DROP 后不行，要重建。

cards.en:
DROP DATABASE removes a whole database:
DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE
After it, SHOW DATABASES lists only SCHOOLA to SCHOOLD. Once a database is deleted, all its tables, if any, will be deleted as well. This is the most destructive statement in the chapter, so be sure a backup exists. Order of destruction from small to large: DELETE (records) → DROP TABLE (table and records) → DROP DATABASE (all tables).
cards.zh: DROP DATABASE 删除整个数据库：DROP DATABASE SCHOOLE，之后 SHOW DATABASES 只剩 SCHOOLA 至 SCHOOLD。Once a database is deleted, all its tables, if any, will be deleted as well. 这是本章破坏性最大的语句，执行前要确保有备份。破坏范围由小至大：DELETE（记录）→ DROP TABLE（表及记录）→ DROP DATABASE（所有表）。

ex.q: Write statements to remove table TEMP from database SHOP, then remove database OLDSHOP completely.
ex.a:
USE SHOP;
DROP TABLE TEMP;
DROP DATABASE OLDSHOP;
ex.az: 先 USE SHOP 再 DROP TABLE；最后 DROP DATABASE。

cards.en:
Example 1.3 combines 1.3 to 1.5. PRODUCT fields: PID (2 letters + 4 digits), PNAME (max 80), STOCK, PRICE, EXPIRY (if any).
(a) Types: PID contains letters → character; STOCK cannot have a decimal → integer; PRICE usually has decimals → real number / float; EXPIRY → date.
(b)
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
  PID CHAR(6),
  PNAME VARCHAR(80),
  STOCK INT,
  PRICE FLOAT,
  EXPIRY DATE
)
(VARCHAR(6) and DOUBLE accepted but not recommended.)
(c) Insert Smart Candy, $14.5, 24/11/2042, 138 in stock, SN2359:
INSERT INTO PRODUCT VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 138, 14.5, '2042-11-24')
No $ in numbers; dates as 'YYYY-MM-DD'; values in table order.
(d) UPDATE PRODUCT SET STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'
cards.zh:
Example 1.3 综合 1.3 至 1.5。
(a) PID 含字母 → 字符；STOCK 不会有小数 → 整数；PRICE 通常有小数 → 实数；EXPIRY → 日期。
(b) 见左方 CREATE TABLE（PID CHAR(6)、PNAME VARCHAR(80)、STOCK INT、PRICE FLOAT、EXPIRY DATE）。
(c) 插入时数字不加 $，日期写成 '2042-11-24'，不写栏位清单时值要按表中次序：INSERT INTO PRODUCT VALUES ('SN2359', 'Smart Candy', 138, 14.5, '2042-11-24')
(d) 缺货：UPDATE PRODUCT SET STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'

ex.q: The question lists the new product's details in the order name, price, expiry, stock, ID. Why does the INSERT put them in a different order?
ex.a: Without a field list, values must follow the table's field order (PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE, EXPIRY), not the order in the question. Alternatively list the fields: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PNAME, PRICE, EXPIRY, STOCK, PID) VALUES ('Smart Candy', 14.5, '2042-11-24', 138, 'SN2359')
ex.az: 不写栏位清单就要跟表的栏位次序；或写明栏位清单。

cards.en:
To maintain data integrity and validate data input, we should set constraints for a table. A constraint is a rule the DBMS enforces on every insert, update and delete.
Primary key is a field or a combination of fields that store unique data for every record. A table should always have a primary key to identify a record from all other records. Moreover, the value stored in the primary key field cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.
Two properties to memorise: unique and not NULL. Typical primary keys are ID fields: SID, HKID, PID. A table has at most one primary key (which may consist of several fields).
cards.zh:
To maintain data integrity and validate data input, we should set constraints for a table. 约束是 DBMS 在每次插入、更新、删除时都会执行的规则，用来维持数据完整性及验证输入。
Primary key is a field or a combination of fields that store unique data for every record. A table should always have a primary key to identify a record from all other records. Moreover, the value stored in the primary key field cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.
主键两大特性：唯一（unique）及不可为 NULL。常见主键是编号栏位：SID、HKID、PID。一个表最多一个主键（可由多个栏位组成）。

ex.q: Give two properties of a primary key.
ex.a:
1. Its value must be unique for every record (used to identify a record from all other records).
2. Its value cannot be NULL.
ex.az: 唯一；不可为 NULL。

cards.en:
Test each candidate field with three questions: possible to have duplications? available for everyone? possible to change? A good primary key: no duplications, available for every record, does not change.
FieldDuplicates?Everyone has?Changes?
HKIDNo, uniqueYesNo, permanent
ENAMEYesYesYes
SEXYesYesNo
DOBYesYesNo
BANKACNoNo, some have no accountYes
EMAILNoNoYes
Only HKID passes all three, so it is the primary key of HKCITIZEN. BANKAC and EMAIL fail because a primary key cannot be NULL.
cards.zh:
用三个问题测试每个候选栏位：会否重复？是否人人都有？会否改变？ 好的主键：不重复、每条记录都有、不会改变。
HKCITIZEN 例子：HKID 唯一、人人都有、永久不变 → 主键。ENAME 会重复也会改；SEX、DOB 会重复；BANKAC、EMAIL 虽然不重复，但不是人人都有（会出现 NULL），也会改变，所以不能做主键。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.4 Q1(a): SHOP(SID, SNAME, OPEN, PHONE, SEX) and MANAGER(MNAME, PHONE, SEX), where PHONE is the manager's 8-digit personal phone number. Name the primary keys.
ex.a: SHOP: SID. MANAGER: PHONE (each manager has a unique personal phone number; names may repeat).
ex.az: SHOP 用 SID；MANAGER 用 PHONE。

cards.en:
Set a primary key when creating a table:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
  SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,
  NAME VARCHAR(40),
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  CNO INT
)
In table diagrams, it is optional to underline the primary key field.
Constraint PRIMARY KEY prevents a field from storing duplicated values or NULL by any means, including insertion and updating.
  • Inserting ('03493','Ada'…), ('03496','Clem'…), ('03493','Eva'…) in one statement fails: duplicate 03493, so no record is inserted.
  • Inserting a record without SID fails: SID would be NULL.
  • After inserting 03506 Gabe and 03513 Dio, UPDATE STUDENT SET SID = '03506' WHERE NAME = 'Dio' results in an error.
cards.zh:
建表时设定主键：SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY。表格图中可选择在主键栏位下加底线。
Constraint PRIMARY KEY prevents a field from storing duplicated values or NULL by any means, including insertion and updating.
  • 同一句插入两个 03493 → 整句失败，一条都不插入；
  • 插入时没有 SID → SID 为 NULL，失败；
  • 把 Dio 的 SID 更新为已存在的 03506 → 出错。
（注意：SQLite 的非整数主键因历史原因可接受 NULL，本站练习若要测试，可另加 NOT NULL。）

ex.q: STUDENT(SID PK) contains 03506 Gabe. Which succeed? (i) INSERT ('03507','Ivy','1C',2) (ii) INSERT (NAME,CLASS) VALUES ('Jo','1A') (iii) UPDATE STUDENT SET SID='03506' WHERE SID='03507'
ex.a:
(i) succeeds: new unique SID.
(ii) fails: SID would be NULL.
(iii) fails: 03506 would be duplicated.
ex.az: (i) 成功；(ii) SID 为 NULL 失败；(iii) 重复失败。

cards.en:
We may also set a combination of fields as the primary key of the table. Such a primary key is called a composite key. The same keyword PRIMARY KEY is used, written as a separate line listing the fields:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
  NAME VARCHAR(40),
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  CNO INT,
  PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO)
)
Under this constraint, students are allowed to have duplicated classes or duplicated class numbers. However, every combination of the class and the class number must be unique. E.g. (1B,15) and (1C,15) are fine; two rows of (1C,15) are not. Use a composite key when no single field is unique but a combination is, e.g. PCODE+GCODE for games, FLOOR+RNUM for hotel rooms.
cards.zh:
We may also set a combination of fields as the primary key of the table. Such a primary key is called a composite key. 同样用 PRIMARY KEY，另写一行列出栏位：PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO)。
Under this constraint, students are allowed to have duplicated classes or duplicated class numbers. However, every combination of the class and the class number of a student must be unique. 例如 (1B,15) 和 (1C,15) 可以并存，两个 (1C,15) 就不行。没有单一栏位唯一、但组合唯一时用复合键，例如游戏的 PCODE+GCODE、酒店房间的 FLOOR+RNUM。

ex.q: With PRIMARY KEY(CLASS, CNO), the table holds (Ada,1A,1), (Clem,1B,13), (Gabe,1C,15). Can we insert (Dio,1C,15)? (Ann,1A,15)?
ex.a:
(Dio,1C,15): no, combination 1C+15 already exists.
(Ann,1A,15): yes, 1A+15 is a new combination even though 1A and 15 each appear already.
ex.az: 1C+15 已存在不可；1A+15 是新组合可以。

cards.t: Foreign key: host table and parent table
cards.tz: 外键：host table 与 parent table
cards.en:
Foreign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y. In this relationship, table X is considered as the host table, while table Y is considered as the parent table.
Example: CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME, TEACHER, LOCATION) holds classes 1A to 1D. STUDENT should refer to CLASSLIST so that no student belongs to a non-existing class. So CLASS in STUDENT (host) is a foreign key referring to CLASSNAME in CLASSLIST (parent). The two fields need not share the same name, but they should have the same data type. One parent record (class 1A) can be referred to by many host records (many students).
cards.zh:
Foreign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y. X 称为 host table，Y 称为 parent table。
例子：CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME, TEACHER, LOCATION) 存 1A 至 1D 班。STUDENT 应参照 CLASSLIST，so that no student belongs to a non-existing class。所以 STUDENT（host）的 CLASS 是外键，参照 CLASSLIST（parent）的 CLASSNAME。两个栏位名称可以不同，但数据类型应相同。一条 parent 记录（1A 班）可被多条 host 记录（多名学生）参照。

ex.q: Example 1.4(b): GAME(PCODE, GCODE, GID, GNAME, GENREID, PRICE); PUBLISHER(CODE, NAME, CAPTION); GENRE(ID, NAME, CAPTION). Name two foreign keys of GAME.
ex.a: PCODE (refers to CODE in PUBLISHER) and GENREID (refers to ID in GENRE).
ex.az: PCODE 参照 PUBLISHER(CODE)；GENREID 参照 GENRE(ID)。

cards.en:
Set a foreign key in CREATE TABLE with a separate line:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
  SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,
  NAME VARCHAR(40),
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME)
)
Read it as: FOREIGN KEY (field in host table) REFERENCES parent_table (primary key in parent table). The parent table must be created first, and the referenced field must be its primary key. A table may have several FOREIGN KEY lines. (In SQLite, foreign keys are only enforced after PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;.)
cards.zh: 建表时另写一行：FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME)。读法：FOREIGN KEY (host table 的栏位) REFERENCES parent_table (parent table 的主键)。parent table 要先建立，被参照的栏位要是它的主键。一个表可有多行 FOREIGN KEY。（SQLite 要先执行 PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; 才会检查外键。）

ex.q: Chapter Exercise 1(d) idea: create INTEREST(MCID, MEMID, CHESSID) where MEMID refers to MEMBER and CHESSID refers to CHESS.
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE INTEREST (
  MCID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  MEMID INT,
  CHESSID CHAR(3),
  FOREIGN KEY (MEMID) REFERENCES MEMBER(MEMID),
  FOREIGN KEY (CHESSID) REFERENCES CHESS(CHESSID)
)
Data types must match the parent keys (CHESSID like '001' is CHAR(3)).
ex.az: 两行 FOREIGN KEY；类型要与 parent 主键一致。

cards.tz: 外键的效果（参照完整性）
cards.en:
Constraint FOREIGN KEY prevents a field from storing a value that does not exist in the corresponding field of the parent table by any means, including insertion, update and deletion. With classes 1A to 1D in CLASSLIST:
  • Host side: INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','1E') fails (no class 1E). Inserting Ada in 1A works, but UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '1E' WHERE SID = '03493' results in an error.
  • Parent side: since a student is in class 1A, class 1A in CLASSLIST cannot be renamed to 1E, nor can it be deleted: UPDATE CLASSLIST SET CLASSNAME = '1E' WHERE CLASSNAME = '1A' and DELETE FROM CLASSLIST WHERE CLASSNAME = '1A' both fail. Class 1D (no students) can be deleted.
To delete a referenced parent record, first delete or change the host records that refer to it.
cards.zh:
Constraint FOREIGN KEY prevents a field from storing a value that does not exist in corresponding field of the parent table by any means, including insertion, update and deletion.
  • Host 方：插入班别 1E 的学生会失败；把学生的 CLASS 更新为 1E 也会出错。
  • Parent 方：只要仍有学生属 1A，CLASSLIST 中的 1A 就不能改名为 1E，也不能删除。没有学生的 1D 则可以删除。
要删除被参照的 parent 记录，须先删除或修改参照它的 host 记录。

ex.q: Chapter Exercise 2(c): DELETE FROM RTYPE WHERE RTYPEID = 6 (Presidential Suite) cannot be executed. Suggest a reason and what to run first.
ex.a:
Reason: RTYPEID in ROOM is a foreign key referencing RTYPE, and some rooms in ROOM still have RTYPEID = 6, so deleting it would leave them referring to a non-existing type.
First run e.g. DELETE FROM ROOM WHERE RTYPEID = 6 (or update those rooms to another type).
ex.az: ROOM 仍有房间参照类型 6；先删除或修改这些房间。

cards.en:
There are other constraints in MySQL. They are useful for data validation and shorten our time for data management.
CREATE TABLE STUDENT1A (
  SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,
  NAME VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
  CNO INT UNIQUE,
  HOUSE CHAR(1),
  SCORE INT DEFAULT 0,
  FOREIGN KEY (HOUSE) REFERENCES HOUSELIST(HOUSE),
  CHECK (SCORE >= 0)
)
KeywordEffect
PRIMARY KEYidentifies a record; a foreign key may refer to it; unique and not NULL
NOT NULLvalue cannot be NULL
UNIQUEvalue must be unique for each record
FOREIGN KEYvalue must come from the referenced field (HOUSE in HOUSELIST)
DEFAULTvalue will be 0 if not assigned
CHECKcondition SCORE >= 0 must be TRUE for every record
cards.zh:
There are other constraints in MySQL. They are useful for data validation and shorten our time for data management. 见左方 STUDENT1A 例子及 Table 1.3：
  • NOT NULL：不可为 NULL；
  • UNIQUE：每条记录的值都要不同；
  • FOREIGN KEY：值必须来自 parent table（HOUSELIST 的 HOUSE）；
  • DEFAULT：没有给值时自动用默认值（0）；
  • CHECK：条件（SCORE >= 0）对每条记录都必须为 TRUE。

ex.q: Insert ('03001','Amy',NULL,'R') into STUDENT1A (SCORE not given). What is stored? Then UPDATE STUDENT1A SET SCORE = -5 WHERE SID = '03001'?
ex.a:
Record stored with CNO NULL (UNIQUE allows NULL) and SCORE = 0 (DEFAULT), assuming house R exists in HOUSELIST.
The update fails: CHECK (SCORE >= 0) would be FALSE.
ex.az: SCORE 取默认 0；更新为 -5 违反 CHECK 失败。

cards.t: PRIMARY KEY vs UNIQUE vs NOT NULL
cards.en:
Duplicates?NULL?How many per table
PRIMARY KEYNoNoone (may be composite)
UNIQUENoYes (allowed)many
NOT NULLYes (allowed)Nomany
So PRIMARY KEY ≈ UNIQUE + NOT NULL, plus it is the field used to identify records and the one foreign keys refer to. Use UNIQUE for other fields that must not repeat (shop name, email); use NOT NULL for compulsory fields (name).
cards.zh:
可重复？可 NULL？每表数量
PRIMARY KEY否否一个（可复合）
UNIQUE否可以多个
NOT NULL可以否多个
所以 PRIMARY KEY ≈ UNIQUE + NOT NULL，而且它用来识别记录、供外键参照。其他不可重复的栏位（店名、电邮）用 UNIQUE；必填栏位（姓名）用 NOT NULL。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.4 rule: 'No two shops should share the same name' and 'each field should not be left empty'. Which constraints go on SNAME?
ex.a: SNAME VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL: UNIQUE stops two shops sharing a name; NOT NULL stops an empty name (UNIQUE alone would still allow NULL).
ex.az: UNIQUE NOT NULL 两个都要。

cards.en:
We may also apply more than one keyword to a field, as well as apply a keyword to more than one field.
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
  SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,
  NAME VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TBA',
  CLASS CHAR(2),
  CNO INT,
  UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO)
)
NAME has two keywords; UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO) makes the combination unique (like a composite key, but NULL allowed and not the primary key). Table-level constraints (PRIMARY KEY(...), FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE(...), CHECK(...)) go on their own lines after the fields.
cards.zh: We may also apply more than one keyword to a field, as well as apply a keyword to more than one field. 例如 NAME 同时有 NOT NULL 和 DEFAULT 'TBA'；UNIQUE(CLASS, CNO) 令班别与学号的组合唯一（像复合键，但容许 NULL，也不是主键）。表级约束（PRIMARY KEY(...)、FOREIGN KEY、UNIQUE(...)、CHECK(...)）在栏位之后另起一行。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.4(b): Write SHOP so that no shop opens before 08:00, default opening 09:00, unique shop names, no empty fields except SEX, PHONE refers to MANAGER.
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE SHOP (
  SID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  SNAME VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  OPEN TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '09:00',
  PHONE CHAR(8) NOT NULL,
  SEX CHAR(1),
  FOREIGN KEY (PHONE) REFERENCES MANAGER(PHONE),
  CHECK (OPEN >= '08:00')
)
ex.az: 每条规则对应一个约束。

cards.en:
AUTO_INCREMENT is a feature that can be applied to a primary key field. For a NOTICE table, NID only identifies notices and is not shown on the web page, so there is no need to assign it manually as long as every notice has a unique NID.
CREATE TABLE NOTICE (
  NID INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  AUTHOR VARCHAR(255),
  CONTENT VARCHAR(255),
  CREATETIME DATETIME
)
INSERT INTO NOTICE (AUTHOR, CONTENT, CREATETIME) VALUES
  ('Zack', 'Good morning', '2026-06-02 20:26:26'),
  ('Yen', 'Goodbye', '2026-06-13 19:16:36')
NID will be automatically assigned, starting from 1. In SQLite the same effect comes from NID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (optionally AUTOINCREMENT, no underscore).
cards.zh: AUTO_INCREMENT is a feature that can be applied to a primary key field. NOTICE 表的 NID 只用来识别公告，不在网页显示，只要每则公告 NID 唯一，就不必人手编号。设定 NID INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT 后，插入时不写 NID，NID 会自动由 1 开始编号（1、2、3…）。SQLite 对应写法是 NID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY（可加 AUTOINCREMENT，没有底线）。

ex.q: Three notices are inserted without NID into an empty NOTICE table with AUTO_INCREMENT. What NIDs do they get?
ex.a: 1, 2 and 3, in insertion order (Zack 1, Yen 2, Xeno 3).

cards.en:
GAME(PCODE, GCODE, GID, GNAME, GENREID, PRICE): GCODE is unique only within a publisher; GID = PCODE + GCODE (format XXYYY).
(a) Primary key: either GID or PCODE+GCODE; one field → GID.
(b) Foreign keys: PCODE → PUBLISHER(CODE), GENREID → GENRE(ID).
(c)
CREATE TABLE GAME (
  PCODE CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
  GCODE CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
  GID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY,
  GNAME VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  GENREID INT,
  PRICE FLOAT,
  FOREIGN KEY (PCODE) REFERENCES PUBLISHER(CODE),
  FOREIGN KEY (GENREID) REFERENCES GENRE(ID)
)
(d) GID is redundant: it repeats PCODE and GCODE. PCODE is needed as a foreign key, so drop GID (not PCODE+GCODE) and use PCODE+GCODE as the primary key.
A redundant field stores data that can be derived from other fields or found in another table (e.g. manager's SEX in SHOP is already in MANAGER).
cards.zh:
GAME 表：GCODE 只在同一发行商内唯一；GID = PCODE + GCODE。
(a) 主键可以是 GID 或 PCODE+GCODE；只要一个栏位 → GID。
(b) 外键：PCODE → PUBLISHER(CODE)，GENREID → GENRE(ID)。
(c) 见左方 CREATE TABLE。
(d) GID 是冗余栏位，重复了 PCODE 和 GCODE。PCODE 要作外键，所以删 GID，改用 PCODE+GCODE 作复合主键。
冗余栏位（redundant field）：其数据可由其他栏位推算或在另一表找到，例如 SHOP 中店长的 SEX 已存在于 MANAGER（Checkpoint 1.4(c)）。

ex.q: After dropping GID, write the primary key line for GAME.
ex.a: PRIMARY KEY (PCODE, GCODE)
ex.az: PRIMARY KEY (PCODE, GCODE)

cards.en:
After creating a table, its structure can still be altered. We can add, modify or drop fields and constraints. Note that some of the alterations may result in data loss so we should proceed with caution.
If a table name is spelt wrong:
ALTER TABLE STUDNET RENAME STUDENT
Form: ALTER TABLE old_table RENAME new_table. The records are kept unchanged. MySQL also accepts RENAME TO; SQLite requires ALTER TABLE STUDNET RENAME TO STUDENT.
cards.zh:
After creating a table, its structure can still be altered. 建表后仍可修改结构：新增、修改、删除栏位和约束。部分修改可能导致数据流失，要小心。
表名拼错时：ALTER TABLE STUDNET RENAME STUDENT，格式 ALTER TABLE 旧表名 RENAME 新表名，记录不变。MySQL 也接受 RENAME TO；SQLite 必须写 RENAME TO。

ex.q: Rename table MEMBR to MEMBER.
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE MEMBR RENAME MEMBER
(SQLite: ALTER TABLE MEMBR RENAME TO MEMBER)
ex.az: ALTER TABLE MEMBR RENAME MEMBER

cards.en:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD NAME VARCHAR(40)
Form: ALTER TABLE table ADD field data_type [constraints]. The new field is added at the end. Beware that the newly added field contains no data if it does not have a default value: every existing record gets NULL.
We may include constraints when adding a new field, just like how we define a field when creating a table:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD NAME VARCHAR(40) DEFAULT 'John'
Now every existing record gets 'John'. (SQLite writes ADD COLUMN, MySQL accepts both.)
cards.zh:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD NAME VARCHAR(40)，格式 ALTER TABLE 表 ADD 栏位 数据类型 [约束]，新栏位加在最后。若没有默认值，新栏位没有数据：所有现有记录都是 NULL。
新增时可像建表一样加约束：ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD NAME VARCHAR(40) DEFAULT 'John'，现有记录全部得到 'John'。（SQLite 写 ADD COLUMN，MySQL 两种都可。）

ex.q: Example 1.5(a): add MTYPE to USER with default 'Regular'.
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE USER ADD MTYPE CHAR(7) DEFAULT 'Regular'
Length must be at least 7 ('Regular'/'Premium'); VARCHAR is also fine.
ex.az: 长度至少 7。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.5(c): add SCORE to BOOKCLUB with default 55.5.
ex.a: ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD SCORE FLOAT DEFAULT 55.5
ex.az: FLOAT 加 DEFAULT 55.5。

cards.en:
If a field name is spelt wrong:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT RENAME COLUMN LAME TO NAME
Form: ALTER TABLE table RENAME COLUMN old_field TO new_field. The data in the field is kept; only the name changes. Note the words COLUMN and TO are needed here, unlike renaming a table. This statement works the same in SQLite. Renaming a field does not change its data type or constraints; to change the type you need MODIFY instead. Any SQL statements that use the old name (saved queries, programs) must be updated to use the new name, otherwise they will give an error such as 'unknown column'.
cards.zh: 栏位名拼错时：ALTER TABLE STUDENT RENAME COLUMN LAME TO NAME，格式 ALTER TABLE 表 RENAME COLUMN 旧栏位 TO 新栏位。数据保留，只改名称。注意要写 COLUMN 和 TO（与重命名表不同）。SQLite 写法相同。

ex.q: Rename field PHNO to PHONE in table MANAGER.
ex.a: ALTER TABLE MANAGER RENAME COLUMN PHNO TO PHONE
ex.az: RENAME COLUMN ... TO ...

cards.en:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY SID INT
Form: ALTER TABLE table MODIFY field data_type [constraints].
When changing the data type of a field, the DBMS will also try to convert the data type of all values stored in that field. Such a conversion may result in data loss, e.g. any leading zeros will be trimmed when a character string is changed into an integer: '03493' becomes 3493. If there is any value that cannot be converted properly, the change of data type will fail (e.g. 'AC1389' cannot become INT).
MODIFY redefines the whole field, so constraints not repeated (e.g. NOT NULL) are removed. SQLite has no MODIFY.
cards.zh:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY SID INT，格式 ALTER TABLE 表 MODIFY 栏位 数据类型 [约束]。
更改数据类型时，DBMS 会尝试转换该栏所有值，可能导致数据流失，例如字符串改为整数时前导零会被删去：'03493' 变成 3493。若有值无法正确转换，更改会失败（例如 'AC1389' 不能变 INT）。
MODIFY 会重新定义整个栏位，没有重写的约束（如 NOT NULL）会被移除。SQLite 没有 MODIFY。

ex.q: Example 1.5(d): MTYPE in USER now stores type IDs 0 to 3. Change it to an integer field. What must happen to the data first?
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE USER MODIFY MTYPE INT
Existing values like 'Regular' cannot be converted to integers, so they should first be updated to the IDs (e.g. UPDATE USER SET MTYPE = '0' WHERE MTYPE = 'Regular'), otherwise the change may fail.
ex.az: 先把文字改成编号，否则转换会失败。

cards.en:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP CNO
Form: ALTER TABLE table DROP field. Once a field is deleted, all its values will be deleted as well. Adding back a field with the same name does not help: the re-added field contains NULL or its default. A field used in a constraint (primary key, foreign key) may need the constraint dropped first. SQLite writes DROP COLUMN. Before dropping, check whether the data is still needed elsewhere and make a backup; e.g. a club removing HKID numbers for privacy reasons should be sure no other process depends on them.
cards.zh: ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP CNO，格式 ALTER TABLE 表 DROP 栏位。Once a field is deleted, all its values will be deleted as well. Adding back a field with the same name does not help：重新加回同名栏位只会是 NULL 或默认值。若栏位用于主键、外键等约束，可能要先删除约束。SQLite 写 DROP COLUMN。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.5(a): remove HKID from BOOKCLUB for privacy.
ex.a: ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB DROP HKID
ex.az: ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB DROP HKID

cards.t: Adding and dropping a primary key
cards.en:
When adding constraints, all existing data must not violate the constraints to be added, otherwise such an operation will fail.
Two ways to set an existing field as the primary key:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD PRIMARY KEY (SID)
ALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY
The second requires you to input the data type and cannot set a composite key. If any value of SID is duplicated or NULL, it cannot be set as the primary key.
Drop: 
ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP PRIMARY KEY
Since a table must not have more than one primary key, the name of the primary key field is not specified.
cards.zh:
加约束时，现有数据都不可违反该约束，否则操作失败。
把现有栏位设为主键的两种方法：ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD PRIMARY KEY (SID) 或 ALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY。第二种要写数据类型，且不能设复合键。SID 若有重复或 NULL 值就不能设为主键。
删除：ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP PRIMARY KEY，因一个表只能有一个主键，所以不用写栏位名。

ex.q: Chapter Exercise 2(a): ROOM already has PRIMARY KEY (FLOOR, RNUM). Can ALTER TABLE ROOM ADD PRIMARY KEY (RID) run?
ex.a: No. A table cannot have more than one primary key. Drop the existing one first: ALTER TABLE ROOM DROP PRIMARY KEY.
ex.az: 不能，一表只能有一个主键，要先 DROP PRIMARY KEY。

cards.t: Misconception: adding a new PRIMARY KEY field to a filled table
cards.tz: 误解：在已有数据的表新增主键栏位
cards.en:
Checkpoint 1.5(b): BOOKCLUB has over 500 records. Can this run?
ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD MEMID INT PRIMARY KEY
No. The new field would be NULL (or the same default, 0) for all existing records. However, the PRIMARY KEY constraint forbids the value of a primary key to be NULL or duplicated. Since a primary key should not be NULL, a DBMS usually sets a default value (0 or empty string), so all 500 records get the same value, which is a duplicate. A safe approach: add the field without the constraint, fill unique values with UPDATE, then ADD PRIMARY KEY (or use AUTO_INCREMENT, which numbers existing rows).
cards.zh:
Checkpoint 1.5(b)：BOOKCLUB 已有 500 多条记录，ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD MEMID INT PRIMARY KEY 能否执行？
不能。新栏位在所有现有记录中都会是 NULL（或同一个默认值 0）。但 PRIMARY KEY 不允许 NULL 或重复。DBMS 通常为主键设默认值（0 或空字符串），于是 500 条记录值都一样 → 重复。安全做法：先加没有约束的栏位，用 UPDATE 填入唯一值，再 ADD PRIMARY KEY（或用 AUTO_INCREMENT 自动为现有记录编号）。

ex.q: Explain why the statement fails, in exam wording.
ex.a: MEMID would be NULL / 0 for all records in BOOKCLUB if it were added. However, the PRIMARY KEY constraint forbids the value of a primary key to be NULL / duplicated.
ex.az: MEMID 全部为 NULL/0，违反主键不可 NULL/重复。

cards.t: Adding and dropping foreign keys; SHOW CREATE TABLE
cards.tz: 加入及删除外键；SHOW CREATE TABLE
cards.en:
Add:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASS)
If CLASS in STUDENT contains any value that does not exist in CLASS in CLASSLIST, it cannot be set as the foreign key.
Since there can be more than one foreign key in a table, when dropping a foreign key, we need to specify which one to drop. Each foreign key has a constraint name; find it with
SHOW CREATE TABLE STUDENT
which returns the full statement to recreate the table, including e.g. CONSTRAINT `student_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`CLASS`) REFERENCES `classlist` (`CLASS`). Then:
ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP FOREIGN KEY STUDENT_IBFK_1
cards.zh:
加入：ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASS)。STUDENT 的 CLASS 若有任何值不在 CLASSLIST 中，就不能设为外键。
一个表可以有多个外键，所以删除时要指明哪一个。每个外键都有约束名称（constraint name），用 SHOW CREATE TABLE STUDENT 查看（会显示重建该表的完整语句，例如 CONSTRAINT `student_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY ...），然后 ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP FOREIGN KEY STUDENT_IBFK_1。

ex.q: Example 1.5(e): set MTYPE in USER as a foreign key referring to TID in MTYPELIST.
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE USER ADD FOREIGN KEY (MTYPE) REFERENCES MTYPELIST(TID)
The two fields have different names; that is allowed.
ex.az: 两栏名称不同也可以。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.5(f): make every BOOKCLUB record have a valid group number from BCGROUP(GNUM).
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD FOREIGN KEY (BCGROUP) REFERENCES BCGROUP(GNUM)
GNUM must be the primary key of BCGROUP.
ex.az: GNUM 须为 BCGROUP 的主键。

cards.en:
KeywordAddDrop
NOT NULLALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY NAME CHAR(16) NOT NULLALTER TABLE STUDENT MODIFY NAME CHAR(16)
UNIQUEALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD UNIQUE(EMAIL)ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP INDEX EMAIL
DEFAULTALTER TABLE STUDENT ALTER NAME SET DEFAULT 'John'ALTER TABLE STUDENT ALTER NAME DROP DEFAULT
CHECKALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD CHECK (CNO > 0)ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP CHECK STUDENT_CHK_1
Patterns: NOT NULL is changed by MODIFY (redefine the field); DEFAULT by ALTER field SET / DROP DEFAULT; UNIQUE is dropped with DROP INDEX; CHECK is dropped by its constraint name (e.g. STUDENT_CHK_1, found with SHOW CREATE TABLE; yours may vary). SQLite cannot add or drop these with ALTER TABLE.
cards.zh: 见左表（Table 1.4）。规律：NOT NULL 用 MODIFY 重新定义栏位来加/删；DEFAULT 用 ALTER 栏位 SET / DROP DEFAULT；UNIQUE 用 ADD UNIQUE(...) 加、DROP INDEX 删；CHECK 用 ADD CHECK (...) 加、按约束名称删（例如 STUDENT_CHK_1，用 SHOW CREATE TABLE 查看，实际名称可能不同）。SQLite 不能用 ALTER TABLE 加删这些约束。

ex.q: Checkpoint 1.5(d): make SCORE in BOOKCLUB always greater than 10.
ex.a:
ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD CHECK (SCORE > 10)
Existing data must all satisfy the condition, otherwise it fails (default 55.5 is fine).
ex.az: ADD CHECK (SCORE > 10)。

cards.en:
USER(UID CHAR(8), USERNAME VARCHAR(40), CREDIT FLOAT).
(a) ALTER TABLE USER ADD MTYPE CHAR(7) DEFAULT 'Regular'
(b) Premium → Bronze: UPDATE USER SET MTYPE = 'Bronze' WHERE MTYPE = 'Premium'
(c)(i) SELECT * FROM USER ORDER BY MTYPE (ASC is default) (ii) strings are sorted alphabetically: Bronze, Gold, Regular, Silver, not the 'level' order Regular, Bronze, Silver, Gold. This is a reason to store types as IDs in a separate table.
(d) MTYPELIST(TID INT 0–3, TNAME CHAR(7)); change MTYPE to integer: ALTER TABLE USER MODIFY MTYPE INT
(e) ALTER TABLE USER ADD FOREIGN KEY (MTYPE) REFERENCES MTYPELIST(TID)
cards.zh: (a) 新增 MTYPE，默认 'Regular'。(b) 用 UPDATE + WHERE 把 Premium 改成 Bronze。(c)(i) SELECT * FROM USER ORDER BY MTYPE；(ii) 字符串按字母排序：Bronze, Gold, Regular, Silver，不是等级次序，所以较好用编号另存一个表。(d) ALTER TABLE USER MODIFY MTYPE INT。(e) 加外键参照 MTYPELIST(TID)，两栏名称不同也可以。

ex.q: Sort these strings in ascending order as SQL would: 'Silver', 'Gold', 'Regular', 'Bronze'.
ex.a: Compare first letters: B < G < R < S → Bronze, Gold, Regular, Silver.
ex.az: 按首字母：Bronze, Gold, Regular, Silver。

cards.t: Numbers stored as strings sort wrongly
cards.tz: 数字存成字符串会排错
cards.en:
Chapter Exercise 3: PLAYER has SCORE1 CHAR(2). SELECT PID, SCORE1 FROM PLAYER ORDER BY SCORE1 DESC gives 7, 11, 1, -4: player 002 with 11 is not first.
Reason: SCORE1 is a character string, so it is sorted in alphabetical (character) order, not numeric order. Comparing '7' and '11' character by character, '7' > '1', so '7' comes first in descending order.
Fix: change the field to a numeric type:
ALTER TABLE PLAYER MODIFY SCORE1 INT
then sort again. Lesson: choose numeric types for anything you calculate or sort numerically.
cards.zh:
Chapter Exercise 3：PLAYER 的 SCORE1 CHAR(2)，ORDER BY SCORE1 DESC 得到 7、11、1、-4，最高分的 002（11 分）不在第一。
原因：SCORE1 是字符串，按字符（字母）次序而非数值排序。'7' 与 '11' 逐字比较，'7' > '1'，所以降序时 7 在前。
修正：改为数值类型 ALTER TABLE PLAYER MODIFY SCORE1 INT 再排序。教训：要计算或按数值排序的栏位要用数值类型。

ex.q: Sort '9', '10', '100', '2' ascending as strings.
ex.a: Character order: '10' < '100' < '2' < '9'. As integers it would be 2, 9, 10, 100.

cards.tz: DEFAULT 0 可能掩盖缺失数据
cards.en:
Chapter Exercise 3(d): players present in both rounds get a consolation prize; absent players get none. Should SCORE1 and SCORE2 default to 0?
No. A score of 0 is a valid score (the player was present but scored 0). If the default were 0, an absent player would look the same as a present player who scored 0, and the prize could not be decided. Leaving the default as NULL keeps 'absent' (no value) different from 'scored 0'. This links back to the misconception that 0 is NULL: 0 is a value, NULL is a lack of value.
cards.zh:
Chapter Exercise 3(d)：两轮都出席的玩家有安慰奖，缺席则没有。SCORE1、SCORE2 默认应否设为 0？
不应该。0 分是有效分数（出席但得 0 分）。默认为 0 的话，缺席者与出席得 0 分者无法分辨，就不能决定奖项。保持默认 NULL，可分辨“缺席（没有值）”与“得 0 分”。这正呼应“0 不是 NULL”。

ex.q: Write a query listing PIDs of players who get a consolation prize, assuming absent scores are NULL.
ex.a:
SELECT PID FROM PLAYER
WHERE SCORE1 IS NOT NULL AND SCORE2 IS NOT NULL
ex.az: 两轮分数都 IS NOT NULL。

cards.tz: 本章总结：SQL 语句总表
cards.en:
StatementUsage
SHOW DATABASES / SHOW TABLESlist databases / tables
SHOW CREATE TABLE tableshow the SQL to create the table
USE databaseuse the database
CREATE DATABASE / CREATE TABLEcreate
DROP TABLE / DROP DATABASEdrop
SELECT [DISTINCT] f1, f2 FROM t [WHERE c] [ORDER BY f3 ordering]select data
INSERT INTO t [(f1, f2)] VALUES (...), (...)insert records
UPDATE t SET f1 = v1, f2 = v2 [WHERE c]update data
DELETE FROM t [WHERE c]delete data
ALTER TABLE old RENAME newrename table
ALTER TABLE t RENAME COLUMN old TO newrename field
ALTER TABLE t ADD field type [constraints] / ADD constraintadd field / constraint
ALTER TABLE t MODIFY field type [constraints]modify field
ALTER TABLE t DROP field / DROP constraintdrop field / constraint
Glossary: composite key 複合鍵, data type 數據類型, database 數據庫, DBMS 數據庫管理系統, field 欄位, foreign key 外鍵碼, primary key 主關鍵碼, record 記錄, SQL 結構化查詢語言, table 數據表.
cards.zh:
本章语句总表见左方。记忆方法：数据库层面 SHOW/CREATE/USE/DROP DATABASE；表结构层面 CREATE TABLE、ALTER TABLE（RENAME、RENAME COLUMN、ADD、MODIFY、DROP）、DROP TABLE；数据层面 INSERT、SELECT、UPDATE、DELETE。
术语：composite key 复合键、data type 数据类型、database 数据库、database management system 数据库管理系统、field 栏位、foreign key 外键、primary key 主键、record 记录、Structured Query Language 结构化查询语言、table 数据表。

ex.q: Classify each as working on database, table structure or data: DROP DATABASE, ALTER TABLE ... ADD, UPDATE, CREATE TABLE, DELETE FROM.
ex.a:
Database: DROP DATABASE.
Table structure: ALTER TABLE ... ADD, CREATE TABLE.
Data: UPDATE, DELETE FROM.
ex.az: 数据库：DROP DATABASE；结构：ALTER、CREATE TABLE；数据：UPDATE、DELETE。

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three database management tasks listed in the textbook?
o: Retrieval of information from a database
Modification, deletion and insertion of data
mc.e: The three tasks are retrieval; modification, deletion and insertion of data; and modification of the database structure.
mc.ez: 数据库管理三项工作不包括网络加密。

mc.q: In a database, a single piece of information such as a student's class is a
mc.e: A field is a single piece of information.

mc.q: A complete set of fields describing one student is a
mc.e: A record is a complete set of fields.

mc.q: Which is correct about the data hierarchy?
o: A table is a collection of records
A database is a collection of fields only
mc.e: Database > table > record > field.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of an online library management system over checkout cards and log books?
o: Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time
Librarians must copy data into log books
mc.e: The system searches data quickly instead of manually.
mc.ez: 系统可在短时间内搜寻。

mc.q: Which DBMS described in the textbook has a graphical user interface?
mc.e: Microsoft Access is a DBMS with a GUI; MySQL is used without a GUI (unless via a tool such as MySQL Workbench).

mc.q: Which keyword is used for summarisation?
mc.e: Table 1.1: summarisation uses GROUP BY.

mc.q: Which may be a result of a poor database design?
mc.e: A poor design may make data unreliable or inaccurate, degrade performance and lose flexibility.
mc.ez: 设计差令数据不可靠、不准确。

mc.q: Which statement lists the databases in MySQL?
mc.e: The command is SHOW DATABASES (plural).

mc.q: Which statement can be executed without error?
mc.e: Database names should not contain spaces.

mc.q: Which statement can be executed without error?
o: create table shop (id int, name char(30))
create table shop id int, name char(30)
mc.e: Every field needs a data type and the list must be in brackets after the table name.

mc.q: What is wrong with: CREATE TABLE HOTEL (HID INT, HNAME CHAR(40), HADDRESS CHAR(40)
o: Field names must be lower case
mc.e: The bracket opened before HID is never closed.

mc.q: A user types SHOW DATABASES and presses Enter, but MySQL gives no response. Why?
o: The statement has not been terminated with a semicolon
mc.e: MySQL will not respond until it sees a semicolon.

mc.q: Before manipulating data in tables after starting MySQL, we must
mc.e: We must specify which database to use with USE.

mc.q: Which pair of symbols is correct?
o: Backquotes enclose strings; quotation marks enclose names
Backquotes enclose names with spaces; quotation marks enclose strings and dates
mc.e: `name with space` vs 'string value'.
mc.ez: 反引号包名称，单引号包字符串和日期。

mc.q: In CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), ...), CHAR(5) means
o: a string of 5 characters at most
mc.e: CHAR(5) means a string of 5 characters at most.
mc.ez: 最多 5 个字符的字符串。

mc.q: A field stores 4-digit book codes that may begin with zeros, e.g. 0472. The best data type is
mc.e: Numbers with leading zeros must be stored as strings, otherwise the zeros are removed.

mc.q: Value '000123' is stored in an INT field. What is stored?
mc.e: Leading zeros are removed when stored as a number.

mc.q: Which data type is most suitable for whether an event has finished (1 or 0)?
mc.e: Only 0 or 1, so Boolean.

mc.q: Which is the correct date value format for a DBMS?
mc.e: Dates are written in quotes as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

mc.q: Without quotes, the value 2036-04-15 inserted into a numeric context evaluates to
mc.e: It is read as the subtraction 2036 - 4 - 15 = 2017.

mc.q: Which statement about CHAR and VARCHAR is correct?
o: VARCHAR(100) storing 5 characters uses the same space as 100 characters
CHAR(100) storing 5 characters uses the same space as 100 characters
CHAR needs extra space for length information
VARCHAR has better performance than CHAR
mc.e: CHAR occupies a fixed size; VARCHAR uses extra space for the length and is slightly slower.

mc.q: Which field is best stored as VARCHAR rather than CHAR?
mc.e: Names vary greatly in length.

mc.q: Which data type stores '2025-12-31 11:30:00'?
mc.e: Date and time together use DATETIME.

mc.q: A field EID ranges from 0 to 999,999 with no leading zeros. To minimise storage it should be
mc.e: An integer (4 bytes) is smaller than a 6-character string.

mc.q: Which is NOT a real number data type?
mc.e: INTEGER is an integer type.

mc.q: Which statement inserts a record correctly when values are listed in a different order from the table?
o: INSERT INTO STUDENT (CNO, NAME, SID, CLASS) VALUES (28, 'Eva', '03505', '1B')
mc.e: If you specify the fields, you can arrange the values in any order.
mc.ez: 写明栏位后值可任意次序。

mc.q: After INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS) VALUES ('03506', 'Gabe', '1C'), Gabe's CNO is
mc.e: A field left out during insertion has a NULL value (no default set).

mc.q: Which statement about NULL is correct?
o: NULL has the data type number
When a field value is 0 it is not NULL
mc.e: 0 is a number value; NULL is a lack of value with no data type.

mc.q:
How many records are returned?
SELECT NAME, CNO FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B'
Table STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) holds: 03493 Ada 1A 1; 03496 Clem 1B 15; 03505 Eva 1B 28; 03506 Gabe 1C NULL; 03510 Finn 1B 7; 03513 Dio 1C 13; 03517 Ben 1A 9.
mc.e: Clem, Eva and Finn are in 1B.

mc.q:
What is the output?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' ORDER BY CNO
Table STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) holds: 03493 Ada 1A 1; 03496 Clem 1B 15; 03505 Eva 1B 28; 03506 Gabe 1C NULL; 03510 Finn 1B 7; 03513 Dio 1C 13; 03517 Ben 1A 9.
mc.e: Sorted by CNO ascending: 7, 15, 28.

mc.q:
What is the output?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '1B' ORDER BY CNO DESC
Table STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) holds: 03493 Ada 1A 1; 03496 Clem 1B 15; 03505 Eva 1B 28; 03506 Gabe 1C NULL; 03510 Finn 1B 7; 03513 Dio 1C 13; 03517 Ben 1A 9.
mc.e: Descending CNO: 28, 15, 7.

mc.q:
What is the output?
SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT ORDER BY CLASS
Table STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) holds: 03493 Ada 1A 1; 03496 Clem 1B 15; 03505 Eva 1B 28; 03506 Gabe 1C NULL; 03510 Finn 1B 7; 03513 Dio 1C 13; 03517 Ben 1A 9.
mc.e: DISTINCT removes duplicated results.

mc.q:
What is the output?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT ORDER BY CLASS, CNO (first three rows)
Table STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO) holds: 03493 Ada 1A 1; 03496 Clem 1B 15; 03505 Eva 1B 28; 03506 Gabe 1C NULL; 03510 Finn 1B 7; 03513 Dio 1C 13; 03517 Ben 1A 9.
mc.e: Class 1A first (Ada 1, Ben 9), then 1B sorted by CNO: Finn 7 comes first.

mc.q: Which statement about SELECT is correct?
o: SELECT removes non-selected fields from the table
The SQL result is a new copy; the actual table is not changed
mc.e: Using SELECT FROM never changes the data in the actual table.

mc.q: The default sorting order of ORDER BY is
mc.e: ASC is the default.

mc.q: Which statement shows all fields of finished events in EVENT (FINISHED is Boolean)?
