  • It is used to show frequently retrieved data;（显示常用数据）
  • When used properly, it may simplify SQL statements;（简化 SQL）
  • It refers to data from other tables or views, thus does not need manual updates;（不需手动更新）
  • Similar to tables, its structure can be modified;（结构可修改）
  • If the referred tables or views are deleted, the view no longer works.（被引用的表/view 删除后失效）
补充：view 可只显示部分栏位，隐藏敏感资料；与把数据复制到新表相比不占储存空间，且永远与原表一致。

ex.q: A manager copies the result of a join into a new table SUMMARY every day instead of creating a view. Give two disadvantages.
ex.a: (1) SUMMARY must be updated manually; between updates it is out of date, causing data inconsistency. (2) It takes extra storage space for duplicated data. A view always shows current data and stores none.
ex.az: 需要手动更新、可能不一致；占用额外储存空间。

cards.en:
Without an index, to search by student name the DBMS must go through the table row by row. In the worst case, finding 'Guy' in an 11-record table needs 11 checks (the whole table).
If a field (e.g. NAME) is expected to be searched frequently, we can index it to speed up the data retrieval process.
Indexing NAME creates an index table containing the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only (here NAME with SID). The data in the index table is sorted in alphabetic order (or ascending order for a number field).
NAMESID
Ada03493
Ben03517
……
Jean03410
cards.zh:
没有索引时，用名字搜寻要逐行 (row by row) 查找；最坏情况在 11 条记录中找 Guy 要查 11 次（整个表）。
若某栏位（如 NAME）经常被搜寻，可为它建立 index 索引，加快数据检索。
Indexing NAME creates an index table containing the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only. 索引表中的数据已排序（字母序，数字则升序）。

ex.q: A library table BOOK has 50 000 records and users search by TITLE all day. Explain why indexing TITLE helps.
ex.a: Without an index, the DBMS checks records row by row (up to 50 000 checks). Indexing TITLE builds a sorted index table of titles with pointers to records, so the DBMS can use binary search, needing at most about 16 checks (2^16 = 65 536 ≥ 50 000).
ex.az: 没有索引要逐行查最多 50 000 次；有索引可二分搜寻，最多约 16 次。

cards.en:
Because the index table is sorted, the DBMS can perform binary search. Searching for Guy among 11 sorted names (Ada, Ben, Clem, Dio, Eva, Finn, Gabe, Guy, Hans, Ivy, Jean):
  1. Check the middle (6th) record, Finn: F is before G → eliminate records 1–6.
  2. Middle of the rest (9th), Hans: H is after G → eliminate records 9–11.
  3. Middle of the rest (7th), Gabe: Ga is before Gu → eliminate record 7.
  4. Check the 8th, Guy: found.
Worst case: 4 checks instead of 11.
Tip: even a table with 1024 records takes at most 10 searches if indexed, because 1024 = 210. Each check halves the remaining records.
cards.zh:
索引表已排序，所以可以做 binary search 二分搜寻。在 11 个已排序名字中找 Guy：查第 6 个 Finn（F 在 G 前，删前半）→ 第 9 个 Hans（H 在 G 后，删后半）→ 第 7 个 Gabe（Ga 在 Gu 前）→ 第 8 个 Guy 找到。最坏 4 次而不是 11 次。
Tip：1024 条记录最多只需 10 次，因为 1024 = 210；每次比较都把剩余记录减半。

ex.q: An indexed field has 2000 records. What is the maximum number of checks with binary search? Without the index?
ex.a: 210 = 1024 < 2000 ≤ 2048 = 211, so at most 11 checks with the index. Without it, up to 2000 checks (row by row).
ex.az: 有索引最多 11 次；没有索引最多 2000 次。

cards.en:
The index table needs to be updated when:
  • the data in the indexed field changes (e.g. Guy's name is changed to Gal); or
  • a new record is added (e.g. a new student Hope is added).
If it were not updated, searches for Gal and Hope would fail, since those names are not in the index table.
Though the DBMS updates index tables automatically, it still takes time to update and storage space to store the index table. (Deleting records also requires index changes.)

Therefore it is wise to index a field only if that field is expected to be searched frequently. Indexing every field slows down INSERT/UPDATE and wastes space.
cards.zh:
以下情况要更新索引表：
  • 被索引栏位的数据改变（如 Guy 改名 Gal）；
  • 新增记录（如新增学生 Hope）。
不更新的话，搜寻 Gal、Hope 会失败。DBMS 虽然会自动更新索引，但仍然要花时间更新，也要储存空间。

所以只应为经常被搜寻的栏位建立索引。为每个栏位都建索引会令 INSERT/UPDATE 变慢、浪费空间。

ex.q: A table LOG receives 10 000 new records per minute but is searched only once a month. Should the field USERID be indexed? Explain.
ex.a: Probably not. Every new record forces the DBMS to update the index table, costing time on 10 000 inserts per minute, and the index takes storage space. Since the field is searched rarely, the speed gain does not justify the cost.
ex.az: 不应该：插入极频繁，每次都要更新索引，耗时又占空间，而搜寻很少。

cards.en:
To index a field of a table:
CREATE INDEX SNAME ON STUDENT (NAME)
SNAME = index name, STUDENT = table name, NAME = field to be indexed. Normally, the index name is used only when we have to drop the index.

To delete an index (MySQL, as in the book):
ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP INDEX SNAME
The Chapter Summary also shows the shorter DROP INDEX ENAMEIDX (MySQL: DROP INDEX ENAMEIDX ON EMPLOYEE; SQLite: DROP INDEX ENAMEIDX).
If we forget the index name, we can find it with SHOW CREATE TABLE STUDENT (MySQL).

Creating or dropping an index does not change the data or the query results; it only changes how fast searching is.
cards.zh:
为栏位建立索引：CREATE INDEX SNAME ON STUDENT (NAME)：SNAME 是索引名，STUDENT 是表名，NAME 是被索引的栏位。索引名通常只在删除索引时用到。
删除（MySQL，课本写法）：ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP INDEX SNAME；Chapter Summary 亦写 DROP INDEX ENAMEIDX（SQLite 写 DROP INDEX 名称）。
忘记索引名可用 SHOW CREATE TABLE 查看。
建立或删除索引不会改变数据或查询结果，只影响搜寻速度。

ex.q: Write a statement to create an index named ENAMEIDX on the field ENAME of table EMPLOYEE, and one to remove it in MySQL.
ex.a:
CREATE INDEX ENAMEIDX ON EMPLOYEE (ENAME)
ALTER TABLE EMPLOYEE DROP INDEX ENAMEIDX
ex.az: CREATE INDEX 索引名 ON 表 (栏位)；ALTER TABLE 表 DROP INDEX 索引名。

cards.en:
Memorise (Chapter Summary):
  • It allows the DBMS to perform binary search on the indexed field to speed up the data retrieval process;
  • The DBMS will update it if changes are made to the data in the indexed field or a new record is added;
  • It takes time for the DBMS to update;
  • It takes storage space to store; and
  • Only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
Compare with a view: a view is a virtual table that simplifies statements and stores no data; an index is a sorted structure that speeds up searching and does take storage.
cards.zh:
要背：
  • It allows the DBMS to perform binary search on the indexed field to speed up the data retrieval process;
  • The DBMS will update it if changes are made to the data in the indexed field or a new record is added;
  • It takes time for the DBMS to update;
  • It takes storage space to store;
  • Only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
与 view 比较：view 是虚拟表，简化语句，不储存数据；index 是已排序的结构，加快搜寻，要占储存空间。

ex.q: State one advantage and two disadvantages of indexing the field PHONE in a CUSTOMER table.
ex.a: Advantage: searches by PHONE are faster because the DBMS can use binary search on the sorted index. Disadvantages: the index takes storage space; it takes time to update whenever a phone number changes or a customer is added.
ex.az: 优点：二分搜寻较快；缺点：占储存空间、更新要时间。

cards.en:
PATIENT(ID, PNAME, SEX, WEIGHT, HEIGHT, RID), ROOM(ID, RNAME, CAPACITY).
  • (a) Not every room has patients → LEFT JOIN from ROOM:
    CREATE VIEW RPNUM AS
  SELECT r.ID, RNAME, CAPACITY, COUNT(p.ID) AS PNUM FROM ROOM r
  LEFT JOIN PATIENT p ON r.ID = RID GROUP BY r.ID
    Select and group by r.ID (not RID, which is NULL for empty rooms); use COUNT(p.ID) (COUNT(*) would treat an empty room as 1 patient); alias PNUM.
  • (b) SELECT RNAME FROM RPNUM WHERE PNUM < CAPACITY
  • (c) SELECT AVG(PNUM) FROM RPNUM WHERE RNAME <> 'B01'
  • (d) Some patients have no room → PATIENT LEFT JOIN ROOM:
    CREATE VIEW PBMI AS
  SELECT p.ID, PNAME, SEX, WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT AS BMI, RNAME
  FROM PATIENT p LEFT JOIN ROOM r ON RID = r.ID
  • (e) SELECT SEX, MIN(BMI) FROM PBMI GROUP BY SEX
  • (f) SELECT RNAME, MAX(BMI) FROM PBMI GROUP BY RNAME ORDER BY RNAME
cards.zh:
• (a) 不是每间房都有病人 → ROOM LEFT JOIN PATIENT。要选取和分组 r.ID（RID 对空房是 NULL）；用 COUNT(p.ID)（COUNT(*) 会把空房当作 1 人）；别名 PNUM。
  • (b) PNUM < CAPACITY。(c) AVG(PNUM)，WHERE 排除 B01。
  • (d) 有病人未分配房间 → PATIENT LEFT JOIN ROOM，BMI = WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT。
  • (e) 按性别 MIN(BMI)。(f) 按房间 MAX(BMI)，ORDER BY RNAME。

ex.q: A patient weighs 72 kg and is 1.8 m tall. What BMI does view PBMI show? Why is WEIGHT/HEIGHT/HEIGHT correct?
ex.a: 72 / 1.8 / 1.8 = 40 / 1.8 = 22.2. Dividing by HEIGHT twice equals dividing by HEIGHT², matching BMI = mass ÷ height².
ex.az: 72/1.8/1.8 ≈ 22.2；除两次 HEIGHT 即除以 HEIGHT 的平方。

cards.t: Checkpoint 3.5 pattern: views of views for payments
cards.tz: Checkpoint 3.5：以 view 建立 view 计算欠款
cards.en:
Food delivery: CUSTOMER(CID, CNAME, SEX, DEPOSIT), MEAL(MID, MNAME, OPRICE, DISCOUNT), FORDER(CID, MID, NUM, ETA, PAID).
  • (b) sales per meal before 2025-01-25 using FORDER2: SELECT MNAME, SUM(TPRICE) FROM FORDER2 WHERE ETA < '2025-01-25' GROUP BY MID
  • (c) FORDER2 redefined to unpaid orders only (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, PAID = FALSE).
  • (d) amount due per customer, built on FORDER2, keeping customers with no unpaid orders:
    CREATE VIEW CPAYMENT AS
  SELECT CNAME, SEX, DEPOSIT, SUM(TPRICE) AS DUE
  FROM CUSTOMER c LEFT JOIN FORDER2 f ON c.CID = f.CID
  GROUP BY c.CID
  • (e) SELECT SEX, SUM(DUE) FROM CPAYMENT GROUP BY SEX
  • (f) customers whose deposit cannot cover their unpaid orders: SELECT CNAME FROM CPAYMENT WHERE DEPOSIT < DUE
Note: a customer with no unpaid order has DUE = NULL (SUM of nothing); DEPOSIT < NULL is not TRUE, so they are correctly not listed.
cards.zh:
送餐应用：(b) 用 FORDER2 按餐点求销售额；(c) 用 CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW 改成只显示未付款订单；(d) 以 FORDER2 建立 CPAYMENT，CUSTOMER LEFT JOIN FORDER2，SUM(TPRICE) AS DUE；(e) 按性别加总 DUE；(f) DEPOSIT < DUE 的顾客。
注意：没有未付款订单的顾客 DUE 为 NULL，DEPOSIT < NULL 不是 TRUE，所以正确地不会列出。

ex.q: Customer Amy has deposit $100 and two unpaid orders: 2 meals at $40 with discount 0.25, and 1 meal at $30 with no discount. What is DUE and is she listed in (f)?
ex.a: Order 1: 40 × (1 − 0.25) × 2 = 60. Order 2: 30 × 1 × 1 = 30. DUE = 90. Since 100 < 90 is false, she is not listed.

cards.en:
Joins: INNER (matching only), LEFT (all left + matching), RIGHT (all right + matching), FULL (both; not in MySQL), equi-join and NATURAL JOIN (other ways to do INNER JOIN), self join (one table, two aliases), CROSS JOIN (every row × every row).
Subquery operators: IN (values exist in other tables), EXISTS (subquery has a result), ANY (compare with any value; OR), ALL (compare with all values; AND).
Set operators: UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT.
Views: CREATE VIEW, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, DROP VIEW. Indices: CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX.

Glossary:
equi-join 等連接outer join 外連接
index 索引self join 自連接
inner join 內連接subquery 子查詢
natural join 自然連接view 檢視
cards.zh:
连接：INNER（只有配对）、LEFT（左表全部+配对）、RIGHT（右表全部+配对）、FULL（两边全部；MySQL 没有）、equi-join 与 NATURAL JOIN（INNER JOIN 的其他写法）、self join（同表两个别名）、CROSS JOIN（每行配每行）。
子查询：IN、EXISTS、ANY (OR)、ALL (AND)。集合：UNION、UNION ALL、INTERSECT、EXCEPT。View：CREATE / CREATE OR REPLACE / DROP VIEW。Index：CREATE / DROP INDEX。
词汇：equi-join 等連接、outer join 外連接、index 索引、self join 自連接、inner join 內連接、subquery 子查詢、natural join 自然連接、view 檢視。

ex.q: EMPLOYEE(EID, NAME, AGE). Explain: SELECT e1.NAME FROM EMPLOYEE e1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM EMPLOYEE e2 WHERE e1.AGE - e2.AGE >= 10)
ex.a: It lists the names of employees who are at least 10 years older than at least one other employee. For each e1, the correlated subquery looks for any e2 at least 10 years younger; EXISTS is TRUE if one is found.
ex.az: 列出比至少一名员工年长 10 岁或以上的员工。

mc.q: Which of the following is a problem of storing club name, room and teacher inside every student record?
o: A new club with no members cannot be stored if SID is the primary key
mc.e: With club data inside STUDENT, a club without students has no SID, but SID is the primary key and cannot be NULL, so the club cannot be stored (insertion problem).
mc.ez: 主键 SID 不能是 NULL，没有学生的新学会无法储存。

mc.q: Science Club (3 members) moves to Room 301. How many records must be updated if club data is stored in STUDENT, and how many if it is stored in a separate CLUB table?
mc.e: Each member's record holds the room in the single-table design (3 updates); with a CLUB table, only one record changes.
mc.ez: 单表要改 3 条，分表只改 1 条。

mc.q: What is the main advantage of a linking table SC(SID, CID) when students may join many clubs?
o: It removes the need for primary keys
A student may join many clubs without duplicating student data
It stores the number of clubs of each student
mc.e: Each (student, club) pair becomes one row in SC, so student data in STUDENT is never repeated.
mc.ez: 学生可参加多个学会而不重复储存学生资料。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: Only matched records: Ben (NULL) and English Club (no student) are excluded, leaving 6.
mc.ez: 只有配对的记录，共 6 行。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: All 7 students are kept; Ben gets NULL club fields; English Club is not included.

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM CLUB LEFT JOIN STUDENT ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID
mc.e: All clubs are kept: 6 matched rows plus English Club with NULL student = 7. This equals STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB.
mc.ez: 6 行配对加 English Club 一行，共 7 行。

mc.q: Which statement about FULL JOIN is correct?
o: It is the same as CROSS JOIN
It includes unmatched records from both tables and is not available in MySQL
It requires the two tables to have the same number of fields
mc.e: FULL JOIN keeps records from both the left and right tables; MySQL does not support the keyword (use LEFT JOIN … UNION … RIGHT JOIN).
mc.ez: FULL JOIN 两边都保留；MySQL 不支援此关键字。

mc.q: In MySQL, which can produce the same result as STUDENT FULL JOIN CLUB?
o: The result of STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB combined by UNION with the result of STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched students, RIGHT JOIN keeps unmatched clubs, and UNION merges them removing duplicate matched rows.
mc.ez: LEFT JOIN 结果 UNION RIGHT JOIN 结果。

mc.q: Which statement about the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN is correct?
o: ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID gives a different result from ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
The order of the two fields in ON has no effect; the order of the tables does
ON must always use fields with the same name
ON can only be used with INNER JOIN
mc.e: Which CID comes first in the ON clause has no effect; which table is written first (left table) does.
mc.ez: ON 中字段次序无影响，表的左右次序才有影响。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). Why does the following cause an error?
SELECT NAME, ROOM FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
o: ROOM is not a field of CLUB
NAME is ambiguous because both tables have a field called NAME
LEFT JOIN cannot select specific fields
CID must be written as STUDENT.CID in SELECT
mc.e: Both STUDENT and CLUB have NAME, so the table must be specified (STUDENT.NAME or CLUB.NAME).
mc.ez: 两表都有 NAME，须注明表名。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is returned?
SELECT c.NAME FROM STUDENT s INNER JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SCORE > 80 ORDER BY c.NAME
o: Art Club, Chess Club, Science Club
mc.e: Scores above 80: Clem 89 (Chess), Eva 83 (Science), Ben 86 (no club, dropped by INNER JOIN). Sorted: Chess Club, Science Club.
mc.ez: Ben 没有学会被 INNER JOIN 排除。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What does the following return for English Club?
SELECT c.NAME, COUNT(*) FROM CLUB c
  LEFT JOIN STUDENT s ON s.CID = c.CID GROUP BY c.CID
mc.e: The LEFT JOIN creates one row (English Club, NULL student). COUNT(*) counts rows, so it gives 1. COUNT(s.SID) would give 0.
mc.ez: COUNT(*) 计算行数，得 1；应用 COUNT(s.SID) 得 0。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is the average score shown for Chess Club?
SELECT c.NAME, AVG(SCORE) FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SID <> '03506' GROUP BY c.CID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
mc.e: Chess Club members: Clem 89 and Finn 35, average 62. (Gabe, removed by WHERE, is in Science Club.)

mc.q: A manager wants each team's average salary, excluding teams whose average salary is below 20000. Which clause should contain the condition?
mc.e: The condition is on a group summary, so it must be in HAVING after GROUP BY. WHERE would exclude individual employees before grouping.
mc.ez: 条件针对组的汇总值，要用 HAVING。

mc.q: TEAM stores MEMNUM, the number of employees in each team. Why is this field undesirable?
o: It cannot be a primary key
It must be updated whenever employees are added, or data becomes inconsistent; it can be computed with COUNT()
It takes the place of a foreign key
mc.e: MEMNUM is derivable data. Storing it risks data inconsistency; compute it with COUNT() instead.
mc.ez: 可计算的数据，储存会造成不一致。

mc.q: Every employee belongs to a department. To list each employee with their department name, excluding departments with no employees, which joins are suitable when EMPLOYEE is the left table?
mc.e: No employee lacks a department, so LEFT and INNER give the same result. RIGHT JOIN would add departments with no employees.
mc.ez: LEFT 和 INNER 结果相同；RIGHT 会多出空部门。

mc.q: Which statement is equivalent to STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID?
o: SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB WHERE STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
SELECT * FROM STUDENT CROSS JOIN CLUB
mc.e: Equi-join (tables in FROM with an equality condition in WHERE) is another way to perform INNER JOIN.
mc.ez: Equi-join 就是 INNER JOIN 的另一写法。

mc.q: Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB return (no WHERE clause)?
mc.e: Without a join condition, this is a CROSS JOIN: 7 × 4 = 28 rows.

mc.q: Why can't the textbook's STUDENT and CLUB tables be joined properly with NATURAL JOIN?
o: They share two field names, NAME and CID, and NAME is not a foreign key
NATURAL JOIN needs an ON clause
mc.e: NATURAL JOIN joins on all same-named fields; joining on NAME (student name = club name) is meaningless.
mc.ez: 两表有 NAME、CID 两个同名栏位，NAME 不是外键。

mc.q: What is required to perform a self join?
o: The table must have a composite primary key
The same table must be given two different aliases
The table must be joined with CROSS JOIN
The table must contain NULL values
mc.e: Two aliases let the DBMS treat the table as two different tables temporarily.
mc.ez: 同一表要给两个不同别名。

mc.q: STUDENT has CMSID, the SID of each student's class monitor. Which lists each student with their monitor's name?
o: SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.CMSID = s2.SID
SELECT NAME, NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CMSID = SID
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.SID = s2.SID
mc.e: s1 is the student, s2 the monitor; the link is s1.CMSID = s2.SID.
mc.ez: s1 是学生，s2 是班长，条件 s1.CMSID = s2.SID。

mc.q: When pairing students from STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2, which extra condition removes both self-pairs and duplicated pairs?
mc.e: s1.SID < s2.SID excludes equal SIDs (self-pairs) and keeps only one ordering of each pair. <> alone still leaves duplicates.
mc.ez: < 同时去除自配和重复；<> 仍有重复。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows are returned?
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2
WHERE ABS(s1.SCORE - s2.SCORE) < 16 AND s1.SID < s2.SID
mc.e: Pairs: Clem–Eva, Clem–Ben, Eva–Ben, Gabe–Finn = 4.

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT s.NAME, c.NAME FROM STUDENT s
  LEFT JOIN SC ON SC.SID = s.SID
  LEFT JOIN CLUB c ON c.CID = SC.CID
mc.e: 8 rows of SC give 8 (student, club) rows, plus Ben with NULL = 9.
mc.ez: SC 8 行加 Ben 一行，共 9 行。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). How many rows does the equi-join version return?
SELECT s.NAME, c.NAME FROM STUDENT s, SC, CLUB c
WHERE SC.SID = s.SID AND c.CID = SC.CID
mc.e: Equi-join is an INNER JOIN, so Ben (no club) is dropped: 8 rows.

mc.q: What does GROUP_CONCAT(c.NAME) do in a query grouped by student?
o: Counts the clubs of each student
Joins the club names of each group into one comma-separated string
mc.e: GROUP_CONCAT combines multiple string values in a group into one string, so a student's clubs appear in one row.
mc.ez: 把同组字串合并成一个以逗号分隔的字串。

mc.q: In Example 3.2, to list each employee with the name of their team leader using EMPLOYEE and TEAM, what is needed?
o: Two copies of EMPLOYEE with different aliases
mc.e: The leader is also an employee, so EMPLOYEE is used twice (e for members, l for leaders).
mc.ez: 组长也是员工，EMPLOYEE 要用两个别名。

mc.q: Table L has 3 rows and table R has 5 rows. How many rows does L CROSS JOIN R return?
mc.e: CROSS JOIN matches each row of L with each row of R: 3 × 5 = 15.

mc.q: BUYER Ada needs 4 apples and 7 oranges. Seller Finn sells apples at $14.0 and oranges at $11.4. What COST does PA*NA+PO*NO give?
What does SELECT NAME, MAX(SCORE) FROM STUDENT return according to the textbook?
o: The name of the top scorer and the top score
The highest score with a name that is not related to it
mc.e: NAME is not summarised data; it is just the first student's name, unrelated to MAX(SCORE).

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE > (SELECT AVG(SCORE) FROM STUDENT)
mc.e: Average = 407 / 7 ≈ 58.1. Above it: Clem 89, Eva 83, Dio 67, Ben 86.

mc.q: Why does WHERE SCORE = (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) cause an error when STUDENT2 has three rows?
o: A subquery after = must return a single value
= must be written as IN for numbers
mc.e: After a comparison operator, the subquery must return one value; use IN for a list.
mc.ez: 比较运算符后的子查询必须只返回一个值。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SID NOT IN (SELECT SID FROM SC)
mc.e: Every student except Ben appears in SC.
mc.ez: 只有 Ben 不在 SC。

mc.q: Which statement about the subquery after IN is correct?
o: It may select any number of fields
It should select only a single field, returning one list of values
It must return exactly one row
mc.e: IN checks a single list of values, so the subquery selects only one field.
mc.ez: IN 后子查询只选一个栏位。

mc.q: The join version SELECT s.NAME FROM STUDENT s, SC WHERE s.SID = SC.SID AND SCORE > 70 lists Clem three times. What fixes this?
mc.e: Clem has three rows in SC; SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicates. The IN version avoids them naturally.

mc.q: STUDENT has fields (SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE); STUDENT2 has (ID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, DOB). Which INSERT works?
o: INSERT INTO STUDENT (SELECT ID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, 0 FROM STUDENT2)
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SELECT ID, NAME FROM STUDENT2)
mc.e: The subquery must return the same number of fields as STUDENT (5); names need not match. SELECT * would put DOB into SCORE (wrong meaning).
mc.ez: 栏位数目要相同（5 个），名称不必相同。

mc.q: Which statement best describes EXISTS?
o: It checks whether a value appears in a list
It checks whether a subquery returns at least one row
It compares a value with all values in a list
mc.e: EXISTS checks for the existence of the result of a subquery.
mc.ez: 检查子查询是否有结果。

mc.q: In WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM STUDENT2 s2 WHERE s.SCORE = s2.SCORE), what can replace the 1?
o: Any field or value, since it is not used for comparison or display
mc.e: EXISTS only checks whether rows exist, so the selected value does not matter.
mc.ez: 选什么都可以，EXISTS 只看是否有行。

mc.q: STUDENT2 scores are 83, 47 and NULL. How many rows does SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE NOT IN (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) return (STUDENT scores 0, 89, 83, 47, 35, 67, 86)?
mc.e: Every comparison with NULL gives NULL, so x NOT IN (83, 47, NULL) is never TRUE.
mc.ez: 与 NULL 比较得 NULL，没有行符合。

mc.q:
With the same data (STUDENT2 scores 83, 47, NULL), how many rows does the NOT EXISTS version return?
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s WHERE NOT EXISTS
  (SELECT 1 FROM STUDENT2 s2 WHERE s.SCORE = s2.SCORE)
mc.e: Only Eva (83) and Gabe (47) have a match; the other 5 students are returned.
mc.ez: Eva、Gabe 有配对，其余 5 人返回。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to CLASS = ANY (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)?
o: CLASS NOT IN (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)
mc.e: = ANY joins equalities with OR, which is exactly IN.

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT valid SQL?
mc.e: ANY and ALL must be followed by a subquery, not a list of values.
mc.ez: ANY/ALL 后面必须是子查询。

mc.q: New students' classes are 3A, 3B, 3B. Which students satisfy CLASS <> ANY (SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT2)?
mc.e: <> ANY = <> '3A' OR <> '3B'; every class differs from at least one of them, so it is always TRUE.
mc.ez: 总与其中一个不同，全部成立。

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. SCORE > ANY (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2) is equivalent to:
mc.e: > ANY means higher than at least one, i.e. higher than the minimum (47).

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. Which STUDENT scores (0, 89, 83, 47, 35, 67, 86) satisfy SCORE < ALL (SELECT SCORE FROM STUDENT2)?
mc.e: < ALL means lower than every one, i.e. < 47. 47 itself is not lower.

mc.q: New students' scores are 83, 47 and 60. Which students satisfy BOTH SCORE > ANY (…) AND SCORE < ANY (…)?
mc.e: > ANY means > 47; < ANY means < 83. Only Dio (67) is in between.
mc.ez: 需要 47 < 分数 < 83，只有 Dio 67。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to NOT IN (subquery)?
mc.e: <> ALL joins inequalities with AND, exactly like NOT IN.

mc.q: When the subquery returns classes 3A and 3B, what does WHERE CLASS = ALL (subquery) return?
o: No rows, because a class cannot equal two different values
mc.e: = ALL = '3A' AND '3B', impossible to fulfil, like WHERE FALSE.

mc.q: In spoken English 'higher than any new student' means higher than all of them. In SQL, SCORE > ANY (…) means:
o: Higher than at least one of them
mc.e: SQL's ANY means SOME: higher than at least one.
mc.ez: ANY 即 SOME：至少高于一个。

mc.q:
Why is the following statement wrong?
SELECT NAME, h.NAME FROM BREED WHERE ID IN
  (SELECT BID FROM CAT, HOTEL h WHERE HID = h.ID AND h.NAME = 'Alpha')
o: IN cannot be used with a join in the subquery
The main query cannot retrieve data (h.NAME) from the subquery
Aliases are not allowed in subqueries
mc.e: h exists only inside the subquery; to output hotel names you must join in the main query.
mc.ez: 主查询不能取子查询的栏位。

mc.q: A query should list hotels that have no Ragdoll cats. Which is correct?
o: ID IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME <> 'Ragdoll')
ID NOT IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME = 'Ragdoll')
mc.e: Find hotels that do have Ragdolls, then take the others. The <> version lists hotels with any non-Ragdoll cat and misses hotels with no cats.
mc.ez: 先找有 Ragdoll 的酒店，再 NOT IN。

mc.q: What is the purpose of SELECT h.NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) FROM HOTEL h LEFT JOIN CAT c ON h.ID = c.HID GROUP BY h.ID?
o: Count the cats in each hotel
Count the number of different breeds in each hotel, including hotels with none
List hotels with more cats than capacity
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps every hotel; COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) counts different breeds; empty hotels get 0.
mc.ez: 计算每间酒店的品种数目。

mc.q: Which describes a correlated subquery?
o: A subquery that uses only constants
A subquery that refers to a field of the outer query and is evaluated for each outer row
mc.e: E.g. (SELECT COUNT(c.ID) FROM CAT c WHERE HID = h.ID) uses h from the outer query.
mc.ez: 引用外层查询的栏位，对外层每行执行一次。

mc.q:
Use STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE), SC(SID, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) from the textbook (Clem joins clubs 1, 2, 4; Ada 2; Eva 4; Gabe 4; Finn 1; Dio 4; Ben none; English Club (3) has no member). What is returned?
SELECT NAME FROM CLUB WHERE CID IN
  (SELECT CID FROM SC GROUP BY CID HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2)
o: Chess Club, Art Club, Science Club
mc.e: SC counts: club 1 → 2, club 2 → 2, club 4 → 4, club 3 → 0. Clubs with ≥ 2: Chess, Art, Science.
mc.ez: 学会 1、2 各 2 人，学会 4 有 4 人。

mc.q: STUDENT has 7 SIDs; STUDENT2 has 4 STUDENTIDs, one of which (03517) is also in STUDENT. How many rows does SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION ALL SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 return?
mc.e: UNION ALL keeps duplicates: 7 + 4 = 11.
mc.ez: UNION ALL 保留重复，11 行。

mc.q: Same tables. How many rows does SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID, NAME FROM STUDENT2 return, given 03517 is 'Ben' in STUDENT and 'Benz' in STUDENT2?
mc.e: Only completely identical rows are removed; (03517, Ben) ≠ (03517, Benz), so all 11 rows remain.
mc.ez: 只有完全相同的行才删除，11 行。

mc.q: Same tables. What does SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT INTERSECT SELECT STUDENTID, NAME FROM STUDENT2 return?
mc.e: No row is completely identical in both results.
mc.ez: 没有完全相同的行，空集。

mc.q: What is the requirement for combining two results with UNION?
mc.e: Only the number of fields must match; names may differ (the first result's names are used).

mc.q: Where must ORDER BY be placed in a statement using UNION?
o: At the end, applying to the whole combined result
ORDER BY cannot be used with UNION
mc.e: ORDER BY sorts the whole combined result and must be at the end.

mc.q: In SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 ORDER BY ?, which field name should be used?
o: Either; both work in all DBMS
mc.e: The combined result takes the field names of the first result, so ORDER BY SID.
mc.ez: 采用第一个结果的栏位名 SID。

mc.q: In SELECT SID FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 WHERE CLASS = '3B', which rows are filtered by the WHERE clause?
mc.e: Each SELECT has its own WHERE; this WHERE belongs to the second SELECT only.
mc.ez: WHERE 只属于第二个 SELECT。

mc.q: Which is a reason to use UNION ALL rather than UNION?
o: When the number of occurrences matters; it is also faster as it does not search for duplicates
To combine results with different numbers of fields
mc.e: UNION ALL keeps duplicates and skips duplicate checking.

mc.q: STUDENT SIDs: 03493, 03496, 03505, 03506, 03510, 03513, 03517. STUDENT2 STUDENTIDs: 03517, 03518, 03519, 03520. How many rows does SELECT STUDENTID FROM STUDENT2 EXCEPT SELECT SID FROM STUDENT return?
mc.e: Rows in STUDENT2 but not STUDENT: 03518, 03519, 03520.
mc.ez: STUDENT2 有而 STUDENT 没有的 3 个。

mc.q: Which statement correctly lists participants in team 'A' in at least one of FOOTBALL and RELAYRACE?
o: (SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE) WHERE TEAM = 'A'
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
mc.e: 'At least one' → UNION; each SELECT needs its own WHERE.
mc.ez: 至少一项 → UNION，各自 WHERE。

mc.q: 'List each participant aged at least 22 who does not participate in both events at the same time.' Which subquery is used with NOT IN?
o: SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL EXCEPT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
mc.e: Exclude those in both events: NOT IN (… INTERSECT …). UNION would exclude anyone in either event.
mc.ez: 排除同时参加两项的人：INTERSECT。

mc.q: What does SELECT COUNT(SID) FROM STUDENT UNION SELECT COUNT(STUDENTID) FROM STUDENT2 return (7 and 4 records)?
mc.e: Each SELECT produces its own count; UNION stacks them. To count unique IDs use COUNT(*) FROM (… UNION …) u.

mc.q: Which describes joining tables rather than combining results?
o: Stacks rows of results storing the same kind of data
Matches values in specific fields to link related data from tables storing different kinds of data
mc.e: Joining links related tables side by side; combining stacks similar results.
mc.ez: 连接按字段值配对不同种类的相关表。

mc.q: Which best describes a view?
o: A copy of a table stored separately
A virtual table defined by a SQL statement that does not store its own data
A sorted index of a field
mc.e: A view works as a virtual table referring to data from other tables.

mc.q: After UPDATE STUDENT SET SCORE2 = SCORE2 + 10 WHERE SID = '03369', what should be done to the view SCORESHEET built on STUDENT?
o: Nothing; the view shows the new data automatically
mc.e: A view refers to data from other tables; it needs (and should get) no manual update.

mc.q: Why must calculated fields like SCORE1*0.4+SCORE2*0.6 be given an alias in a view?
o: Otherwise the view cannot be created in any DBMS
So that the field can be selected easily later
To make it a primary key
mc.e: Without an alias, selecting the calculated column from the view is hard.

mc.q: COUNTCLUB is created by SELECT SID, COUNT(*) AS CLUBNUM FROM SC GROUP BY SID. A student who joins no club:
o: does not appear in the view
mc.e: The student has no row in SC, so the view (built only from SC) does not contain them.
mc.ez: 不在 SC，所以不在 view 中。

mc.q: COUNTCLUB is redefined as SELECT s.SID, COUNT(*) AS CLUBNUM FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN SC ON SC.SID = s.SID GROUP BY s.SID. What is CLUBNUM for a student with no club?
mc.e: The LEFT JOIN gives one row with NULL CID; COUNT(*) counts it as 1. COUNT(CID) is needed to get 0.

mc.q: Which statement modifies an existing view in MySQL?
mc.e: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW redefines an existing view.

mc.q: View SCORESHEET references view COUNTCLUB. What happens after DROP VIEW COUNTCLUB?
o: SCORESHEET keeps working with old data
The base table SC is deleted
mc.e: If a referenced view is deleted, the view that references it no longer works.
mc.ez: 引用它的 view 失效。

mc.q: Which is NOT a property of views?
o: It speeds up searching by binary search
mc.e: Binary search on a sorted field is the property of an index, not a view.
mc.ez: 二分搜寻是 index 的特性。

mc.q: Why does MAX(COUNT(*)) fail in most DBMS, and what is a fix?
o: COUNT cannot be used with GROUP BY; use SUM
An aggregate cannot directly summarise another aggregate; treat the grouped result as a table with an alias, or use ORDER BY … LIMIT 1
MAX only works on text; use TOP
mc.e: Use SELECT MAX(TOTAL) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS TOTAL … GROUP BY SID) t, or ORDER BY TOTAL DESC LIMIT 1.
mc.ez: 聚合函数不能直接嵌套；用别名子表或 LIMIT。

mc.q: An index table for NAME contains:
o: All fields of the table, unsorted
The indexed field, sorted, with a pointer to the related records
A copy of all records sorted by every field
mc.e: An index table contains the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only, sorted.
mc.ez: 被索引栏位（已排序）及指向记录的指针。

mc.q: An indexed field has 1024 records. At most how many checks does binary search need?
mc.e: 1024 = 2^10, so at most 10 searches (textbook tip).

mc.q: Binary search for 'Guy' in the sorted list Ada, Ben, Clem, Dio, Eva, Finn, Gabe, Guy, Hans, Ivy, Jean: which record is checked first?
mc.e: The middle (6th) record, Finn, is checked first.
mc.ez: 先查中间第 6 个 Finn。

mc.q: When must the DBMS update an index table?
o: When data in the indexed field changes or a new record is added
Only when the table is dropped
mc.e: Changes to the indexed field and new records require index updates (done automatically by the DBMS).
mc.ez: 被索引栏位改变或新增记录时。

mc.q: Why should only frequently searched fields be indexed?
o: Indices take time to update and storage space to store
Only one index is allowed per database
mc.e: The cost (update time and storage) is only worth it for fields searched often.
mc.ez: 索引要时间更新和储存空间。

mc.q: Which creates an index named SNAME on the NAME field of STUDENT?
mc.e: CREATE INDEX index_name ON table_name (field).
mc.ez: CREATE INDEX 索引名 ON 表 (栏位)。

mc.q: In Example 3.5, view RPNUM must list every room with its number of patients. Why is r.ID selected and grouped instead of RID?
o: RID is NULL for rooms with no patients, so those rooms would lose their ID
GROUP BY cannot use foreign keys
mc.e: After ROOM LEFT JOIN PATIENT, RID (from PATIENT) is NULL for empty rooms.
mc.ez: 空房的 RID 为 NULL。

mc.q: Which statement correctly calculates BMI in view PBMI (WEIGHT in kg, HEIGHT in m)?
mc.e: BMI = mass ÷ height²; dividing by HEIGHT twice equals dividing by HEIGHT².
mc.ez: 除以身高两次即除以身高平方。

mc.q: Hans has SCORE1 = 82 and SCORE2 = 67. What FSCORE does SCORESHEET show (FSCORE = SCORE1*0.4 + SCORE2*0.6)?
Using the 3.4 textbook data, which students join the most clubs (4 each)?
mc.e: Hans and Clem each have 4 rows in SC.
mc.ez: Hans 和 Clem 各 4 个学会。

sq.q:
Tom keeps his assignments in one table.
FieldDescription
TITLEtitle of the assignment
DUE_DATEdue date
SUBJECTsubject (NOT NULL)
TEACHERteacher responsible for the subject
CLASS_TIMEclass time of the subject
CLASS_DAYclass day of the subject
DONEwhether completed
MARKmark; NULL if unmarked

parts.q: Write a SQL statement to list the title of each assignment with a mark higher than the average mark of all assignments.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT TITLE FROM ASSIGNMENT
WHERE MARK > (SELECT AVG(MARK) FROM ASSIGNMENT)
Subquery computing AVG(MARK) [1]
Correct comparison in WHERE of the main query [1]

parts.q: Mr Suen replaces Mr Lee as the English teacher. Tom runs UPDATE ASSIGNMENT SET TEACHER = 'Mr Suen' WHERE TITLE = 'Creative Writing Task 1'. What potential issue may occur?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Other English assignments still show Mr Lee, so the data becomes inconsistent (update anomaly). [1]

parts.q: Modify the statement to prevent the issue.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
UPDATE ASSIGNMENT SET TEACHER = 'Mr Suen'
WHERE SUBJECT = 'English'
UPDATE … SET TEACHER = 'Mr Suen' [1]
WHERE SUBJECT = 'English' (all English assignments) [1]

parts.q: Tom splits the table into ASSIGNMENT and SUBJECT. Suggest the fields of each table.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: ASSIGNMENT(TITLE, DUE_DATE, SUBJECT, DONE, MARK) [1]
SUBJECT(SUBJECT, TEACHER, CLASS_TIME, CLASS_DAY) [1]
SUBJECT in ASSIGNMENT is a foreign key referring to SUBJECT (primary key of SUBJECT) [1]

parts.q: Using the new design, list the title of each assignment for the subject taught by Miss Chan.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT TITLE FROM ASSIGNMENT a, SUBJECT s
WHERE a.SUBJECT = s.SUBJECT AND TEACHER = 'Miss Chan'
Join on SUBJECT [1]
Condition TEACHER = 'Miss Chan' [1]
(Accept: SUBJECT IN (SELECT SUBJECT FROM SUBJECT WHERE TEACHER = 'Miss Chan'))

sq.q: Mike stores product information in PRODUCT(ITEM_ID, ITEM_NAME, CATEGORY, PRICE, QUANTITY).

parts.q: List the name of each product which has a quantity greater than the average quantity of all products in its category.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT ITEM_NAME FROM PRODUCT p
WHERE QUANTITY > (SELECT AVG(QUANTITY) FROM PRODUCT p2
                  WHERE p2.CATEGORY = p.CATEGORY)
Correlated subquery with AVG(QUANTITY) [1]
Linked by same CATEGORY [1]

parts.q: Find the total potential revenue (PRICE × QUANTITY) of products with a price greater than the average price of all products in the 'Electronics' category.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT SUM(PRICE * QUANTITY) FROM PRODUCT
WHERE PRICE > (SELECT AVG(PRICE) FROM PRODUCT
               WHERE CATEGORY = 'Electronics')
SUM(PRICE * QUANTITY) [1]
Subquery for Electronics average price [1]

parts.q: List the names of related products for each product (related = same category).
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT p1.ITEM_NAME, p2.ITEM_NAME AS RELATED
FROM PRODUCT p1, PRODUCT p2
WHERE p1.CATEGORY = p2.CATEGORY AND p1.ITEM_ID <> p2.ITEM_ID
Self join with two aliases on CATEGORY [1]
Exclude the product itself [1]

parts.q: REVIEW(ITEM_ID, RATING) is added. State the purpose of: SELECT * FROM PRODUCT p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM REVIEW r WHERE r.ITEM_ID = p.ITEM_ID AND r.RATING = 5)
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Lists all details of products [1]
that have received at least one review with rating 5 [1]

sq.q: Mrs Chan stores data in STUDENT(STU_ID, NAME, CLASS) and GRADE(SUBJECT, STU_ID, SCORE).

parts.q: List the names of the top scorers and their scores in 'Maths'.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT NAME, SCORE FROM STUDENT s, GRADE g
WHERE s.STU_ID = g.STU_ID AND SUBJECT = 'Maths'
  AND SCORE = (SELECT MAX(SCORE) FROM GRADE WHERE SUBJECT = 'Maths')
Join STUDENT and GRADE for Maths [1]
Subquery MAX(SCORE) for Maths (handles ties) [1]

parts.q: Some students have no records in GRADE. Using LEFT JOIN, list their names.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN GRADE g
  ON s.STU_ID = g.STU_ID
WHERE g.STU_ID IS NULL
STUDENT LEFT JOIN GRADE on STU_ID [1]
WHERE g.STU_ID IS NULL [1]

parts.q: Rewrite (b) using EXISTS.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s WHERE NOT EXISTS
  (SELECT 1 FROM GRADE g WHERE g.STU_ID = s.STU_ID)
NOT EXISTS with correlated condition [1]

parts.q: List the name of each student with an average score higher than 80.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT s, GRADE g
WHERE s.STU_ID = g.STU_ID
GROUP BY s.STU_ID HAVING AVG(SCORE) > 80
GROUP BY student [1]
HAVING AVG(SCORE) > 80 [1]

sq.q: A taxi app uses USER(UID, UNAME, PHONE, EMAIL), TAXI(DID, DNAME, PHONE, TNUMBER) and ORDERS(OID, UID, DID, ORIGIN, DEST). DID in ORDERS is NULL until a driver accepts the order.

parts.q: Write down the primary key and foreign keys (if any) of each table.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: USER: PK UID; no FK [1]
TAXI: PK DID; no FK [1]
ORDERS: PK OID; FKs UID (→ USER) and DID (→ TAXI) [1]

parts.q: List the names of users whose orders have not been accepted by any driver yet.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT DISTINCT UNAME FROM USER u, ORDERS o
WHERE u.UID = o.UID AND o.DID IS NULL
Join USER and ORDERS [1]
DID IS NULL [1]

parts.q: List the names of users who have never called for a taxi.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT UNAME FROM USER WHERE UID NOT IN (SELECT UID FROM ORDERS)
[1]

parts.q: For each driver, list their ID, name and the number of orders accepted.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT t.DID, DNAME, COUNT(o.OID) FROM TAXI t
  LEFT JOIN ORDERS o ON t.DID = o.DID
GROUP BY t.DID
LEFT JOIN so drivers with 0 orders are kept [1]
COUNT(o.OID) with GROUP BY t.DID [1]

parts.q: List the order IDs, user names and driver names of all accepted orders.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT OID, UNAME, DNAME FROM ORDERS o, USER u, TAXI t
WHERE o.UID = u.UID AND o.DID = t.DID
Three tables in FROM [1]
o.UID = u.UID [1]
o.DID = t.DID (inner join drops unaccepted orders) [1]

sq.q: A school uses STUDENT(SID, SNAME, SEX, CLASS, CNO), ACTIVITY(AID, ANAME, ADATE) and REG(SID, AID).

parts.q: State the primary key and foreign keys (if any) of REG.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Primary key: composite key (SID, AID) [1]
Foreign keys: SID → STUDENT, AID → ACTIVITY [1]

parts.q: State the purpose of: SELECT AID, ANAME, COUNT(*) FROM REG r LEFT JOIN ACTIVITY a ON r.AID = a.AID GROUP BY AID
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Lists each registered activity's ID and name with the number of students who registered for it. [1]

parts.q: List the student ID and the number of activities registered by each student, counting only activities held between 2024-09-01 and 2025-03-01.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT SID, COUNT(*) FROM REG r, ACTIVITY a
WHERE r.AID = a.AID
  AND ADATE BETWEEN '2024-09-01' AND '2025-03-01'
GROUP BY SID
Join with date condition [1]
GROUP BY SID with COUNT [1]

parts.q: List the name of each student from class '4A' who registered fewer than 3 activities.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: 
SELECT SNAME FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN REG r ON s.SID = r.SID
WHERE CLASS = '4A'
GROUP BY s.SID HAVING COUNT(r.AID) < 3
LEFT JOIN keeps students with 0 activities [1]
HAVING COUNT(r.AID) < 3 [1]

sq.q: A gym uses MEMBER(MID, MNAME, LEVEL) and CLASSREG(MID, CNAME, FEE). Some members have not registered for any class.

parts.q: Explain the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN when MEMBER is the left table and CLASSREG is the right table.
parts.ms:
INNER JOIN includes only members with matching records in CLASSREG [1]
LEFT JOIN includes all members, with NULL class fields for members without registration [1]

parts.q: Write a SQL statement to list every member's name with the total fee they pay (show members with no class).
parts.ms:
SELECT MNAME, SUM(FEE) FROM MEMBER m
  LEFT JOIN CLASSREG c ON m.MID = c.MID
GROUP BY m.MID
LEFT JOIN from MEMBER [1]
SUM(FEE) grouped by m.MID [1]

parts.q: A staff member writes SELECT MNAME, COUNT(*) FROM MEMBER m LEFT JOIN CLASSREG c ON m.MID = c.MID GROUP BY m.MID to count classes per member. Identify the error and correct it.
parts.ms:
Members with no class are counted as 1 because the joined row still exists [1]
Use COUNT(c.CNAME) (or COUNT(c.MID)) so NULL is not counted [1]

parts.q: Rewrite to list members with no class using a subquery instead of a join.
parts.ms:
SELECT MNAME FROM MEMBER WHERE MID NOT IN (SELECT MID FROM CLASSREG)
[1]

sq.q: STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, SCORE) and NEWSTU(SID, NAME, CLASS, SCORE). NEWSTU scores are 70, 52 and 91.

parts.q: Rewrite without ANY or ALL: (i) SCORE > ANY (SELECT SCORE FROM NEWSTU) (ii) SCORE < ALL (SELECT SCORE FROM NEWSTU)
parts.ms:
(i) SCORE > (SELECT MIN(SCORE) FROM NEWSTU), i.e. > 52 [1]
(ii) SCORE < (SELECT MIN(SCORE) FROM NEWSTU), i.e. < 52 [1]

parts.q: A teacher says CLASS <> ANY (SELECT CLASS FROM NEWSTU) finds students in classes that no new student is in. Comment, and give a correct criterion.
parts.ms:
Incorrect: <> ANY joins conditions with OR, so it is TRUE whenever NEWSTU has two different classes (meaningless) [1]
Use CLASS NOT IN (SELECT CLASS FROM NEWSTU) or CLASS <> ALL (…) [1]

parts.q: One NEWSTU score is changed to NULL. Explain why SELECT NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SCORE NOT IN (SELECT SCORE FROM NEWSTU) now returns no rows, and give a correct alternative.
parts.ms:
x NOT IN (a, b, NULL) = x<>a AND x<>b AND x<>NULL [1]
x<>NULL is NULL, so the whole condition is never TRUE [1]
Use NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM NEWSTU n WHERE n.SCORE = STUDENT.SCORE), or add WHERE SCORE IS NOT NULL in the subquery [1]

sq.q: Two branches store members in BRANCH1(MID, NAME, PHONE) and BRANCH2(MID, NAME, PHONE). Some members belong to both branches.

parts.q: Write a statement to list the MIDs of members in either branch, without duplicates, sorted by MID.
parts.ms:
SELECT MID FROM BRANCH1
UNION
SELECT MID FROM BRANCH2
ORDER BY MID
UNION [1]
Single ORDER BY at the end [1]

parts.q: Write a statement to list the MIDs of members of BRANCH1 only.
parts.ms:
SELECT MID FROM BRANCH1 EXCEPT SELECT MID FROM BRANCH2
[1]

parts.q: Write a statement to count the members who belong to both branches.
parts.ms:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM
  (SELECT MID FROM BRANCH1 INTERSECT SELECT MID FROM BRANCH2) b
INTERSECT [1]
Result treated as a table with alias and counted [1]

parts.q: Give one situation where UNION ALL should be used instead of UNION, and one advantage of UNION ALL.
parts.ms:
When the number of occurrences matters, e.g. counting how many branch memberships there are [1]
Faster, as it does not compare rows to remove duplicates [1]

parts.q: Explain the difference between combining results with UNION and joining BRANCH1 with BRANCH2.
parts.ms:
UNION stacks rows of results storing the same kind of data with equal numbers of fields [1]
Joining matches values (e.g. MID) to link data side by side into wider rows [1]

sq.q: A clinic uses DOCTOR(DID, DNAME, SPECIALTY) and APPT(AID, DID, PNAME, ADATE, FEE). The manager often needs each doctor's number of appointments and total fee.

parts.q: Create a view DSTAT showing each doctor's DID, DNAME, number of appointments NUM and total fee TOTAL, including doctors with no appointment.
parts.ms:
CREATE VIEW DSTAT AS
  SELECT d.DID, DNAME, COUNT(AID) AS NUM, SUM(FEE) AS TOTAL
  FROM DOCTOR d LEFT JOIN APPT a ON d.DID = a.DID
  GROUP BY d.DID
CREATE VIEW … AS SELECT [1]
LEFT JOIN from DOCTOR with GROUP BY d.DID [1]
COUNT(AID) (not COUNT(*)) with aliases NUM and TOTAL [1]

parts.q: Using DSTAT, list the names of doctors with the most appointments.
parts.ms:
SELECT DNAME FROM DSTAT WHERE NUM = (SELECT MAX(NUM) FROM DSTAT)
Subquery MAX(NUM) [1]
Correct comparison [1]

parts.q: A new appointment is inserted into APPT. Does DSTAT need to be updated? Explain.
parts.ms:
No [1]
A view does not store data; it refers to APPT and DOCTOR, so the new appointment is reflected automatically [1]

parts.q: State two properties of views other than the one in (c).
parts.ms: Any two: shows frequently retrieved data; may simplify SQL statements; its structure can be modified (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW); stops working if the referred tables/views are deleted [1 each]

sq.q: A library table BOOK(BID, TITLE, AUTHOR, YEAR) has 60 000 records. Users search by TITLE frequently; YEAR is rarely searched.

parts.q: Write a SQL statement to create an index named TIDX on TITLE.
parts.ms:
CREATE INDEX TIDX ON BOOK (TITLE)
[1]

parts.q: Explain how the index speeds up searching for a title. State the maximum number of checks needed.
parts.ms:
The index table stores TITLE sorted with pointers to the records [1]
The DBMS can perform binary search, halving the range each check [1]
2^16 = 65 536 ≥ 60 000, so at most 16 checks (vs up to 60 000 row by row) [1]

parts.q: Should YEAR also be indexed? Explain with two disadvantages of indices.
parts.ms:
No, because YEAR is rarely searched [1]
An index takes storage space [1]
The DBMS must spend time updating it when the field changes or records are added [1]

parts.q: Write a statement to remove the index in MySQL.
parts.ms:
ALTER TABLE BOOK DROP INDEX TIDX
(accept DROP INDEX TIDX ON BOOK) [1]

cards.en:
A relational database organises data in a tabular form. Each table consists of columns and rows, and each row is a record. Every database we managed with SQL in Chapters 1 to 3 was a relational database.

Tables are linked to each other through shared values (keys), so data about different things (students, clubs, classes) is kept in separate tables and joined when needed. Other database types exist, but they are not the focus of the DSE syllabus and are not commonly used today.

The theory of relational databases gives names to every part of the design: entity type, entity, attribute, relationship and domain. This chapter maps each of these to what you actually see in a DBMS such as MySQL.

Key sentence: A relational database organises data in tables of rows (records) and columns (fields).
cards.zh:
Relational database（关系式数据库）把数据用表格形式（tabular form）组织：每个 table 由 columns（列）和 rows（行）组成，每一行是一条 record。第 1 到 3 章用 SQL 管理的数据库全部都是关系式数据库。

不同的表通过共同的值（key）连起来，所以学生、学会、班别等不同事物的数据放在不同的表，需要时再 JOIN。其他类型的数据库也有，但不是 DSE 重点，现在也不常用。

关系式数据库理论给设计中的每部分起了名字：entity type、entity、attribute、relationship、domain。本章会把它们一一对应到 DBMS（如 MySQL）里看到的东西。

要背：A relational database organises data in tables of rows (records) and columns (fields).

ex.q: A table STUDENT has 5 columns and 120 rows. How many records and how many fields does it hold?
ex.a:
Each row is a record and each column is a field.
Records = 120; fields = 5.
ex.az: 每行一条记录，每列一个字段：120 条 record，5 个 field。

cards.en:
The hierarchical database was the first type of database to be developed. Data is stored as a tree: every node has one parent (e.g. School → Classroom / Staffroom / Special Room → Room 101, Computer Room ...). Each node stores its own ID and its parent ID.

It is now obsolete and almost replaced by the relational database. The same data in relational form uses two tables, e.g. ROOM(RID, RNAME, RTID) and ROOMTYPE(RTID, RTNAME): the RTID in ROOM points to a row in ROOMTYPE.

A relational database may look more complicated than a hierarchical one (more tables, codes instead of a picture of a tree), but it is much easier to manage in a DBMS: you can query, join, sort and update any table with SQL without walking down a tree.
cards.zh:
Hierarchical database（层次式数据库）是最早出现的数据库类型。数据像一棵树：每个节点只有一个 parent（例如 School → Classroom / Staffroom / Special Room → Room 101、Computer Room……），每个节点存自己的 ID 和 parent ID。

现在它已经过时（obsolete），几乎被 relational database 取代。同样的数据用关系式表示要两张表，例如 ROOM(RID, RNAME, RTID) 和 ROOMTYPE(RTID, RTNAME)，ROOM 里的 RTID 指向 ROOMTYPE 的一行。

关系式数据库看起来更复杂（表更多、用代码代替树图），但在 DBMS 里容易管理得多：任何表都可以直接用 SQL 查询、JOIN、排序、更新，不用沿着树一层层找。

ex.q: In the relational version, ROOM has (22, 'Art Room', 2) and ROOMTYPE has (2, 'Special Room'). Write an SQL query that lists every room name with its room-type name.
ex.a:
Join on the shared code RTID:
SELECT R.RNAME, T.RTNAME
FROM ROOM R, ROOMTYPE T
WHERE R.RTID = T.RTID
Art Room is shown with Special Room.
ex.az: 用共同的 RTID 做 JOIN，即可得到每间房和它的类型，例如 Art Room → Special Room。

cards.t: Relational database elements vs DBMS elements
cards.tz: 关系式数据库元素与 DBMS 元素对照
cards.en:
Table 4.1 must be memorised. Each element of a relational database is stored as (or represented by) an element of the DBMS:
Relational databaseDBMS
Entity typeTable
EntityRecord (row, also called a tuple)
AttributeField (column)
RelationshipForeign key
DomainData type and constraint
So when a question asks for the entity type of a table, answer with the kind of thing each row describes ("students", "school events"), not with a field name. When it asks how a relationship is implemented, answer "by a foreign key". When it asks how a domain is enforced, answer "by the data type and constraints (e.g. CHECK)".
cards.zh:
表 4.1 必须背熟。关系式数据库的每个元素在 DBMS 中都有对应：
Relational databaseDBMS
Entity typeTable
EntityRecord（行，也叫 tuple）
AttributeField（列）
RelationshipForeign key
DomainData type and constraint
所以题目问某表的 entity type，要答每一行描述的是什么东西（"students"、"school events"），不是答字段名；问 relationship 怎样实现，答"by a foreign key"；问 domain 怎样保证，答"by the data type and constraints（例如 CHECK）"。

ex.q: In table CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH), identify the entity type, one entity, one attribute, and what would represent the relationship 'students join clubs'.
ex.a:
Entity type: clubs (the table CLUB).
Entity: one record, e.g. the Chess Club row.
Attribute: e.g. ROOM (a field).
Relationship: a foreign key CID in STUDENT referencing CLUB(CID).
ex.az: Entity type = clubs；entity = 某一条记录（如 Chess Club）；attribute = 字段如 ROOM；关系用 STUDENT 里的 foreign key CID 表示。

cards.en:
An entity is either:
  • a physical object, such as a building, a product, a student or an employee; or
  • a conceptual object, such as an organisation, a transaction, a course or a job.
An entity must be unique: we should always be able to differentiate between two entities (this is why tables need keys later in 4.2).

In a DBMS an entity is represented by a row, i.e. a record in a table. A record is sometimes called a tuple. For example, in table STUDENT the record (03493, Ada, F, 1A, 1) is one entity.

Tip: an entity is like a proper noun or a specific noun phrase, e.g. "a student named Ada" or "a chocolate bar sold in a store". It is never a verb or an adjective.
cards.zh:
Entity（实体）可以是：
  • physical object（实物）：建筑物、产品、学生、雇员；或
  • conceptual object（概念上的对象）：机构、交易（transaction）、课程、职位。
Entity must be unique：必须总能区分两个 entity（所以 4.2 要讲 key）。

在 DBMS 中，一个 entity 用表里的一行，即一条 record 表示，record 有时叫 tuple。例如 STUDENT 里 (03493, Ada, F, 1A, 1) 就是一个 entity。

提示：entity 像专有名词或具体名词短语，如 "a student named Ada"；不会是动词或形容词。

ex.q: Classify each as a physical or conceptual entity: (i) a laptop with serial no. X91, (ii) a bank transfer made at 10:05, (iii) the course 'ICT S5'.
ex.a:
(i) Physical object.
(ii) Conceptual object (a transaction).
(iii) Conceptual object (a course).
ex.az: (i) 实物；(ii) 概念对象（交易）；(iii) 概念对象（课程）。

cards.en:
An entity type is a collection of entities sharing similar attributes. A specific student is an entity; a collection of students from the same school is an entity type.

In a DBMS an entity type is represented by a table, e.g. the table STUDENT. Its rows are the entities.

Tip: an entity type always represents a common noun or noun phrase ("products", "students", "school events"), never a verb or an adjective.

Exam habit: when asked "State the entity types of A and B", answer with plural common nouns describing what each row of the table is, e.g. "School events and students respectively." Do not answer with the table name alone or with a field.
cards.zh:
Entity type（实体类型）是一组有相似 attributes 的 entities 的集合。某一个学生是 entity；同一所学校的所有学生合起来是 entity type。

在 DBMS 中 entity type 用一张 table 表示，如 STUDENT 表，表里每一行就是一个 entity。

提示：entity type 一定是普通名词或名词短语（"products"、"students"、"school events"），不是动词或形容词。

答题习惯：问 "State the entity types of A and B"，用复数普通名词说出每一行代表什么，例如 "School events and students respectively."，不要只写表名或字段名。

ex.q: Table A has fields PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE, SID. Table B has SID, SNAME, OPEN, CLOSE. State the entity types of A and B.
ex.a:
Each row of A describes a product, each row of B describes a shop.
Products and shops respectively.
ex.az: A 每行是一件产品，B 每行是一间店：Products and shops respectively。

cards.t: Misconception: attribute mistaken for an entity type
cards.tz: 易错：把属性当成实体类型
cards.en:
A common MC trap lists pairs like "Entity type: Weight, Attribute: Computer". This is wrong: weight is a property, so it is an attribute of computers, and computers are the entity type.

How to check: ask "is this a thing we keep many records of, each with its own properties?" If yes, it is an entity type. Ask "is this one property describing such a thing?" If yes, it is an attribute.

Examples of wrong pairs: Age with attributes Patient and Gender (Age is an attribute of patients); Duration as an entity type of a concert (duration is an attribute of concerts); Height as an entity type of students (height is an attribute of students).
cards.zh:
常见 MC 陷阱：给出 "Entity type: Weight, Attribute: Computer" 这类组合。这是错的：weight 是一种性质，所以是 computers 的 attribute，而 computers 才是 entity type。

判断方法："这是不是我们要存很多条记录、每条有自己性质的东西？"是 → entity type；"这是不是描述这种东西的一个性质？"是 → attribute。

错误例子：Age 当 entity type、Patient 和 Gender 当 attribute（Age 其实是 patients 的 attribute）；Duration 当 entity type（是 concert 的 attribute）；Height 当 entity type（是 students 的 attribute）。

ex.q: Activity 4.1 Q2: Which set is NOT correct? A. Book: Year of publication, ISBN  B. Product: Number in stock, Price  C. Age: Patient, Gender  D. Transaction: Date, Time
ex.a: C. Age is an attribute (of patients), not an entity type; patient should be the entity type with attributes age and gender.
ex.az: 答 C：Age 是 patients 的 attribute，不能当 entity type。

cards.en:
An attribute is the property of an entity. An entity can have multiple attributes. In table STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CNO), the name (NAME) and the sex (SEX) of a student are attributes of the entity type students; SID, CLASS and CNO are attributes too.

In a DBMS an attribute is usually represented by a column, i.e. a field of a table.

Each attribute has a domain (the set of allowed values, see Domain card). Attributes are described in a table structure (Field / Description), which is the usual format in DSE questions.

Remember: entity type → table, entity → record, attribute → field.
cards.zh:
Attribute（属性）是 entity 的性质（property）。一个 entity 可以有多个 attributes。STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CNO) 中，学生的名字 NAME、性别 SEX 都是 students 这个 entity type 的 attribute；SID、CLASS、CNO 也是。

在 DBMS 中 attribute 一般用表的一列，即一个 field 表示。

每个 attribute 都有自己的 domain（可取值的集合，见 Domain 卡）。DSE 题目常用 table structure（Field / Description）来描述 attributes。

记住：entity type → table，entity → record，attribute → field。

ex.q: Name two attributes of the entity type 'books' that would make sensible fields.
ex.a: e.g. ISBN, title, year of publication, price, number of pages (any two).
ex.az: 例如 ISBN、书名、出版年份、价格、页数，任选两个。

cards.en:
Some attributes can be derived (calculated) from other attributes. They are called derived attributes.
AttributeDerived attribute
Date of birthAge (year difference between today and DOB)
Scores of a studentAverage score
Price and costProfit = price − cost
Weight and heightBMI
Working hoursTotal working hours (SUM())
Derived attributes usually need not be stored: they can be calculated in a query when needed. Storing them causes extra updates and risk of inconsistency (e.g. AGE changes every year, BHOUR must change whenever OPEN or CLOSE changes). Typical answer: "Store the date of birth instead of age, because age changes but birthday does not, so the data need not be updated frequently; age can be calculated from the birthday."
cards.zh:
有些 attribute 可以由其他 attributes 算出来，叫 derived attribute（衍生属性）。
AttributeDerived attribute
出生日期Age（今天与出生日期相差的年数）
各科分数平均分
售价和成本Profit = price − cost
体重和身高BMI
工作时数总工时（SUM()）
衍生属性一般不必储存，需要时在查询里计算即可。存了反而要经常更新，还可能不一致（AGE 每年都变；OPEN/CLOSE 一改 BHOUR 也要改）。标准答法："Store the birthday instead of age: age changes but birthday does not, so data need not be updated frequently; age can be calculated from the birthday."

ex.q: SHOP(SID, SNAME, OPEN, CLOSE, BHOUR). Which field is a derived attribute? Show how it could be computed instead of stored (SQLite).
ex.a:
BHOUR is derived: it is the hour difference between OPEN and CLOSE.
SELECT SNAME,
  (strftime('%s', CLOSE) - strftime('%s', OPEN)) / 3600.0 AS BHOUR
FROM SHOP
(MySQL: TIMEDIFF(CLOSE, OPEN).)
ex.az: BHOUR 是衍生属性（CLOSE − OPEN）。可在查询中计算，不用存。

cards.en:
A relationship is the connection between entities. For example, with the entity types students and clubs, a student may join a club, so "join" is the relationship between these two entity types.

Tip: a relationship represents a verb or verb phrase, not a noun or adjective. In a DBMS it is represented by the connection made by foreign keys between tables.

Example: STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH). STUDENT references CLUB by CID: Ada has CID 2, so she joined Art Club. Ben has CID NULL, meaning he has not joined any club.

Exam answer format: "B participates in A", "B sells A / A is sold by B".
cards.zh:
Relationship（关系）是 entities 之间的联系。例如有 students 和 clubs 两个 entity type，学生可以参加学会，所以 "join" 就是两者之间的 relationship。

提示：relationship 是动词或动词短语，不是名词或形容词。在 DBMS 中用表与表之间的 foreign key 连接表示。

例：STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CID) 与 CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH)。STUDENT 通过 CID 引用 CLUB：Ada 的 CID 是 2，所以她参加了 Art Club；Ben 的 CID 是 NULL，表示没参加学会。

答题格式："B participates in A"、"B sells A / A is sold by B"。

ex.q: Using the tables above, which club did Eva (CID 4) join? Write the SQL that finds it.
ex.a:
CID 4 in CLUB is Science Club.
SELECT C.NAME FROM STUDENT S, CLUB C
WHERE S.CID = C.CID AND S.NAME = 'Eva'
ex.az: CID 4 对应 Science Club；用 JOIN 查。

cards.t: Active and passive voice in relationships
cards.en:
A relationship sentence reads "X verb Y", so the voice must match the direction:
ExampleXYRelationship
Managers manage departments.ManagerDepartmentManage
Departments are managed by managers.DepartmentManagerBe managed by
Parents have children.ParentChildHave
Artists perform songs.ArtistSongPerform
Theorems are proved by mathematicians.TheoremMathematicianBe proved by
Check each option by reading it aloud. "Product sells Shop" is wrong (products are sold by shops). "Patient is married to Doctor" is not the right relationship (patients are treated by doctors). "Lesson is taught by Teacher" is correct.
cards.zh:
Relationship 句子读作 "X 动词 Y"，语态要配合方向：
例子XY关系
Managers manage departments.ManagerDepartmentManage
Departments are managed by managers.DepartmentManagerBe managed by
Parents have children.ParentChildHave
Theorems are proved by mathematicians.TheoremMathematicianBe proved by
做题时把选项读出来检查。"Product sells Shop" 错（应是 products are sold by shops）；"Patient is married to Doctor" 不合理（应是 treated by）；"Lesson is taught by Teacher" 正确。

ex.q: Activity 4.2 Q2: Which is correct? A. Payment–Recipient: X is received by Y  B. Author–Book: X is written by Y  C. Duration–Concert: X is the time occupied by Y  D. Employee–Company: X employs Y
ex.a: A. A payment is received by a recipient. B should be 'X writes Y'; C: duration is an attribute of concerts, not an entity type; D should be 'X is employed by Y'.
ex.az: 答 A。B 应为 writes；C 的 duration 是 attribute；D 应为 is employed by。

cards.t: Misconception: specific entities used as entity types
cards.tz: 易错：把特定实体当成实体类型
cards.en:
We should NOT treat specific entities as entity types. An entity type should not be a particular subject like Physics or Chemistry, but subjects as a whole.

Example: "Students study Physics, Chemistry or Biology" gives entity types Student and Subject with relationship Study. Physics, Chemistry and Biology are entities (records) of SUBJECT, not three separate tables.

Design consequence: do not create tables PHYSICS, CHEMISTRY, BIOLOGY, or fields like TAKE_PHY, TAKE_CHEM. Create SUBJECT(SUBID, SUBNAME) and a linking table such as ENROL(SID, SUBID). Then adding a new subject is just inserting a row, not changing the structure.
cards.zh:
不要把特定 entity 当成 entity type。entity type 不应是某一科如 Physics 或 Chemistry，而应是整体的 subjects。

例："Students study Physics, Chemistry or Biology" 的 entity types 是 Student 和 Subject，relationship 是 Study。Physics、Chemistry、Biology 只是 SUBJECT 表里的记录。

设计上：不要建 PHYSICS、CHEMISTRY 三张表，也不要建 TAKE_PHY、TAKE_CHEM 等字段。应建 SUBJECT(SUBID, SUBNAME) 及连接表 ENROL(SID, SUBID)。以后加新科目只需 INSERT 一行，不用改表结构。

ex.q: A designer makes fields PHY, CHEM, BIO (Y/N) in STUDENT. Suggest a better design and give the SQL to count students taking Physics.
ex.a:
Use SUBJECT(SUBID, SUBNAME) and ENROL(SID, SUBID).
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ENROL E, SUBJECT S
WHERE E.SUBID = S.SUBID AND S.SUBNAME = 'Physics'
ex.az: 改用 SUBJECT 表和 ENROL 连接表，再用 JOIN + COUNT。

cards.t: Why split data into tables (Mary's single-table idea)
cards.tz: 为何要分表（Mary 的单表方案）
cards.en:
Think About (p.206): Mary says CLUB is unnecessary and puts CNAME, CROOM, CTEACH directly into STUDENT. Problems:
  • Update problem: when the name, room or teacher of a club changes, we must update the records of all students who join that club; missing one makes the data inconsistent. If STUDENT stores only the club's identity code, STUDENT need not be updated at all.
  • Deletion problem: if the records of all students who join a club are deleted, the data of this club is permanently lost.
Example: in STUDENTCLUB, changing Science Club's teacher from Mr Wong to Mr Suen needs three records updated; if Ada (the only Art Club member) leaves, Art Club's data is lost.

Also, repeated club data wastes storage (data redundancy).
cards.zh:
Think About（p.206）：Mary 认为 CLUB 表多余，把 CNAME、CROOM、CTEACH 直接放进 STUDENT。问题：
  • 更新问题：学会的名字、房间或老师一改，就要更新所有参加该学会的学生记录；漏改一条就数据不一致（inconsistent）。若 STUDENT 只存学会 ID，就完全不用改 STUDENT。
  • 删除问题：若某学会所有学生记录都被删，该学会的数据会永久丢失。
例：STUDENTCLUB 中把 Science Club 老师由 Mr Wong 改为 Mr Suen 要改 3 条记录；Art Club 唯一成员 Ada 退学，Art Club 资料就没了。

此外重复存学会资料也浪费空间（data redundancy）。

ex.q: In STUDENTCLUB(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CNAME, CROOM, CTEACH), three students are in Science Club. Write the SQL to change its teacher and say how many rows change. Compare with the two-table design.
ex.a:
UPDATE STUDENTCLUB SET CTEACH = 'Mr Suen'
WHERE CNAME = 'Science Club'
3 rows change. With CLUB as a separate table, only 1 row changes:
UPDATE CLUB SET TEACH = 'Mr Suen' WHERE CID = 4
ex.az: 单表要改 3 行，分表只改 CLUB 的 1 行。

cards.en:
A domain of an attribute is the set of all available values. The values in a domain always share the same data type.

Ways to write a domain:
  • A description: "a string of a 5-digit number", "a string of 40 characters at most".
  • A set of values: SEX ∈ {'M', 'F'}, CLASS ∈ {'1A', '1B', '1C', '1D'}.
  • A range: CNO ∈ {1 .. 30} (an integer between 1 and 30).
A foreign key's domain is the set of values of the primary key it references, plus NULL if allowed. E.g. CID in STUDENT has domain {1, 2, 3, 4, NULL} when CLUB holds CIDs 1 to 4.

In a DBMS a domain is implemented by the data type and constraints (e.g. CHAR(5), CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30)).
cards.zh:
Domain（域）是一个 attribute 所有可取值的集合，同一 domain 中的值数据类型相同。

表示方法：
  • 文字描述："a string of a 5-digit number"、"a string of 40 characters at most"。
  • 列举集合：SEX ∈ {'M', 'F'}，CLASS ∈ {'1A', '1B', '1C', '1D'}。
  • 范围：CNO ∈ {1 .. 30}（1 到 30 的整数）。
Foreign key 的 domain 是它所引用的 primary key 的值，再加上 NULL（如允许）。例如 CLUB 有 CID 1–4 时，STUDENT.CID 的 domain 是 {1, 2, 3, 4, NULL}。

在 DBMS 中，domain 用 data type 和 constraint（如 CHAR(5)、CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30)）实现。

ex.q: Students' ages range from 11 to 18. A field OPEN stores a shop's daily opening time. State the domains of AGE and OPEN.

cards.t: Common data types in a DBMS
cards.en:
Table 4.7:
Data typeKeywordSizeExample
IntegerINT / INTEGER4 bytes0, 283, -19
Real: floating pointFLOAT / DOUBLE4 / 8 bytes569.1, -27.382
Real: fixed pointDECIMALvaries34.50
Character: fixed lengthCHAR(n)varies'a', '1B 23'
Character: variable lengthVARCHAR(n)varies'rA9@Us'
BooleanBOOL / BOOLEAN1 byte0 (FALSE), 1 (TRUE)
DateDATE3 bytes'2025-12-31'
TimeTIME> 3 bytes'11:30:00'
DatetimeDATETIME> 5 bytes'2025-12-31 11:30:00'
Note: in SQLite (used by the practice site) types are flexible, but the same keywords are accepted.
cards.zh:
表 4.7：
类型Keyword大小例子
IntegerINT / INTEGER4 bytes0, 283, -19
Real 浮点FLOAT / DOUBLE4 / 8 bytes569.1
Real 定点DECIMAL不定34.50
定长字符串CHAR(n)不定'1B 23'
变长字符串VARCHAR(n)不定'rA9@Us'
BooleanBOOL / BOOLEAN1 byte0 (FALSE), 1 (TRUE)
DateDATE3 bytes'2025-12-31'
TimeTIME> 3 bytes'11:30:00'
DatetimeDATETIME> 5 bytes'2025-12-31 11:30:00'
注意：练习网站用的 SQLite 类型较宽松，但同样接受这些 keyword。

ex.q: Write a CREATE TABLE for EVENT with EID (integer), ENAME (up to 50 characters), EDATE (date), FEE (e.g. 34.5) and FINISHED (yes/no).
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE EVENT (
  EID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  ENAME VARCHAR(50),
  EDATE DATE,
  FEE FLOAT,
  FINISHED BOOLEAN
)
ex.az: 按每个字段的值选类型：整数 INT、文字 VARCHAR、日期 DATE、小数 FLOAT、是否 BOOLEAN。

cards.t: How to choose a data type
cards.en:
Decide from the values and how they are used, and read the examples given in the question:
  • Codes with leading zeros (e.g. a 6-digit SID such as 003512) → characters, otherwise the zeros are lost as an integer.
  • Phone numbers such as 3320-2310, website addresses, names → characters (no arithmetic, may contain '-').
  • Money with cents such as 30.9 or 34.5 → real / float, not integer.
  • Counts (stock, pages) → integer.
  • Yes/No facts (paid? finished? registered?) → Boolean.
  • Dates → date; daily opening time → time.
A foreign key must have the same data type as the primary key it references ("consistent with the answer in (b)").
cards.zh:
根据取值和用途决定，并留意题目给的例子：
  • 有前导零的代码（如 6 位 SID 003512）→ characters，用整数会丢掉前面的 0。
  • 电话号码如 3320-2310、网址、名字 → characters（不做运算，可能含 '-'）。
  • 金额有小数如 30.9、34.5 → real / float，不能用 integer。
  • 数量（库存、页数）→ integer。
  • 是/否（已付款？已结束？）→ Boolean。
  • 日期 → date；每日开门时间 → time。
Foreign key 的类型必须与它引用的 primary key 一致（"consistent with the answer in (b)"）。

ex.q: Show in SQLite why a 6-digit SID like 003512 should not be stored as an integer.
ex.a:
SELECT CAST('003512' AS INTEGER);   -- 3512
SELECT '003512';                    -- '003512'
As an integer the leading zeros are lost, so SID should be characters, e.g. CHAR(6).
ex.az: 转成整数会变 3512，前导零丢失，所以用 CHAR(6)。

cards.en:
Activity 4.3 tests whether a domain is reasonable:
  • Exchange rate as "an integer within {1 .. 10}" is NOT reasonable: an exchange rate is usually a real number, and can be lower than 1 or higher than 10.
  • Day of the week as "a date within {'1970-01-01' .. '2099-12-31'}" is NOT reasonable: a day of the week is one of {'Mon', ..., 'Sun'}, not a date.
  • Reasonable: price as a real number within {1 .. 9999}; blood type from {'O','A','B','AB'}; region from {'New Territories','Kowloon','Hong Kong Island'}; age of a bar customer as an integer at least 18; clothes size from {'XS','S','M','L','XL'}.
Check two things: is the data type right, and does the range/set include every real value and nothing impossible?
cards.zh:
Activity 4.3 考 domain 是否合理：
  • 汇率定为 "an integer within {1 .. 10}" 不合理：汇率通常是 real number，也可能小于 1 或大于 10。
  • 星期几定为 "a date within {'1970-01-01' .. '2099-12-31'}" 不合理：应是 {'Mon', …, 'Sun'} 之一，不是日期。
  • 合理的：价格为 {1 .. 9999} 内的实数；血型 {'O','A','B','AB'}；地区 {'New Territories','Kowloon','Hong Kong Island'}；酒吧顾客年龄 ≥ 18 的整数；衣服尺码 {'XS','S','M','L','XL'}。
检查两点：数据类型对不对？范围/集合是否包含所有真实值而不包含不可能的值？

ex.q: Is 'Mark of a test: an integer within {0 .. 100}' reasonable if the test allows half marks?
ex.a: Not reasonable: with half marks (e.g. 72.5) the type must be a real number within {0 .. 100}.
ex.az: 不合理：有半分，要用实数 {0 .. 100}。

cards.t: Example 4.1: entity types, data types, domain, relationship
cards.en:
Example 4.1 (school events): A(EID, ENAME, EDATE, FEE, FINISHED), B(SID, EID, AGE, PAID). Ages range 11 to 18; SID is a unique 6-digit number, some starting with zero; FEE e.g. 34.5.

Method:
  1. (a) Entity types: what does each row describe? → school events and students respectively.
  2. (b) EID integer / characters; EDATE date; FEE real / float (34.5 is not an integer).
  3. (c) SID characters (leading zeros); EID consistent with (b); PAID Boolean.
  4. (d) Domain of AGE: {11 .. 18}.
  5. (e) Relationship: B participates in A.
Always use evidence from the question (examples, descriptions) to justify each choice.
cards.zh:
Example 4.1（学校活动）：A(EID, ENAME, EDATE, FEE, FINISHED)、B(SID, EID, AGE, PAID)。年龄 11–18；SID 是唯一 6 位数字，有些以 0 开头；FEE 如 34.5。

做法：
  1. (a) Entity types：每行描述什么？→ school events and students respectively。
  2. (b) EID 整数/字符；EDATE 日期；FEE real / float（34.5 不是整数）。
  3. (c) SID characters（前导零）；EID 与 (b) 一致；PAID Boolean。
  4. (d) AGE 的 domain：{11 .. 18}。
  5. (e) 关系：B participates in A。
每个选择都要用题目中的证据（例子、描述）支持。

ex.q: Checkpoint 4.1: A(PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE, SID) and B(SID, SNAME, OPEN, CLOSE, BHOUR). Give data types of PNAME, STOCK, PRICE and the relationship.
ex.a:
PNAME: characters; STOCK: integer; PRICE: real / float.
Relationship: B sells A / A is sold by B.
ex.az: PNAME 字符、STOCK 整数、PRICE 实数；关系：B sells A。

cards.en:
A database schema is a text string that describes a database table. Format:
TABLE (FIELD1, FIELD2, FIELD3, ...)
e.g. STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL): the table name comes first, then the attributes in brackets.

The primary key is often underlined in the schema: STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL). A composite primary key has all its fields underlined, e.g. ENROL (SID, SUBID).

In DSE answers, write the schema, underline the primary key, and state the foreign keys on the next line ("Foreign key: GID" or "Foreign key: N/A"). More examples: CLASS (CLASS, ROOM, TEACHID); TEACHER (TEACHID, TEACHNAME, TITLE, SEAT); SUBJECT (SUBID, SUBNAME, TEACHID).
cards.zh:
Database schema（模式）是描述一张数据库表的文字串，格式：
TABLE (FIELD1, FIELD2, FIELD3, ...)
如 STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL)：先写表名，括号内是 attributes。

Primary key 通常加底线：STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL)。复合主键的每个字段都加底线，如 ENROL (SID, SUBID)。

DSE 作答：写出 schema，给 primary key 加底线，下一行写出 foreign keys（"Foreign key: GID" 或 "Foreign key: N/A"）。更多例子：CLASS (CLASS, ROOM, TEACHID)；TEACHER (TEACHID, TEACHNAME, TITLE, SEAT)。

ex.q: Checkpoint 4.4(a): PAYMENT has TID, PAYERID, PAYEEID, AMOUNT, TTIME; PAYERID and PAYEEID refer to ACCOUNT(AID). Write the schema.
ex.a:
PAYMENT (TID, PAYERID, PAYEEID, AMOUNT, TTIME)
Foreign key: PAYERID, PAYEEID
ex.az: 主键 TID 加底线；外键 PAYERID、PAYEEID（一张表可有多个外键）。

cards.en:
To distinguish between records in a database table, there must be key fields. Different types of key fields serve different purposes:
  • Candidate key: always stores unique data for every record, so it can identify records.
  • Composite key: a candidate key made of more than one field.
  • Primary key: the one candidate key chosen by the database administrator to identify records.
  • Foreign key: a field that refers to the primary key of another table, showing a relationship.
This links back to 4.1: an entity must be unique, so the table needs keys that can tell two records apart.
cards.zh:
为了区分表中的记录，必须有 key fields（关键字段）。不同的 key 有不同用途：
  • Candidate key（候选键）：每条记录的值都唯一，可用来识别记录。
  • Composite key（复合键）：由多于一个字段组成的 candidate key。
  • Primary key（主键）：数据库管理员从 candidate keys 中选出来识别记录的那一个。
  • Foreign key（外键）：引用另一表 primary key 的字段，用来表示关系。
与 4.1 呼应：entity 必须唯一，所以表需要 key 来分辨两条记录。

ex.q: STUDENT(SID, NAME, HKID, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL, CLUBID). Classify the keys if SID is chosen as the primary key and CLUBID refers to CLUB.
ex.a:
Candidate keys: SID, HKID, EMAIL, CLASS+CNO (composite key).
Primary key: SID.
Foreign key: CLUBID.
ex.az: 候选键 SID、HKID、EMAIL、CLASS+CNO；主键 SID；外键 CLUBID。

cards.en:
A candidate key is a key field that always stores unique data for every record. Therefore a candidate key can be used to identify records.

Since it identifies records, its stored value cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.

Summary (p.237): a candidate key
  • stores unique data;
  • cannot store NULL;
  • may consist of more than one field;
  • must be minimal; and
  • is the candidate for the primary key.
Important: "unique" means unique for all possible records, not just the current data. NAME may have no duplicates today, but two students could share a name, so NAME is not a candidate key. EMAIL is: no two students share the same personal email address.
cards.zh:
Candidate key（候选键）是每条记录都存唯一值的关键字段，所以可用来识别记录。

因为要识别记录，它的值不能为空，即不能是 NULL。

总结（p.237）：candidate key
  • 存唯一的数据；
  • 不能存 NULL；
  • 可由多于一个字段组成；
  • 必须是 minimal（最少）；
  • 是 primary key 的候选。
重点："唯一"是指所有可能的记录都唯一，不只是目前的数据。NAME 现时没有重复，但两个学生可能同名，所以 NAME 不是 candidate key；EMAIL 是，因为两个学生不会有同一个个人电邮。

ex.q: Use SQL to test whether EMAIL currently has duplicates or NULLs in STUDENT. Does passing the test prove it is a candidate key?
ex.a:
SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT
GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT WHERE EMAIL IS NULL;
Empty / 0 results show the current data is OK, but it does not prove a candidate key: the decision depends on whether duplicates are possible in reality.
ex.az: 查询无重复只说明现在的数据没问题，是否 candidate key 要看现实中是否可能重复。

cards.en:
