ex.a: Circle next to Task: reading from Employee, an employee may or may not have tasks (optional). Bar next to Employee: reading from Task, each task must be held by an employee (mandatory).
ex.az: 圆圈在 Task 旁：员工可以没有任务；竖线在 Employee 旁：每个任务必须属于某员工。

cards.t: Mandatory and optional sides in real life
cards.tz: 生活中的强制与非强制
cards.en:
Look for wording that guarantees participation.

Mandatory side examples (every entity must take part):
• Each employee must belong to one department.
• Every course must be taught by one or more lecturers.
• An assignment must be done by at least one student.
• Each vehicle must have a vehicle registration plate.

Optional side examples (not every entity takes part):
• An employee may or may not have any tasks at hand.
• Each hotel room may or may not be occupied by guests.
• A social media account may or may not have a profile picture.
• A citizen may or may not own a vehicle.

Key words: must, every, exactly, at least one → mandatory; may, may not, some, not every, possibly none → optional.
cards.zh:
看描述是否保证参与。

Mandatory 例子：每个员工必须属于一个部门；每门课必须有一位或以上讲师；每份功课至少由一个学生完成；每辆车必须有车牌。

Optional 例子：员工手头可能没有任务；酒店房间可能没人住；社交账户可能没有头像；市民可能没有车。

关键词：must, every, exactly, at least one → mandatory；may, may not, some, not every, possibly none → optional。

ex.q: 'Each patient is assigned to a ward. It is possible that there are not enough patients to fill every ward.' Decide each side for Ward — Accommodate — Patient.
ex.a:
Each patient is assigned to a ward → from the Patient side, participation is mandatory (bar next to Ward).
Some wards may have no patients → from the Ward side, participation is optional (circle next to Patient).
ex.az: 每个病人一定有病房 → mandatory；病房可能没病人 → optional。（课本 Checkpoint 5.2(b)）

cards.en:
When both sides are mandatory: for each entity a of type A, there must be at least one related entity b, and vice versa.

Example: School — Have — Principal with a bar on both ends.
• Every school must have a principal.
• Every principal must belong to a school.

In tables, this means the foreign key column may not be NULL, and in practice every row of the other table is referenced by at least one row.

Use this only when the scenario really guarantees both directions. Many exam scenarios that look mandatory on one side are optional on the other, e.g. there may be spare computers, spare rooms or awards not given.
cards.zh:
两边都 mandatory：for each a，至少有一个相关 b，反之亦然。

例：School — Have — Principal 两端都画竖线：
• 每间学校必须有校长；
• 每位校长必须属于一间学校。

在表中：外键不能 NULL，另一表每行也至少被引用一次。

只有情景真的保证两个方向都参与才用。很多题目一边强制另一边其实可选（多出来的电脑、空房间、没颁出的奖）。

ex.q: 'An assignment must be done by at least one student, and every student must do at least one assignment.' Draw the constraints.
ex.a: Student —Do— Assignment with a bar near Assignment (each student must do an assignment) and a bar near Student (each assignment must be done by a student). Both sides mandatory.
ex.az: 两个方向都有 must → 两端都画竖线。

cards.tz: B. 一边强制一边非强制
cards.en:
When side A is mandatory and side B is optional:
• for each a, there may or may not be a related b;
• for each b, there must be at least one related a.

Example: Teacher — Be assigned to — Class (class teacher).
• A teacher may or may not be assigned as a class teacher (circle next to Class).
• Every class must have a class teacher (bar next to Teacher).

In tables: if the foreign key is in CLASS (CLASS.TID), it is NOT NULL. If it were stored in TEACHER (TEACHER.CID), it could be NULL for teachers without a class.

This is the most common combination in exam questions.
cards.zh:
A 那边 mandatory、B 那边 optional：
• 每个 a 可有可无相关 b；
• 每个 b 必须至少有一个相关 a。

例：Teacher — Be assigned to — Class（班主任）：
• 老师可以不是班主任（Class 旁画圆圈）；
• 每班必须有班主任（Teacher 旁画竖线）。

表中：外键放在 CLASS（CLASS.TID）就 NOT NULL；若放在 TEACHER（TEACHER.CID）则没班的老师为 NULL。

这是考试最常见的组合。

ex.q: Restaurant: each occupied table is served by exactly one waiter; each waiter must serve at least one occupied table; an unoccupied table has no waiter. Give the participation of Waiter — Serve — Table.
ex.a:
Waiter side: each waiter must serve a table → mandatory (bar next to Table).
Table side: an unoccupied table has no waiter → optional (circle next to Waiter).
ex.az: 服务员必须服务至少一张台 → 强制；空台没有服务员 → 非强制。（课本 Checkpoint 5.2(c)）

cards.en:
When both sides are optional: each entity a may or may not have a related b, and vice versa.

Example: Citizen — Be infected with — Disease, circles on both ends.
• A citizen may not have any disease.
• A disease (e.g. a rare one) may have no infected citizens at the moment.

Summary table
CombinationMeaningExample
Mandatory & mandatoryboth must take partSchool–Principal
Mandatory & optionalone must, the other may notTeacher–Class
Optional & optionalneither must take partCitizen–Disease
cards.zh:
两边都 optional：每个 a 可以没有相关 b，反之亦然。

例：Citizen — Be infected with — Disease，两端都画圆圈：
• 市民可以没有病；
• 某种疾病（如罕见病）可以暂时没有患者。

总结
组合意思例
强制+强制两边都必须参与School–Principal
强制+非强制一边必须，一边可不Teacher–Class
非强制+非强制两边都不必Citizen–Disease

ex.q: Citizen — Own — Vehicle: a citizen may or may not own a vehicle; a vehicle may be owned by a company instead of a citizen. Which combination?
ex.a: Both sides are optional: a citizen may own no vehicle, and a vehicle may have no citizen owner. Circles on both ends.
ex.az: 市民可无车，车可属于公司 → 两边都画圆圈。

cards.en:
Method:
1. Write the relationship as two sentences, one in each direction.
2. For each sentence ask: is it guaranteed that every entity takes part?
3. Words like must, exactly, at least one, every, each ... is assigned → mandatory. Words like may, some, not enough, possibly none → optional.
4. Use the numbers carefully: if there are more of one type than can be matched, some will be left out → optional.

Examples from the book:
• 40 computers, 25 students, each student uses exactly one computer → student side mandatory; there are spare computers → computer side optional.
• 16 subjects × 3 awards = 48 awards, 40 students. A student is not guaranteed an award → optional. Each subject has at least 5 students so every award is given → mandatory.
Do not judge by numbers alone; judge by what the scenario guarantees.
cards.zh:
方法：
1. 把关系写成两个方向的句子；
2. 每句问：是否保证每个实体都参与？
3. must, exactly, at least one, every, each ... is assigned → mandatory；may, some, not enough, possibly none → optional；
4. 小心数量：一边比另一边多、配不完 → 多的那边 optional。

课本例子：
• 40 台电脑、25 个学生，每人恰用一台 → 学生一边 mandatory；有空闲电脑 → 电脑一边 optional。
• 16 科 × 3 奖 = 48 个奖、40 名学生：学生不保证得奖 → optional；每科至少 5 人，奖一定颁出 → mandatory。
别只看数字，要看情景保证了什么。

ex.q: Food delivery: each order is assigned an available courier; each courier gets at most one order at a time; there may not be enough orders for every courier. Decide both sides of Food order — Be assigned to — Courier.
ex.a:
Each food order is assigned a courier → order side mandatory (bar next to Courier).
Not every courier gets an order → courier side optional (circle next to Food order).
ex.az: 每张订单一定有送餐员 → 强制；送餐员可能没单 → 非强制。（课本 Checkpoint 5.2(d)）

cards.en:
The cardinality of a relationship specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type.

It is shown by a character written on the line next to the entity on the far side:
• 1 = one (at most one)
• M (or N) = many

Example: Student — Join —1 Sports event means a student may join one sports event at most. If it were M instead, a student could join many events.

Read both directions: the character next to Sports event tells how many events one student can join; the character next to Student tells how many students one event can have. The three types of relationship are one-to-one (1:1), one-to-many (1:M) and many-to-many (M:N).
cards.zh:
Cardinality（基数）：specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type。

用写在靠近对面实体线旁的字符表示：
• 1 = one（最多一个）
• M（或 N）= many（多个）

例：Student — Join —1 Sports event 表示每个学生最多参加一个项目；若写 M 则可参加多项。

两个方向都要读：Sports event 旁的字符 = 一个学生可参加几项；Student 旁的字符 = 一个项目可有几人。三类关系：one-to-one (1:1)、one-to-many (1:M)、many-to-many (M:N)。

ex.q: Student 1 —Join— M Event (1 written next to Student, M next to Event). Describe it in words.
ex.a: M next to Event: a student can join many events. 1 next to Student: an event can have at most one student. This is a one-to-many relationship from Student to Event.
ex.az: Event 旁 M：学生可参加多项；Student 旁 1：每项最多一人 → 1:M。

cards.tz: 参与限制 vs 基数
cards.en:
The two ideas answer different questions and are drawn together on each end of a line:
• Participation constraint (bar | or circle O) answers "must there be at least one?" (minimum is 1 or 0).
• Cardinality (1 or M) answers "at most how many?" (maximum is one or many).

Combined meanings at one end:
ParticipationCardinalityMeaning
Mandatory1exactly one
Optional1zero or one
MandatoryMat least one, if not many (one or more)
OptionalMzero or many
Exam answers should describe both, e.g. "Each publisher publishes one or more books, while a book is published by exactly one publisher."
cards.zh:
两者回答不同问题，画在同一端：
• Participation（| 或 O）：最少是不是 1（必须有吗）；
• Cardinality（1 或 M）：最多多少。

组合：
参与基数意思
Mandatory1exactly one 恰好一个
Optional1zero or one
MandatoryMat least one, if not many
OptionalMzero or many
答题要两样都写，例：“Each publisher publishes one or more books, while a book is published by exactly one publisher.”

ex.q: Store M —Sell— N Book: circle next to Book, bar next to Store. Describe the relationship.
ex.a:
Next to Book: optional + N → each store may or may not sell more than one different book (zero or many).
Next to Store: mandatory + M → each book is sold by at least one store, if not more.
ex.az: Book 旁圆圈+N：商店可卖零或多本书；Store 旁竖线+M：每本书至少一间店卖。（课本 Checkpoint 5.4 Q3(b)）

cards.en:
In a one-to-one relationship, for each entity a there is at most one related entity b, and vice versa.

Examples:
• School 1 — Have — 1 Principal (both mandatory: each school has exactly one principal).
• Teacher 1 — Be assigned to — 1 Class (a teacher has one class or none; each class has exactly one class teacher).
• Others: employee and desk, vehicle and registration plate, department and department head.

Implementation: put a foreign key in one of the tables, e.g. SCHOOL.PID referencing PRINCIPAL, or TEACHER.CID referencing CLASS. If the side holding the FK is optional (a teacher may have no class), the FK may be NULL. Usually put the FK on the mandatory side (CLASS.TID NOT NULL) to avoid NULLs. The FK should also be unique, since each value may appear only once.
cards.zh:
One-to-one（一对一）：for each a, at most one related b, and vice versa。

例：
• School 1 — Have — 1 Principal（两边强制：每校恰有一位校长）；
• Teacher 1 — Be assigned to — 1 Class（老师有一班或没有；每班恰一位班主任）；
• 其他：员工与座位、车辆与车牌、部门与部门主管。

实现：在其中一个表放外键，如 SCHOOL.PID 或 TEACHER.CID。若放外键那边是 optional（老师可以没班），外键可为 NULL；通常放在强制一边（CLASS.TID NOT NULL）以免 NULL。外键值也应唯一（每个值只出现一次）。

ex.q: TEACHER(TID, TNAME) and CLASS(CID, ROOM). Each class has exactly one class teacher; a teacher may have no class. Where should the foreign key go?
ex.a: Put TID in CLASS: CLASS(CID, ROOM, TID), TID NOT NULL and unique. Every class has a value, so no NULLs. (Putting CID in TEACHER also works but gives NULL for teachers without a class.)
ex.az: 外键放 CLASS.TID（不为空、唯一），避免 NULL。

cards.t: Merging a one-to-one relationship into an attribute
cards.en:
If we do not need to store extra data about the other entity, a one-to-one relationship can be simplified: the other entity becomes just an attribute.

Example: if we only need the principal's name, use
SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, DISTRICT, PRINCIPAL)
instead of separate SCHOOL and PRINCIPAL tables. Principal is no longer an entity type.

Trade-off: this trades flexibility and level of details for simplicity and performance (no join needed). If later we need the principal's phone, email or date of appointment, we must change the table structure. So proceed with caution.

This only works for 1:1. In a 1:M relationship, merging would put many values in one row (violating 1NF) or repeat data.
cards.zh:
若不需要存另一实体的额外资料，1:1 关系可简化：把另一实体变成一个 attribute。

例：只要校长姓名：SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, DISTRICT, PRINCIPAL)，不用独立 PRINCIPAL 表，Principal 不再是 entity type。

代价：trades flexibility and level of details for simplicity and performance（查询不用 join）。以后要存校长电话、电邮就要改表结构，所以要 proceed with caution。

只适用 1:1；1:M 合并会一格多值（违反 1NF）或重复数据。

ex.q: A vehicle has exactly one registration plate and the plate has only its number. Suggest a simpler design.
ex.a: Make the plate number an attribute: VEHICLE(VID, MODEL, COLOUR, PLATENO). No PLATE table and no join are needed. If plate details (issue date, fee) must be stored later, a separate table would be more flexible.
ex.az: 车牌只需号码 → 作为 VEHICLE 的属性 PLATENO；简单但不灵活。

cards.en:
In a one-to-many relationship, for each entity a there are many related entities b, but for each b there is at most one related a.

Examples:
• Class 1 — Have — M Student: each class has at least one student; each student belongs to exactly one class.
• Citizen 1 — Have — M Criminal record: a citizen may have zero or many records (optional); each record belongs to exactly one citizen.
• Others: library borrower and books, food platform account and orders, department and employees, school and classrooms.

Implementation: put the foreign key in the table on the many side, e.g. STUDENT.CID references CLASS.CID, CRIMINALRECORD.CID references CITIZEN.CID. Never try to store the many values in the one side.

Seen from the other direction, a one-to-many relationship is a many-to-one relationship (Student M — Belong to — 1 Class).
cards.zh:
One-to-many（一对多）：每个 a 可有多个 b，但每个 b 最多一个 a。

例：
• Class 1 — Have — M Student：每班至少一人，每生恰属一班；
• Citizen 1 — Have — M Criminal record：市民可零或多条记录；每条记录恰属一人；
• 其他：借书人与书、外卖账户与订单、部门与员工、学校与课室。

实现：外键放在 many 那边的表，如 STUDENT.CID 参照 CLASS.CID。不要把多个值塞进 one 那边。

反过来看就是 many-to-one（Student M — Belong to — 1 Class）。

ex.q: A food platform: each account can place many orders; each order is placed by exactly one account. Write the schemas.
ex.a:
ACCOUNT(AID, USERNAME, PHONE)
ORDERS(OID, ODATE, AMOUNT, AID), AID is a foreign key referencing ACCOUNT.AID (NOT NULL).
SELECT a.USERNAME, COUNT(o.OID)
FROM ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN ORDERS o ON a.AID = o.AID
GROUP BY a.AID, a.USERNAME;
counts orders for every account, including 0.
ex.az: 外键 AID 放在 many 那边的 ORDERS 表。

cards.t: Do not store a one-to-many relationship in one table
cards.tz: 一对多不要合成一个表
cards.en:
It is tempting to copy the class data into the student table: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CNAME, ROOM). This creates redundant data, because the room of a class is repeated once for every student in it.

Problems:
• If the room of 3B changes from 402 to 403, three records must be changed. Missing one gives inconsistent data.
• If Ada, the only student of 3A, is deleted, the room of 3A is lost.
• A new class with no students cannot be stored.

These problems are called anomalies (update, deletion, insertion) and are solved by normalisation (5.4 and 5.5). The correct design is two tables, CLASS(CNAME, ROOM) and STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CNAME) with the foreign key on the many side.
cards.zh:
把班级资料抄进学生表 STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CNAME, ROOM) 会产生 redundant data：每个学生都重复一次班房号。

问题：
• 3B 房间由 402 改 403 要改3 条记录，漏改就不一致；
• 删除 3A 唯一学生 Ada，3A 房间资料消失；
• 没学生的新班无法储存。

这些叫 anomalies（update、deletion、insertion），用 normalisation 解决（5.4、5.5）。正确设计：CLASS(CNAME, ROOM) + STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CNAME)，外键在 many 那边。

ex.q: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CNAME, ROOM) has 3 students in 3B (room 402). The room changes to 403. Write the SQL and state the risk.
ex.a:
UPDATE STUDENT SET ROOM = '403' WHERE CNAME = '3B';
This changes 3 rows. If someone updates by SID for only one student, the table shows 3B in both 402 and 403: data inconsistency (update anomaly). With a separate CLASS table only one row changes.
ex.az: 要改 3 行；只改一部分就不一致。分表后只改 CLASS 一行。

cards.en:
In a many-to-many relationship, for each entity a there are many related entities b, and vice versa. In the ER diagram one side is written M and the other is usually written N.

Examples:
• Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject: both mandatory (each student takes at least one; a subject nobody takes is cancelled).
• Citizen M — Own — N Property: both optional (a citizen may own nothing; a property may belong to the government or a company).
• Others: books and authors, actors and movies, doctors and patients, customers and products.

Implementation: a M:N relationship cannot be stored by a single foreign key. It is usually stored in a separate table whose records each hold one pair, e.g. ENROLMENT(SID, EID) and OWNERSHIP(CID, PID). This is called resolving the relationship.
cards.zh:
Many-to-many（多对多）：每个 a 有多个 b，反之亦然。ER 图一边写 M，另一边通常写 N。

例：
• Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject：两边强制（每生至少选一科；没人选的科会取消）；
• Citizen M — Own — N Property：两边可选（市民可无物业；物业可属政府或公司）；
• 其他：书与作者、演员与电影、医生与病人、顾客与产品。

实现：不能只靠一个外键储存；通常用独立的表，每条记录存一对，如 ENROLMENT(SID, EID)、OWNERSHIP(CID, PID)，这叫 resolve。

ex.q: Is 'author writes book' 1:M or M:N? Justify and give the tables.
ex.a:
M:N: an author can write many books, and a book can have several authors.
Tables: AUTHOR(AID, ANAME), BOOK(ISBN, TITLE), WRITE(AID, ISBN), where AID and ISBN in WRITE are foreign keys.
ex.az: 一个作者多本书，一本书可多作者 → M:N，用 WRITE 表存配对。

cards.t: Drawing an ER diagram from a scenario
cards.en:
Break the scenario into sentences and handle one pair of entity types at a time:
1. Find the two entity types (nouns) and the verb linking them → the relationship diamond.
2. Use must / may wording to set the participation (bar or circle) on each end.
3. Use one, only one, exclusively vs multiple, many, any number, several to set the cardinality (1 or M) on each end.
4. If both ends are many, write M on one and N on the other.
5. Add attributes (ellipses) and underline the keys.

Book example: "A company may own several offices; an office belongs to only one company" → Company 1 — Own — M Office, office end optional (a company may have none), company end mandatory.
"Each worker works in exactly one office; every office has many workers" → Office 1 — Have — M Worker, both mandatory.
"A menu offers many dishes; a dish is on many menus; some dishes are never ordered" → Menu M — Offer — N Dish; Dish M — Be ordered by — N Customer with the dish's participation optional.
cards.zh:
逐句拆，一次处理一对实体：
1. 找两个 entity types（名词）和连接的动词 → 菱形；
2. 用 must / may 决定两端的 participation（竖线或圆圈）；
3. 用 one, only one, exclusively 对比 multiple, many, any number, several 决定 cardinality（1 或 M）；
4. 两端都是多 → 一边 M 一边 N；
5. 加椭圆属性，主键下划线。

例：“公司可有多个办公室，办公室只属一间公司” → Company 1 — Own — M Office，office 端 optional，company 端 mandatory。
“每个工人恰在一个办公室，每个办公室有很多工人” → Office 1 — Have — M Worker，两边强制。
“菜单有多道菜，菜出现在多张菜单；有些菜没人点” → Menu M — Offer — N Dish；Dish M — Be ordered by — N Customer，菜那边 optional。

ex.q: 'Each teacher may teach several elective subjects, or none. Each elective subject is taught by one or several teachers.' Give participation and cardinality for Teacher — Teach — Elective subject.
ex.a:
Next to Elective subject: teacher may teach none or several → optional, N.
Next to Teacher: each subject taught by one or several → mandatory, M.
So Teacher M — Teach — N Elective subject.
ex.az: 老师可教零或多科 → 科目旁圆圈+N；每科至少一个老师 → 老师旁竖线+M。（课本 Checkpoint 5.3 Q1(a)）

cards.t: From table structure to ER diagram
cards.tz: 由表结构反推 ER 图
cards.en:
We can also read an ER diagram off existing tables:
• A foreign key in table X referencing table Y means X and Y have a relationship. The FK side is the many side (a Y key value can appear many times in X) and each X row links to one Y (cardinality 1 next to Y).
• FK NOT NULL → every X must have a Y → mandatory (bar next to Y).
• FK may be NULL → optional.
• Nothing forces every Y key to appear in X → usually optional on that side (circle next to X).
• The FK itself is not drawn as an attribute.

Example: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID NOT NULL, MID NOT NULL) gives Postman 1 — Deliver — M Letter and Letter M — Originate from — 1 Mailbox. A postman may deliver zero or many letters; each letter has exactly one postman.
cards.zh:
也可以由表反推 ER 图：
• X 表有外键参照 Y → X 与 Y 有关系；外键所在的 X 是 many 一边（同一 Y 值可在 X 出现多次），每行 X 只对应一个 Y（Y 旁写 1）。
• 外键 NOT NULL → 每个 X 必有 Y → mandatory（Y 旁竖线）；
• 外键可 NULL → optional；
• 没规定每个 Y 都要出现在 X → 那边通常 optional（X 旁圆圈）；
• 外键本身不画成属性。

例：LETTER(LID, RADD, PID NOT NULL, MID NOT NULL) → Postman 1 — Deliver — M Letter；Letter M — Originate from — 1 Mailbox。邮差可送零或多封，每封信恰一个邮差。

ex.q: STORE(SID, SNAME), PRODUCT(PID, PNAME, PRICE, SID NOT NULL), PRODUCTREVIEW(PRID, PID NOT NULL, PRTEXT, RATING). Draw the relationships.
ex.a:
PRODUCT.SID NOT NULL → Store 1 — Sell — M Product; each product sold by exactly one store.
PRODUCTREVIEW.PID NOT NULL → Product 1 — Review — M Product review; each review is about exactly one product, a product may have zero or many reviews.
Attributes: Store ID, Store name, Store website, Store phone; Product ID, Product name, Product price; Review ID, Review text, Product rating. No SID/PID ellipses on the many side.
ex.az: 外键 NOT NULL → 每个产品恰一间店，每条评论恰一个产品；外键不画成椭圆。（课本 Checkpoint 5.3 Q2）

cards.t: Activity 5.1: four ways to store a many-to-many relationship
cards.en:
Students and elective subjects (M:N) can be stored in four ways. Judge each by: new subject? more than three subjects? list History students? list rooms per student? count subjects per student?
MethodProblem
1. One field holds a list, EIDLIST = '1,11,12'multiple values in one field (breaks 1NF). LIKE '%1%' also matches 11; strings must be split to join or count.
2. One Boolean field per subject: HISTORY, PHYSICS, ICTrepeating attributes. A new subject needs a new field; cannot join to ELECTIVE to get rooms.
3. ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3repeating attributes. More than 3 subjects needs new fields; long SQL with OR / UNION; many NULLs.
4. Separate table ENROLMENT(SID, EID), one record per pairBest: all five tasks are easy with normal JOIN, WHERE and COUNT; no structure change ever needed.
Methods 1–3 violate the rules of 1NF, which is why we need three tables to resolve a M:N relationship.
cards.zh:
学生与选修科（M:N）有四种存法。检验：加新科？选多于三科？列出读 History 的学生？列每生的课室？数每生科数？
方法问题
1. 一个字段存列表 EIDLIST='1,11,12'multiple values（违反 1NF）；LIKE '%1%' 会误中 11；要拆字符串才能 join/计数
2. 每科一个 Boolean 字段repeating attributes；新科要加字段；不能 join ELECTIVE 拿课室
3. ELEC1/ELEC2/ELEC3repeating attributes；超过 3 科要加字段；SQL 冗长；很多 NULL
4. 独立表 ENROLMENT(SID, EID)，一对一条记录最佳：五项都容易，普通 JOIN/WHERE/COUNT；永不用改结构
方法 1–3 都违反 1NF，所以要用三个表来 resolve M:N。

ex.q: With Method 4, write SQL to list the names of students enrolled in History (EID 1).
ex.a:
SELECT s.NAME
FROM STUDENT s, ENROLMENT e
WHERE s.SID = e.SID AND e.EID = 1;
With Method 1, WHERE EIDLIST LIKE '%1%' would wrongly return students taking Physics (11) or ICT (12).
ex.az: 方法 4 只需普通 join；方法 1 的 LIKE '%1%' 会误中 11、12。

cards.en:
To resolve a many-to-many relationship, split it into a one-to-many and a many-to-one relationship by adding an associative entity type in the middle.

Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject becomes
Student 1 — Make — M Enrolment M — Be made for — 1 Elective subject.

The associative table (ENROLMENT) has two foreign keys, SID and EID, referencing the primary keys of STUDENT and ELECTIVE. Usually SID + EID together form a composite primary key, so the same pair cannot be stored twice.

Other book examples:
• Citizen 1 — Have — M Ownership M — Apply to — 1 Property
• Actor 1 — Play — M Role M — Exist in — 1 Movie
• Doctor 1 — Provide — M Treatment M — Treat — 1 Patient
• Customer 1 — Make — M Order M — Include — 1 Product
Any reasonable names for the new entity type and relationships are acceptable.
cards.zh:
Resolve M:N：在中间加一个 associative entity type（关联实体），把它拆成 one-to-many + many-to-one。

Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject 变成
Student 1 — Make — M Enrolment M — Be made for — 1 Elective subject。

关联表 ENROLMENT 有两个外键 SID、EID，分别参照 STUDENT 与 ELECTIVE 的主键；通常 SID + EID 合成 composite primary key，同一对不能存两次。

课本其他例子：
• Citizen 1—Have—M Ownership M—Apply to—1 Property
• Actor 1—Play—M Role M—Exist in—1 Movie
• Doctor 1—Provide—M Treatment M—Treat—1 Patient
• Customer 1—Make—M Order M—Include—1 Product
新实体与关系名合理即可。

ex.q: Resolve Actor M — Star in — N Movie and write the CREATE TABLE for the new table.
ex.a:
Actor 1 — Play — M Role M — Exist in — 1 Movie.
CREATE TABLE ROLE (
  AID INT,
  MID INT,
  RNAME VARCHAR(30),
  PRIMARY KEY (AID, MID),
  FOREIGN KEY (AID) REFERENCES ACTOR(AID),
  FOREIGN KEY (MID) REFERENCES MOVIE(MID)
);
ex.az: 加关联实体 Role，复合主键 AID+MID，两个外键。（参考课本 Checkpoint 5.4 Q1(b)）

cards.en:
Some attributes describe the relationship itself, not either entity. They have no meaning without both sides, so they belong to the associative entity (or are drawn on the M:N diamond before resolving).

Examples:
• Student M — Borrow — N Book: checkout date, due date, return date describe one borrowing, so CHECKOUT(SID, BID, CDATE, DDATE, RDATE).
• Customer — Order — Product: order date, delivery date, product quantity go into ORDER.
• Store — Sell — Book: stock and price differ per store, so SELL(SID, ISBN, STOCK, PRICE).
• Doctor — Treat — Patient: treatment name and date go into TREATMENT.

Tip: ask "does this value depend on both entities?" If yes, it is an attribute of the relationship.
cards.zh:
有些属性描述的是关系本身，离开任一边就没有意义，所以放在 associative entity（resolve 前画在 M:N 菱形上）。

例：
• Student M—Borrow—N Book：借出日期、到期日、归还日 属于某次借书 → CHECKOUT(SID, BID, CDATE, DDATE, RDATE)；
• Customer—Order—Product：订单日期、送货日期、数量 放 ORDER；
• Store—Sell—Book：存货和售价 每间店不同 → SELL(SID, ISBN, STOCK, PRICE)；
• Doctor—Treat—Patient：治疗名称和日期 放 TREATMENT。

技巧：问“这个值是否同时取决于两个实体？”是 → 关系的属性。

ex.q: ER diagram: Store M — Sell — N Book, with ellipses Stock and Price on Sell; Publisher 1 — Publish — M Book. Write all table structures.
ex.a:
STORE(SID, SNAME, LOCAT)
PUBLISHER(PID, PNAME, PHONE)
BOOK(ISBN, BNAME, PDATE, PID) with PID a foreign key (1:M, FK on many side)
SELL(SID, ISBN, STOCK, PRICE): resolves the M:N, and holds the relationship's attributes.
ex.az: Stock、Price 是 Sell 的属性 → 放 SELL 表；PID 放 BOOK。（课本 Checkpoint 5.4 Q3(a)）

cards.en:
Using Student — Join — Sports event:
Next to StudentNext to EventTypeMeaning
11one-to-onea student joins at most one event; an event has at most one student
1Mone-to-manya student joins many events; an event has at most one student
M1many-to-onea student joins at most one event; an event has many students
MNmany-to-manya student joins many events; an event has many students
Tip: the character written next to the far entity says how many of that entity each entity on this side can relate to.

Implementation summary: 1:1 → FK in one table (or merge into an attribute); 1:M → FK on the many side; M:N → resolve with an associative table holding two FKs.
cards.zh:
以 Student — Join — Sports event 为例：
Student 旁Event 旁类型意思
111:1学生最多一项；项目最多一人
1M1:M学生可多项；项目最多一人
M1M:1学生最多一项；项目可多人
MNM:N学生多项；项目多人
技巧：写在对面实体旁的字符 = 这边每个实体可关联多少个对面实体。

实现：1:1 → 外键放一边（或并成属性）；1:M → 外键放 many 边；M:N → 用含两个外键的关联表。

ex.q: 20 students, each has a zodiac sign; there are 12 zodiac signs; each zodiac sign refers to exactly one constellation. Give the cardinalities.
ex.a:
Student M — Have — 1 Zodiac sign (each student one sign; a sign shared by many students).
Zodiac sign 1 — Refer to — 1 Constellation (one-to-one).
ex.az: 学生多对一星座；星座一对一星宿。（课本 Checkpoint 5.3 Q1(b)）

cards.en:
Data redundancy refers to duplicated pieces of data that are redundant and occupy precious storage space. It is usually caused by a poorly designed database.

Example: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH, EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE) with primary key SID+EID:
SIDSNAMECLASSCTEACHEIDENAMEETEACHSCORE
03493Ada3AMrs Au2PhysicsMr Poon0
03496Clem3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho78
03496Clem3BMr Bao2PhysicsMr Poon98
03496Clem3BMr Bao3ICTMr Suen89
03505Eva3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho83
...
Clem appears in 3 records, so "3B, Mr Bao" is stored 3 times. ICT appears in 3 records, so "Mr Suen" is stored 3 times.

When storage is cheap, wasted space alone is not fatal. The real danger is that redundancy causes three kinds of anomalies: update, insertion and deletion anomalies, which make the data inconsistent or lost.
cards.zh:
Data redundancy（数据冗余）：duplicated pieces of data that are redundant and occupy precious storage space，通常由 poorly designed database 引起。

例：STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH, EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE)，主键 SID+EID：
SIDSNAMECLASSCTEACHEIDENAMEETEACHSCORE
03493Ada3AMrs Au2PhysicsMr Poon0
03496Clem3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho78
03496Clem3BMr Bao2PhysicsMr Poon98
03496Clem3BMr Bao3ICTMr Suen89
03505Eva3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho83
...
Clem 有 3 条记录，“3B, Mr Bao” 存了 3 次；ICT 有 3 条，“Mr Suen” 存了 3 次。

空间够时浪费不致命，真正的问题是冗余会引起三种 anomalies（异常）：update、insertion、deletion，令数据不一致或丢失。

ex.q: In the table above, how many times is the class teacher of 3B stored if 3B has Clem (3 subjects), Eva (1 subject) and Finn (1 subject)?
ex.a: One record per student-subject pair: Clem 3 + Eva 1 + Finn 1 = 5 times. Only 1 is needed in a well-designed database (one row in a class table).
ex.az: 3+1+1 = 5 次；好的设计只需存 1 次。

cards.en:
An update anomaly occurs when a database with data redundancy fails to maintain data consistency after an update is made.

Because the same fact is stored in many records, one change in the real world needs many records to be updated. If only some are updated, the database contains contradicting values (data inconsistency).

Examples with the redundant STUDENT table:
• Clem moves from 3B to 3A → 3 records must change. If only one changes, Clem is in both 3A and 3B.
• The ICT teacher changes from Mr Suen to Mrs Lee → 3 records must change.

Test: does one real-world change require updating more than one record holding duplicated data? If yes, an update anomaly may occur. Changing a value that is stored only once (e.g. one student's score in one subject) causes no anomaly.
cards.zh:
An update anomaly occurs when a database with data redundancy fails to maintain data consistency after an update is made.

同一事实存在多条记录，现实中一个改变就要改很多条；只改一部分，数据库就出现互相矛盾的值（data inconsistency）。

例（冗余的 STUDENT 表）：
• Clem 由 3B 转 3A → 要改 3 条，只改一条就同时在 3A 和 3B；
• ICT 老师由 Mr Suen 换成 Mrs Lee → 要改 3 条。

判断：一个现实改变是否要改多于一条重复记录？是 → 可能 update anomaly。只存一次的值（如某生某科分数）改了没有异常。

ex.q: PROD(PID, PNAME, SID, PRICE, SNAME, SKNAME), PK = PID+SID. HomeZone sells 4 products. Its shopkeeper changes, and only one record is updated. Any anomaly?
ex.a:
Yes, update anomaly. The shopkeeper name is repeated in all 4 HomeZone records; after updating one, the other 3 still show the old name, so the data is inconsistent.
-- correct but must touch 4 rows:
UPDATE PROD SET SKNAME = 'Abby' WHERE SID = 1;
ex.az: 店主名重复 4 次，只改 1 条 → 不一致 → update anomaly。（课本 Checkpoint 5.5(a)）

cards.en:
An insertion anomaly is the inability to insert data of one entity type without having the data of another entity type.

Cause: data of two entity types are mixed in one table, and the primary key includes fields from both. A primary key field cannot be NULL.

Examples with STUDENT (PK = SID+EID):
• A new student Dio has not chosen any elective yet. EID would be NULL, but EID is part of the primary key → cannot insert Dio.
• A new subject Art has no students yet. SID would be NULL → cannot insert Art.

Retail example: a new product not yet sold by any shop, or a new shop that sells no products yet, cannot be added to PROD (PK = PID+SID).
cards.zh:
An insertion anomaly is the inability to insert data of one entity type without having the data of another entity type.

原因：两种实体的数据混在一个表，primary key 由两边字段组成，而主键字段不能 NULL。

例（STUDENT，PK = SID+EID）：
• 新生 Dio 未选科 → EID 只能 NULL，但 EID 是主键一部分 → 无法插入；
• 新科 Art 没人选 → SID 为 NULL → 无法插入。

零售例：未有店卖的新产品，或未卖任何产品的新店，都不能加进 PROD（PK = PID+SID）。

ex.q: Show in SQL why the new student Dio cannot be inserted into STUDENT whose primary key is (SID, EID).
ex.a:
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
VALUES ('03520', 'Dio', '3A', 'Mrs Au');
EID is left NULL. Since EID is part of the primary key, the DBMS rejects the row (in MySQL a PK column is NOT NULL). This is an insertion anomaly.
ex.az: EID 为 NULL 违反主键 → 插不进 → insertion anomaly。

cards.en:
A deletion anomaly is the loss of data of one entity type when deleting the data of another entity type.

Because one record holds data about two entity types, deleting it to remove one fact also removes the other fact, if that record was the only place it was stored.

Examples with STUDENT:
• Ada, the only student of 3A, leaves the school → the class teacher of 3A (Mrs Au) is lost.
• Clem and Eva drop History → History's teacher (Ms Ho) is lost.
• Eva takes only History; when she drops it, her own name and class are lost too.

Retail: removing Smartphone, the only product of FastTech, loses all data about the shop FastTech.
cards.zh:
A deletion anomaly is the loss of data of one entity type when deleting the data of another entity type.

一条记录同时存两种实体资料；为删除一件事而删掉它，若它是另一件事唯一的存放处，那资料也一起消失。

例：
• 3A 唯一学生 Ada 退学 → 3A 班主任 Mrs Au 的资料丢失；
• Clem、Eva 退出 History → History 老师 Ms Ho 资料丢失；
• Eva 只读 History，退出后连她的姓名、班别也丢失。

零售例：删除 FastTech 唯一的产品 Smartphone → FastTech 店资料全失。

ex.q: In PROD, which product's removal causes the loss of a shop's data? Name the anomaly.
ex.a:
FastTech (SID 3) appears only in the Smartphone record. 
DELETE FROM PROD WHERE PID = 4;
removes the only record containing FastTech's name, address and shopkeeper → deletion anomaly.
ex.az: Smartphone 是 FastTech 唯一记录，删了店资料就没有 → deletion anomaly。（课本 Checkpoint 5.5(c)）

cards.en:
Students often mix up the three anomalies. Ask what the action is and what goes wrong:
ActionWhat goes wrongAnomaly
Change a fact stored in many recordssome copies not changed → inconsistentUpdate
Add data of one entity alonePK part would be NULL → rejectedInsertion
Remove a recordother entity's only copy disappearsDeletion
Traps:
• Changing a value stored in only one record (e.g. the price of one product in one shop, PK = PID+SID) causes no anomaly.
• "Adam no longer owns GG Garden" (he is its only owner): we must delete the ownership record, and the property's data disappears → deletion, not update anomaly.
• "Gabe changes his name" when Gabe has two records → update anomaly.
cards.zh:
三种异常容易混。先看动作，再看出什么问题：
动作问题异常
改一个存在多条记录的事实部分没改 → 不一致Update
单独加入一种实体的数据主键部分为 NULL → 被拒Insertion
删除记录另一实体唯一的副本消失Deletion
陷阱：
• 改只存一次的值（某店某产品价格，PK = PID+SID）→ 没有异常；
• “Adam 不再拥有 GG Garden”（唯一业主）→ 要删除记录，物业资料消失 → 是 deletion，不是 update；
• Gabe 有两条记录时改名 → update。

ex.q: PROD (PK = PID+SID): the price of the board game at HappyToy changes from $156 to $140 and one record is updated. Any anomaly?
ex.a: No. The price of that product at that shop depends on the whole key PID+SID and is stored in exactly one record, so updating one record keeps the data consistent.
ex.az: 该价格只存一次 → 改一条即可 → 没有异常。（课本 Checkpoint 5.5(b)）

cards.en:
Normalisation is designing a database in a particular way that:
• reduces data redundancy;
• prevents occurrences of anomalies; and
• improves flexibility.

The usual levels are First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF) and Third Normal Form (3NF). Each level includes all the rules of the level before it: a 3NF table is also in 2NF and 1NF.

In practice, normalising means splitting a big table into smaller related tables linked by foreign keys, so that each fact is stored once. The cost is that queries need more joins.
cards.zh:
Normalisation（规范化）：以特定方式设计数据库，以便：
• reduces data redundancy（减少冗余）；
• prevents occurrences of anomalies（防止异常）；
• improves flexibility（提高灵活性）。

常见级别：1NF、2NF、3NF，每级包含上一级所有规则：3NF 的表也一定是 2NF 和 1NF。

实际做法：把大表拆成多个相关的小表，用外键连接，每个事实只存一次。代价是查询要多做 join。

ex.q: State three purposes of normalisation.
ex.a:
1. To reduce data redundancy (save storage).
2. To prevent update, insertion and deletion anomalies.
3. To improve flexibility, e.g. a city can have any number of landmarks without changing the table structure.
ex.az: 减冗余、防异常、提高灵活性。

cards.en:
Rules of 1NF:
1. Every attribute must not contain multiple values.
2. There must not be any repeating attributes.

Multiple values: one cell holds a list, e.g. ENAME = 'History,Physics,ICT' or AWARD = 'Best Actress (IFCS), Best Actress (OFCS)'.
Repeating attributes: a group of fields storing the same kind of data, e.g. ENAME1, ENAME2, ENAME3; LM1, LM2, LM3; ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3; or one Boolean field per subject. Each cell holds one value, but the table is still not in 1NF.

Methods 1, 2 and 3 of Activity 5.1 all violate 1NF, which leads to inflexibility (fixed maximum number, new fields needed) and difficult queries (string search, OR across many fields).
cards.zh:
1NF 规则：
1. Every attribute must not contain multiple values.（一格不能多值）
2. There must not be any repeating attributes.（不能有重复属性）

Multiple values：一格存列表，如 ENAME = 'History,Physics,ICT'，AWARD 存两个奖。
Repeating attributes：一组字段存同类数据，如 ENAME1/2/3、LM1/2/3、ELEC1/2/3、每科一个 Boolean 字段。每格虽是单值，仍然不是 1NF。

Activity 5.1 方法 1、2、3 都违反 1NF，导致不灵活（上限固定、要加字段）和查询困难（字符串搜索、多字段 OR）。

ex.q: CITY(CTID, CTNAME, TIMEZONE, AREA, POPULATION, LM1, LM2, LM3, CC, CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT). Is it in 1NF?
ex.a: No. LM1, LM2 and LM3 are repeating attributes, so the table is not in 1NF. (A city with a 4th landmark would need a new field.)
ex.az: LM1/LM2/LM3 是重复属性 → 不是 1NF。（课本 Checkpoint 5.6(a)）

cards.en:
To convert a table into 1NF:
• For multiple values: split them so that each value is in a separate record. Clem with 'History,Physics,ICT' becomes 3 records. The new primary key is the old key plus that attribute, e.g. SID+ENAME (or SID+EID).
• For repeating attributes: either turn each into a separate record in the same way, or move them into a new table with a foreign key, e.g. LANDMARK(LMID, LMNAME, CTID) where CTID references CITY.

Counting records: new count = old count + extra values. In Example 5.5, ACTOR has 7 records and two of them hold 2 awards each, so after 1NF there are 7 + 2 = 9 records.

The new LANDMARK table is more flexible: a city can have more than 3 landmarks without changing the structure.
cards.zh:
转 1NF：
• 多值：拆开，每个值一条记录。Clem 的 'History,Physics,ICT' 变 3 条。新主键 = 原主键 + 该属性，如 SID+ENAME。
• 重复属性：同样拆成多条记录，或移到新表并加外键，如 LANDMARK(LMID, LMNAME, CTID)，CTID 参照 CITY。

数记录：新数目 = 原数目 + 多出的值。Example 5.5：ACTOR 7 条，其中两条各有 2 个奖 → 7 + 2 = 9 条。

新的 LANDMARK 表更灵活：城市可多于 3 个地标而不用改结构。

ex.q: A table has 5 records; their HOBBY cells contain 1, 3, 2, 1 and 4 values. How many records after 1NF? What is the new key if the old key is SID?
ex.a: One record per value: 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 4 = 11 records. New primary key: SID + HOBBY.
ex.az: 每个值一条：共 11 条；主键 SID+HOBBY。

cards.en:
A functional dependency exists between two sets of attributes when the values of one set can be uniquely determined by the values of another set.

Notation: X → Y, read "X determines Y" or "Y depends on X".

Examples in STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH, EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE):
• CLASS → CTEACH: knowing the class tells us the class teacher (but not the student's name).
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS}
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}
• {SID, EID} → SCORE: a score needs both the student and the subject.

Functional dependencies come from the meaning of the data (business rules), not just from a few sample rows. Finding them is the first step of 2NF and 3NF.
cards.zh:
A functional dependency exists between two sets of attributes when the values of one set can be uniquely determined by the values of another set.

记法：X → Y，“X 决定 Y”/“Y 依赖 X”。

例：
• CLASS → CTEACH：知道班就知道班主任（但不知学生名）；
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS}；
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}；
• {SID, EID} → SCORE：分数要同时知道学生和科目。

功能相关由数据的意义（业务规则）决定，不只是看几行样本。找出它们是做 2NF、3NF 的第一步。

ex.q: RECORD(PID, PNAME, SEX, AGE, DID, DNAME, DOA, DIAG) of a clinic. Which attribute does SEX depend on? Which does DNAME depend on?
ex.a:
PID → SEX (SEX depends on the patient ID).
DID → DNAME (DNAME depends on the doctor ID).
ex.az: SEX 依赖 PID；DNAME 依赖 DID。（课本 Chapter Exercise Q1(b)）

cards.en:
Full functional dependency: when all attributes that are not primary key are dependent on the primary key (the whole key). Example: ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH) with EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}.

Partial functional dependency: when some non-primary key attributes are dependent on part of the primary key.
Example: STUDENT with PK = SID+EID:
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH} (part of key)
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH} (part of key)
• only {SID, EID} → SCORE uses the whole key.

Key point: a partial functional dependency can exist only when the primary key is a composite key. A 1NF table whose primary key is a single field is automatically in 2NF.
cards.zh:
Full functional dependency（完全功能相关）：all attributes that are not primary key are dependent on the primary key（整个主键）。例：ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)，EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}。

Partial functional dependency（部分功能相关）：some non-primary key attributes are dependent on part of the primary key。
例：STUDENT 主键 SID+EID：
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH}（只靠部分主键）
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}
• 只有 {SID, EID} → SCORE 用整个主键。

重点：partial FD 只会在主键是 composite key 时出现。单字段主键的 1NF 表自动是 2NF。

ex.q: QUESTION(YEAR, QUESTION, MARK, TCODE, TOTALMARK), PK = YEAR+QUESTION. Find a partial dependency.
ex.a: YEAR → TOTALMARK: the total mark of a paper depends only on the year, which is part of the key. So the table has a partial functional dependency and is not in 2NF.
ex.az: TOTALMARK 只依赖 YEAR（主键一部分）→ 部分相关 → 不是 2NF。（课本 Chapter Exercise Q3(c)）

cards.en:
Rules of 2NF:
1. It follows all the rules of 1NF.
2. There must NOT be any partial functional dependency.

In other words, every non-primary key attribute must depend on the whole primary key.

How to normalise to 2NF: write down the functional dependencies and make one table per determinant:
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH} → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH} → ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)
• {SID, EID} → SCORE → ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE)

Activity 5.2 result: after the split, cancelling ICT causes no deletion anomaly, Gabe's new name is changed in one record, and a new student can be inserted directly. We prefer 2NF to reduce data redundancy and anomalies.
cards.zh:
2NF 规则：
1. 符合 1NF 所有规则；
2. There must NOT be any partial functional dependency.

即每个非主键属性都依赖整个主键。

转 2NF：写出所有功能相关，每个决定因素一个表：
• SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH} → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
• EID → {ENAME, ETEACH} → ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)
• {SID, EID} → SCORE → ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE)

Activity 5.2：拆表后取消 ICT 不会 deletion anomaly；Gabe 改名只改一条；新生可直接插入。偏好 2NF 是为了 reduce data redundancy and anomalies。

ex.q: After the 2NF split, write SQL to rebuild the list 'student name, subject name, score'.
ex.a:
SELECT s.SNAME, e.ENAME, en.SCORE
FROM STUDENT s, ENROL en, ELECTIVE e
WHERE s.SID = en.SID AND en.EID = e.EID;
The data is still all there; it is just joined back when needed.
ex.az: 拆表不会丢数据，查询时 join 回来即可。

cards.en:
Transitive functional dependency: when some non-primary key attributes are dependent on other non-primary key attributes.

Example: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
• SID → CLASS
• CLASS → CTEACH
• therefore SID → CTEACH

CTEACH still depends on SID, but only through CLASS, a non-key attribute ("I know a guy who knows a guy"). This causes redundancy: the class teacher is repeated for every student in the class, and changing a class teacher needs many updates.

Other examples: FID → GENRE → GDESC; CTID → CC → {CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT}; CID → FID → FNAME (course → faculty → faculty name).
cards.zh:
Transitive functional dependency（传递功能相关）：some non-primary key attributes are dependent on other non-primary key attributes。

例：STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
• SID → CLASS
• CLASS → CTEACH
• 所以 SID → CTEACH

CTEACH 虽依赖 SID，但其实是经由非主键 CLASS（“我认识一个认识他的人”）。后果：班主任对班中每个学生都重复，换班主任要改很多条。

其他例：FID → GENRE → GDESC；CTID → CC → {CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT}。

ex.q: BOOK(ISBN, TITLE, PID, PNAME) where PID is the publisher ID. Identify the transitive dependency.
ex.a: ISBN → PID and PID → PNAME, so ISBN → PNAME is transitive: PNAME depends on PID, a non-key attribute. BOOK is not in 3NF.
ex.az: PNAME 依赖非主键 PID → 传递相关。

cards.en:
Rules of 3NF:
1. It follows all the rules of 2NF.
2. There must NOT be any transitive functional dependency.

So every non-primary key attribute depends on the primary key and only the primary key; there is no functional dependency between non-key attributes.

How to normalise to 3NF: move the transitively dependent attributes into a new table whose key is the middle attribute, and keep that attribute as a foreign key:
STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH) → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS) + CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH), where STUDENT.CLASS references CLASSLIST.

Benefit: a change of class teacher updates one record in CLASSLIST, avoiding update anomalies.
City example: CITY(CTID, CTNAME, TIMEZONE, AREA, POPULATION, CC) + COUNTRY(CC, CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT).
cards.zh:
3NF 规则：
1. 符合 2NF 所有规则；
2. There must NOT be any transitive functional dependency.

即每个非主键属性依赖 the primary key and only the primary key，非主键之间没有功能相关。

转 3NF：把传递依赖的属性搬到新表，以中间那个属性为主键，并在原表保留它作外键：
STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH) → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS) + CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH)，STUDENT.CLASS 参照 CLASSLIST。

好处：换班主任只改 CLASSLIST 一条，避免 update anomaly。
城市例：CITY(CTID, CTNAME, TIMEZONE, AREA, POPULATION, CC) + COUNTRY(CC, CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT)。

ex.q: Normalise RECORD(PID, PNAME, SEX, AGE, DID, DNAME, DOA, DIAG) of a clinic into 3NF. Assume a patient sees a doctor at most once a day, so PID+DID+DOA identifies a visit.
ex.a:
Dependencies: PID → {PNAME, SEX, AGE}, DID → DNAME, {PID, DID, DOA} → DIAG.
PATIENT(PID, PNAME, SEX, AGE)
DOCTOR(DID, DNAME)
APPOINTMENT(PID, DID, DOA, DIAG), where PID references PATIENT and DID references DOCTOR.
ex.az: 病人、医生分表，诊症表以 PID+DID+DOA 为主键并含两个外键。（参考课本 Chapter Exercise Q1(c)）

cards.en:
Rule1NF2NF3NF
No multiple values for an attribute✓✓✓
No repeating attributes✓✓✓
No partial functional dependency✓✓
No transitive functional dependency✓
Partial FD: a non-key attribute depends on part of the primary key.
Transitive FD: a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute.

Exam method to find the level: check 1NF (any lists? any ELEC1/ELEC2?), then check 2NF only if the key is composite, then check 3NF by asking whether any non-key determines another non-key. Always name the specific attributes in your explanation.
cards.zh:
规则1NF2NF3NF
一格不多值✓✓✓
无重复属性✓✓✓
无部分功能相关✓✓
无传递功能相关✓
Partial FD：非主键依赖部分主键。
Transitive FD：非主键依赖另一个非主键。

判断级别：先查 1NF（有列表？有 ELEC1/ELEC2？），主键是复合键才需查 2NF，再问有没有非主键决定另一非主键（3NF）。解释时要点名具体属性。

ex.q: ENROL(SID, CID1, CID2, CID3), where each student takes 0–3 courses. Daniel says it is in 3NF because there is no transitive dependency. Why is he wrong?
ex.a: CID1, CID2 and CID3 are repeating attributes, so ENROL is not even in 1NF. Since 3NF must satisfy all rules of 1NF and 2NF, it cannot be in 3NF. Fix: ENROL(SID, CID) with one record per enrolment.
ex.az: 有重复属性，连 1NF 都不是；3NF 要包含 1NF 规则。（课本 Chapter Exercise Q2(b)）

cards.en:
ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB, FID, FNAME, RNAME, FYEAR, GENRE, AWARD), primary key ID+FID, 7 records.

(a) 1NF? No: AWARD stores multiple values in one record (Maya and Ted each have 2 awards). Split each award into its own record: 7 + 2 = 9 records.

(b) 2NF? Dependencies:
ID → {NAME, SEX, DOB}
FID → {FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE}
{ID, FID} → {RNAME, AWARD}
NAME, SEX depend on ID only (part of the key) → partial dependency → not 2NF.

(c) 3NF: three entity types Actor, Film, Role:
ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB)
FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE)
ROLE(ID, FID, RNAME, AWARD)
No partial or transitive dependency remains.

(d) Adding GDESC (genre description) to FILM gives FID → GENRE → GDESC, a transitive dependency, so FILM is no longer in 3NF. Fix: GENRE(GENRE, GDESC).
(After 1NF, strictly ROLE's key would include AWARD; the book's answer keeps ID+FID.)
cards.zh:
ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB, FID, FNAME, RNAME, FYEAR, GENRE, AWARD)，主键 ID+FID，7 条记录。

(a) 1NF? 否：AWARD 一格多值（Maya、Ted 各 2 个奖）。每个奖一条：7 + 2 = 9 条。

(b) 2NF? 功能相关：ID → {NAME, SEX, DOB}；FID → {FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE}；{ID, FID} → {RNAME, AWARD}。NAME、SEX 只依赖 ID（部分主键）→ 部分相关 → 非 2NF。

(c) 3NF：三个实体 Actor、Film、Role：
ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB)
FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE)
ROLE(ID, FID, RNAME, AWARD)

(d) 在 FILM 加 GDESC → FID → GENRE → GDESC 传递相关 → FILM 不再是 3NF；应另建 GENRE(GENRE, GDESC)。

ex.q: Write SQL that creates the 3NF table ROLE from the example with the correct keys.
ex.a:
CREATE TABLE ROLE (
  ID INT,
  FID INT,
  RNAME VARCHAR(20),
  AWARD VARCHAR(40),
  PRIMARY KEY (ID, FID),
  FOREIGN KEY (ID) REFERENCES ACTOR(ID),
  FOREIGN KEY (FID) REFERENCES FILM(FID)
);
ex.az: ROLE 复合主键 ID+FID，两个外键。（课本 Example 5.5）

cards.en:
Sometimes redundancy is not a sign of bad design but an intentional way to improve the performance of data retrieval. This is denormalisation: combining normalised tables back into fewer (or one) tables.

Why: after normalising, listing all student data needs a join of 4 tables (STUDENT, CLASSLIST, ENROL, ELECTIVE). With many records, joins are slow.

When it is suitable: the data is rarely updated and is mainly read (e.g. a reporting or archive table, a website's product catalogue snapshot). Then the anomalies caused by redundancy hardly matter, while every query becomes faster and simpler.

Lab 5.1 creates a denormalised table STUDENTDE that stores the joined result, so later queries are just SELECT * FROM STUDENTDE.
cards.zh:
有时冗余不是坏设计，而是 intentional way to improve the performance of data retrieval，这就是 denormalisation（非规范化）：把规范化后的表合回较少（或一个）表。

原因：规范化后列出全部学生资料要 join 4 个表（STUDENT, CLASSLIST, ENROL, ELECTIVE），记录多时很慢。

适用：数据很少更新、主要是读取（报表、存档、产品目录快照）。这时冗余带来的异常影响不大，查询却更快更简单。

Lab 5.1 建立非规范化表 STUDENTDE 存 join 的结果，以后只需 SELECT * FROM STUDENTDE。

ex.q: A school publishes last year's exam results online; the data will never change. Normalised design or denormalised table? Why?
ex.a: Denormalised. The data is read many times and never updated, so update/insertion/deletion anomalies are not a concern. One pre-joined table gives faster retrieval and simpler SQL for the web page.
ex.az: 只读不改 → 非规范化，查询更快、SQL 更简单。

cards.en:
Lab 5.1 builds one table from the four 3NF tables.
CREATE TABLE STUDENTDE (
  SID CHAR(5), SNAME VARCHAR(20), CLASS CHAR(2),
  CTEACH VARCHAR(20), EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(20),
  ETEACH VARCHAR(20), SCORE INT );

INSERT INTO STUDENTDE (
  SELECT s.SID, SNAME, c.CLASS, CTEACH, e.EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE
  FROM STUDENT s, CLASSLIST c, ENROL en, ELECTIVE e
  WHERE s.SID = en.SID AND en.EID = e.EID AND s.CLASS = c.CLASS );

SELECT * FROM STUDENTDE;
Points:
• INSERT INTO table SELECT ... copies the result of a query into a table.
• The WHERE clause holds one join condition per pair of linked tables (4 tables → 3 conditions).
• Ambiguous fields (SID, CLASS, EID) must be prefixed with an alias.
• In SQLite, write the SELECT without brackets: INSERT INTO STUDENTDE SELECT .... Another shortcut is CREATE TABLE STUDENTDE AS SELECT ....
cards.zh:
Lab 5.1 把四个 3NF 表合成一个表（代码同英文版）。
要点：
• INSERT INTO 表 SELECT ... 把查询结果复制进表；
• WHERE 里每对相连的表一个 join 条件（4 表 → 3 个条件）；
• 有歧义的字段（SID, CLASS, EID）要加别名前缀；
• SQLite 里 SELECT 不要加括号：INSERT INTO STUDENTDE SELECT ...；亦可 CREATE TABLE STUDENTDE AS SELECT ...。
INSERT INTO STUDENTDE
SELECT s.SID, SNAME, c.CLASS, CTEACH,
       e.EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE
FROM STUDENT s, CLASSLIST c, ENROL en, ELECTIVE e
WHERE s.SID = en.SID AND en.EID = e.EID
  AND s.CLASS = c.CLASS;

ex.q: After Lab 5.1, write a query on STUDENTDE that lists the names of students taught by Mr Suen, and the same query on the 3NF tables.
ex.a:
Denormalised:
SELECT SNAME FROM STUDENTDE WHERE ETEACH = 'Mr Suen';
Normalised:
SELECT s.SNAME
FROM STUDENT s, ENROL en, ELECTIVE e
WHERE s.SID = en.SID AND en.EID = e.EID
  AND e.ETEACH = 'Mr Suen';
The denormalised query is shorter and needs no join: this is the advantage of denormalisation.
ex.az: 非规范化查询更短、不用 join。

cards.en:
DenormalisationNormalisation
Retrieval speedFaster data retrieval (fewer joins)slower (many joins)
SQLSimpler SQL statements for querieslonger queries
Storagemore storage space requiredless storage
Flexibilitylower flexibility of data managementhigher flexibility
Updatinghigher risk of data inconsistency (update anomaly)no update anomaly
Insertingcannot insert data without data of another entity type (insertion anomaly)no insertion anomaly
Deletinghigher risk of data loss (deletion anomaly)no deletion anomaly
Exam tip: when asked for "one advantage of the original (unnormalised) database", answer faster data retrieval or simpler SQL statements for queries.
cards.zh:
非规范化规范化
查询速度Faster data retrieval（少 join）较慢
SQLSimpler SQL statements较长
空间more storage space required较少
灵活性lower flexibility较高
更新易不一致（update anomaly）无
插入没有另一实体资料就插不进（insertion anomaly）无
删除易丢资料（deletion anomaly）无
考试技巧：问“原本未规范化数据库的一个优点”→ 答 faster data retrieval 或 simpler SQL statements for queries。

ex.q: CITY was normalised into CITY, COUNTRY and LANDMARK. State one advantage of the original single table.
ex.a: Faster data retrieval: listing a city with its country name and head of state needs no join. (Or: simpler SQL statements for queries.)
ex.az: 原表查询快／SQL 简单。（课本 Checkpoint 5.6(f)）

cards.en:
Data privacy concerns the collection, storage and management of personal data, such as residential addresses, personal photos, ID card numbers and even bank account passwords.

When handling personal data, we should:
• use the data for its original purposes only; and
• not disclose the data to unauthorised people.

Violations:
• A doctor uses students' medical examination data for targeted advertising of medical services → not the original purpose.
• A game show website shows the HKID numbers of teammates to a participant → disclosed to unauthorised people.

Database designers protect privacy with access rights and views, and by not showing or exporting fields that are not needed (e.g. HKID, name, email when doing statistics).
cards.zh:
Data privacy（数据私隐）：关乎个人资料的收集、储存与管理，如住址、个人照片、身份证号码、银行密码。

处理个人资料时应：
• use the data for its original purposes only（只用于原来目的）；
• not disclose the data to unauthorised people（不向未获授权者披露）。

违反例子：
• 医生用学生体检数据做医疗服务的定向广告 → 不是原来目的；
• 游戏节目网站向参加者显示队友的 HKID → 泄露给未授权者。

数据库用 access rights 和 views 保护私隐，并且不显示、不导出不需要的字段（统计时去掉 HKID、姓名、电邮）。

ex.q: A gym collects members' phone numbers for booking reminders, then sells the list to an insurance company. Which principle is broken?
ex.a: Both: the data is not used for its original purpose (booking reminders), and it is disclosed to unauthorised people (the insurance company). This violates data privacy.
ex.az: 用作别的用途 + 泄露给未授权者 → 违反数据私隐。

cards.en:
Access rights are the permissions granted to a user to perform certain operations on specific data, such as retrieve, create, update and delete.

Different roles get different rights. Streaming platform table ACCOUNT(AID, USERNAME, SEX, PHONE, EMAIL, ATYPE, ENDOFSUB):
RoleAccess rightSQL
Database schema designcreate and delete tables; alter table structuresCREATE, DROP; ALTER, ADD, MODIFY
Account managementcreate, update, delete accounts; view any accountINSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; SELECT
Sales managementupdate ATYPE and ENDOFSUB of any account; view any accountUPDATE; SELECT
Customerupdate PHONE and EMAIL of own account; view own accountUPDATE; SELECT
To protect data privacy, each customer cannot access the personal data of any other customer.
cards.zh:
Access rights（用户存取权限）are the permissions granted to a user to perform certain operations on specific data, such as retrieve, create, update and delete.

不同角色不同权限。串流平台 ACCOUNT 表：
角色权限SQL
Database schema design建/删表；改结构CREATE, DROP; ALTER, ADD, MODIFY
Account management建/改/删账户；看全部INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; SELECT
Sales management改任何账户的 ATYPE、ENDOFSUB；看全部UPDATE; SELECT
Customer只改自己的 PHONE、EMAIL；只看自己UPDATE; SELECT
为保护私隐，顾客不能存取其他顾客的个人资料。

ex.q: A customer wants to change their email. Write the SQL the system runs for customer AID 1023, and explain how the right is limited.
ex.a:
UPDATE ACCOUNT SET EMAIL = 'tom.ho@mail.com'
WHERE AID = 1023;
The customer has UPDATE right only on PHONE and EMAIL, and only for the row of their own account (AID of the signed-in user); they cannot change ATYPE or other people's rows.
ex.az: 顾客只可改自己那一行的 PHONE、EMAIL。

cards.t: Choosing access rights for a role
cards.en:
Match each task to the SQL commands it needs, then grant only those (least privilege):
• CREATE, ALTER, DROP → database design (table structures).
• INSERT, DELETE → record management (adding/removing records).
• UPDATE → changing existing records.
• SELECT → searching, viewing and exporting data.

Book examples:
• A game show participant may edit their own personal data → UPDATE (on their own record only).
• A researcher may search for and export STUDENT data → SELECT only.

Granting more than needed (e.g. DELETE to a researcher) increases the risk of data loss and of privacy leaks.

In MySQL this is done with GRANT SELECT ON STUDENT TO 'researcher'@'%'; (SQLite has no user accounts or GRANT).
cards.zh:
把每项工作对应所需 SQL 指令，只给这些（最少权限）：
• CREATE, ALTER, DROP → 数据库设计（表结构）；
• INSERT, DELETE → 记录管理（加/删记录）；
• UPDATE → 修改现有记录；
• SELECT → 搜索、查看、导出。

课本例子：
• 参加者可修改自己资料 → UPDATE（只限自己记录）；
• 研究员搜索及导出 STUDENT 数据 → 只给 SELECT。

给多了（如研究员有 DELETE）会增加丢资料和泄露风险。

MySQL 用 GRANT SELECT ON STUDENT TO 'researcher'@'%';（SQLite 没有用户与 GRANT）。

ex.q: A school clerk must add new students and remove students who leave, and look up records, but must not change table structures. Which rights?
ex.a: INSERT (add new students), DELETE (remove leavers) and SELECT (look up). Not CREATE, ALTER or DROP.
ex.az: INSERT + DELETE + SELECT，不给 CREATE/ALTER/DROP。

cards.en:
Setting views can protect data privacy by limiting the access of certain data for specific users. A view is a saved query that behaves like a virtual table. A user given access to the view sees only its rows and columns.

Limit rows with WHERE, limit columns with the field list:
CREATE VIEW AFILM AS
  (SELECT * FROM ACCOUNT WHERE ATYPE IN (0, 1));

CREATE VIEW HOSTVIEW AS
  (SELECT TNUM, PNUM, PNAME, SEX, PHONE FROM P);

CREATE VIEW ANALYSIS AS
  (SELECT SEX, AGE, WEIGHT, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT);
• AFILM: an officer handling film streaming sees only accounts with ATYPE 0 or 1.
• HOSTVIEW: the host sees team number, participant number, name, sex and phone, but no HKID, DOB or address.
• ANALYSIS: for research, identifying fields (SID, SNAME, EMAIL) are removed.

Use the view like a table: SELECT AVG(HEIGHT) FROM ANALYSIS WHERE SEX = 'F';. In SQLite, omit the brackets: CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT ....
cards.zh:
Setting views can protect data privacy by limiting the access of certain data for specific users. View（视图）是一个保存起来的查询，像虚拟表；获准用视图的人只看到其中的行与列。

用 WHERE 限行，用字段列表限列（代码同英文版）。
• AFILM：负责电影串流的职员只看 ATYPE 0、1 的账户；
• HOSTVIEW：主持人只看队号、参加者号码、姓名、性别、电话，看不到 HKID、出生日期、地址；
• ANALYSIS：做研究时去掉 SID、SNAME、EMAIL 等可识别身份的字段。

视图当表用：SELECT AVG(HEIGHT) FROM ANALYSIS WHERE SEX = 'F';。SQLite 不加括号：CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT ...。

ex.q: Students agreed to let their medical data be used to study growth. Write the view and a query for the average height of females aged 11 to 14.
ex.a:
CREATE VIEW ANALYSIS AS
  SELECT SEX, AGE, WEIGHT, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT;

SELECT AVG(HEIGHT) FROM ANALYSIS
WHERE SEX = 'F' AND AGE BETWEEN 11 AND 14;
The view hides SID, SNAME and EMAIL, so researchers cannot identify any student.
ex.az: 视图只含分析所需字段；查询可直接用视图。（课本 Checkpoint 5.7(a)(c)）

cards.t: Example 5.6: subquery and privacy on a web page
cards.en:
Table P(PNUM, TNUM, PNAME, SEX, HKID, DOB, ADDRESS, PHONE) stores game show participants in teams. After Kara (participant 579) signs in, the page lists her teammates with name, HKID, sex and participant number.

(a) SQL: we know Kara's PNUM but not her team, so use a subquery:
SELECT PNAME, HKID, SEX, PNUM FROM P
WHERE TNUM = (SELECT TNUM FROM P WHERE PNUM = '579');
(b) Ethical issue: the HKID number is personal data. The page violates data privacy by showing the HKID numbers of other participants (disclosure to unauthorised people). Remove the HKID column.

(c) Access right: CREATE, ALTER, DROP are for design; INSERT, DELETE for record management. A participant who edits their own data needs UPDATE only.

(d) View for the host:
CREATE VIEW HOSTVIEW AS
  (SELECT TNUM, PNUM, PNAME, SEX, PHONE FROM P);
cards.zh:
P(PNUM, TNUM, PNAME, SEX, HKID, DOB, ADDRESS, PHONE) 存游戏节目参加者及队伍。Kara（579）登入后网页列出队友姓名、HKID、性别、编号。

(a) 只知 PNUM 不知队号 → 用子查询先找 TNUM（代码同英文版）。
(b) HKID 是个人资料，网页向其他参加者显示 HKID，违反 data privacy（泄露给未授权者），应删去该栏。
(c) CREATE/ALTER/DROP 属设计，INSERT/DELETE 属记录管理；参加者改自己资料只需 UPDATE。
(d) 为主持人建 HOSTVIEW，只含 TNUM, PNUM, PNAME, SEX, PHONE。

ex.q: Rewrite Kara's teammate query so that it respects data privacy and does not list Kara herself.
ex.a:
SELECT PNAME, SEX, PNUM FROM P
WHERE TNUM = (SELECT TNUM FROM P WHERE PNUM = '579')
  AND PNUM <> '579';
HKID is removed from the field list; PNUM <> '579' excludes Kara.
ex.az: 去掉 HKID；加 PNUM <> '579' 排除自己。

mc.q: In an ER diagram, which shape represents an entity type?
mc.e: Entity types are rectangles; relationships are diamonds; attributes are ellipses.

mc.q: In an ER diagram, a diamond represents
mc.e: Diamonds are relationships, usually named with a verb.

mc.q: How is the primary key shown in an ER diagram?
o: The rectangle has a double border
The attribute is written in red
mc.e: The key attribute is underlined. Colours have no meaning.
mc.ez: 主键属性加下划线；颜色无意义。

mc.q: Which statement about ER diagrams is correct?
o: A relationship can never have attributes
Foreign keys should be drawn as ellipses of the entity type
mc.e: A relationship may have its own attributes (e.g. Treatment date). Foreign keys are shown by relationships; each entity type (not attribute) becomes a table.
mc.ez: 关系可以有属性；外键用关系表示；实体才变成表。

mc.q: An ER diagram has rectangles Animal, Zone and Species, and diamonds Live in and Belong to. How many tables are needed (no M:N relationship)?
mc.e: One table per entity type: ANIMAL, ZONE, SPECIES.
mc.ez: 每个实体一个表，共 3 个。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.1 Q1(a) (p.248), adapted

mc.q: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID) where PID and MID are foreign keys. In the ER diagram, which ellipses should be attached to Letter?
o: Letter ID, Recipient address, PID, MID
mc.e: Foreign keys are represented by relationships, not attributes.
mc.ez: 外键不画成属性，只画 Letter ID、Recipient address。

mc.q: Which of the following is the best reason to draw an ER diagram before creating tables?
o: It helps decide the table structures
It removes the need for primary keys
mc.e: An ER diagram helps decide the table structures (entity types → tables, attributes → fields).
mc.ez: ER 图帮助决定表结构。

mc.q: Which is NOT a result of bad database design?
mc.e: Clear and concise tables are a feature of good design.
mc.ez: 清晰简洁的表是好设计的特征。

mc.q: A participation constraint specifies
o: the maximum number of related entities
whether each entity participates in a relationship or not
the data type of an attribute
which field is the primary key
mc.e: Participation = must or may take part. Maximum number is cardinality.
mc.ez: 参与限制 = 是否必须参与；最多多少是基数。

mc.q: In an ER diagram, a small circle on a relationship line means the side is
mc.e: Circle = optional; short bar = mandatory.
mc.ez: 圆圈 = 非强制；竖线 = 强制。

mc.q: Which sentence describes a mandatory side?
o: A citizen may or may not own a vehicle
A hotel room may be empty
Each vehicle must have a registration plate
An employee may have no tasks
mc.e: 'Must' means every entity takes part: mandatory.

mc.q: 'Every class must have a class teacher, but a teacher may not be a class teacher.' This is
mc.e: One side must take part (class), the other may not (teacher).
mc.ez: 一边必须、一边可不 → 强制+非强制。

mc.q: Citizen — Be infected with — Disease, where a citizen may have no disease and a disease may have no patients now. Both sides are
mc.e: Neither side is guaranteed to take part.
mc.ez: 两边都不保证参与 → 都 optional。

mc.q: A lab has 40 computers and 25 students. Each student uses exactly one computer. The computer side (does every computer have a student?) is
o: optional, because some computers are unused
mandatory, because each student uses one
mc.e: With 15 spare computers, not every computer participates: optional.
mc.ez: 有空闲电脑 → 电脑那边 optional。

mc.q: In a company each department has 10 to 50 employees and each employee belongs to one department. Which is correct?
o: Department side optional, employee side mandatory
mc.e: Every department has employees and every employee belongs to a department.
mc.ez: 部门一定有员工，员工一定属于部门 → 两边强制。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.2 Q1(a) (p.254), adapted

mc.q: Where is the participation symbol for 'each student must join a sports event' drawn in Student — Join — Sports event?
mc.e: The symbol describing each student is placed next to the far entity (Sports event).
mc.ez: 描述学生的符号画在对面实体 Sports event 旁。

mc.q: If a foreign key column in table X is defined NOT NULL, then for the relationship to the referenced table, the X side is
mc.e: Every X row must reference a row: X participates mandatorily.
mc.ez: 外键 NOT NULL → 每行必须有关联 → mandatory。

mc.q: Cardinality of a relationship specifies
o: how many entities can be related to entities of another entity type
mc.e: Cardinality = how many (1 or M).
mc.ez: 基数 = 可关联多少个。

mc.q: Mandatory participation together with cardinality 1 at one end means
mc.e: Minimum 1 and maximum 1 → exactly one.
mc.ez: 最少 1 最多 1 → 恰好一个。

mc.q: Optional participation with cardinality M at one end means
mc.e: Minimum 0, maximum many.

mc.q: Class 1 — Have — M Student. Where should the foreign key be stored?
o: CLASS stores a list of SIDs
A new table is always required
Both tables store each other's key
mc.e: In a 1:M relationship, the FK goes on the many side.

mc.q: Which pair is most likely many-to-many?
mc.e: A book may have many authors and an author many books.

mc.q: Which pair is one-to-one?
mc.e: Each school has one principal and each principal heads one school.

mc.q: A many-to-many relationship is usually resolved by
o: adding a foreign key to one table
adding an associative entity with two one-to-many relationships
mc.e: M:N → 1:M + M:1 with an associative table.

mc.q: The associative table ENROLMENT(SID, EID) resolving Student–Elective usually has primary key
mc.e: The composite key SID+EID prevents duplicate pairs.

mc.q: Student M — Borrow — N Book. Which attribute belongs to the relationship (associative entity)?
mc.e: The due date describes one borrowing; it needs both student and book.
mc.ez: 到期日属于借书这个关系。

mc.q: Store M — Sell — N Book. Stock and price differ between stores. Where should STOCK and PRICE be stored?
mc.e: They depend on both store and book, so they belong to the associative table.
mc.ez: 同时取决于店和书 → 放 SELL。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.4 Q3 (p.275), adapted

mc.q: STUDENT(SID, NAME, EIDLIST) stores '1,11,12'. Why does WHERE EIDLIST LIKE '%1%' fail to list only History (EID 1) students?
o: It only matches the first character
mc.e: '%1%' matches any string containing 1, including 11 and 12.

mc.q: Activity 5.1 Method 3 uses fields ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3. What is the main problem?
o: Repeating attributes: a student cannot take a 4th subject without changing the structure
mc.e: Repeating attributes fix a maximum and need new fields for more subjects.
mc.ez: 重复属性：多于 3 科要改结构。

mc.q: If we only need the principal's name, a school–principal 1:1 relationship can be stored as SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, PRINCIPAL). This trades
o: flexibility and detail for simplicity and performance
mc.e: Merging gives simplicity and speed but loses flexibility and detail.
mc.ez: 换来简单和效能，牺牲灵活性与细节。

mc.q: PRODUCTREVIEW(PRID, PID NOT NULL, RATING) where PID references PRODUCT. Which describes the relationship?
o: Each review is about exactly one product; a product may have zero or many reviews
Each product has exactly one review
A review may have no product
mc.e: FK NOT NULL → exactly one product per review; a PID can appear 0 or many times.
mc.ez: 外键 NOT NULL → 每条评论恰一产品；产品可零或多条评论。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.3 Q2 (p.268), adapted

mc.q:
Given 
CLASS(CID, ROOM): ('3A','401'),('3B','402')
STUDENT(SID, CID): (1,'3A'),(2,'3B'),(3,'3B'),(4,'3B')
What does SELECT CID, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 return?
mc.e: Only 3B has more than one student (3).
mc.ez: 只有 3B 多于 1 人，共 3 人。

mc.q: Each teacher may teach several elective subjects or none; each subject is taught by one or more teachers. The relationship is
mc.e: Both sides can be many.
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.3 Q1(a) (p.267), adapted

mc.q: Seen from Student, the relationship Class 1 — Have — M Student is
mc.e: From the student side it is many-to-one.

mc.q: Data redundancy means
o: duplicated data that occupies storage space unnecessarily
mc.e: Redundant data is duplicated and wastes storage.

mc.q: Clem moves from 3B to 3A, but only one of her three records is updated. This is
mc.e: Data becomes inconsistent after an update.
mc.ez: 更新后数据不一致 → update anomaly。

mc.q: In STUDENT with PK SID+EID, a new student who has not chosen any elective cannot be added. This is
mc.e: EID would be NULL in the primary key.
mc.ez: 主键 EID 不能 NULL → insertion anomaly。

mc.q: Ada is the only student of 3A. Deleting Ada also removes 3A's class teacher. This is
mc.e: Data of another entity is lost on deletion.
mc.ez: 删除导致另一实体资料丢失。

mc.q: PROD(PID, SID, PRICE, SNAME, SKNAME), PK = PID+SID. The price of one product at one shop changes and one record is updated. Is there an anomaly?
mc.e: That price is stored only once.
mc.ez: 该价格只存一次，没有异常。

mc.q: Adam, the only owner of GG Garden, sells it. Removing his ownership record loses all data about GG Garden. Which anomaly?
mc.e: Data is lost by deleting a record, so it is a deletion anomaly, not update.

mc.q: Which design problem most directly causes anomalies?
mc.e: Redundancy is the cause of update, insertion and deletion anomalies.

mc.q:
Given 
T(SID, SNAME, EID, ETEACH):
(1,'Ada',2,'Mr Poon'),(2,'Clem',1,'Ms Ho'),
(2,'Clem',3,'Mr Suen'),(3,'Eva',1,'Ms Ho')
After DELETE FROM T WHERE SID = 2, which teacher's data disappears completely?
mc.e: Mr Suen appeared only in Clem's record (EID 3). Ms Ho remains in Eva's record.
mc.ez: Mr Suen 只出现在 Clem 的记录。

mc.q: Which is NOT a purpose of normalisation?
mc.e: Normalised data often needs more joins, so queries may be slower.
mc.ez: 规范化后要多 join，查询未必更快。

mc.q: A field ENAME stores 'History,Physics,ICT'. The table violates
mc.e: Multiple values in an attribute break 1NF.

mc.q: CITY has fields LM1, LM2, LM3 (landmark names). The table
o: is in 1NF since each cell has one value
is not in 1NF because of repeating attributes
mc.e: Repeating attributes break 1NF.

mc.q: A table has 7 records. Two records each hold 2 values in AWARD; the rest hold 1. After converting to 1NF there are
mc.e: 7 + 2 extra values = 9.

mc.q: 'CLASS → CTEACH' means
o: the value of CLASS uniquely determines CTEACH
CLASS and CTEACH are the same
mc.e: X → Y: values of X uniquely determine Y.

mc.q: A partial functional dependency can exist only when
o: the table has no primary key
the primary key is a composite key
mc.e: Depending on part of a key needs a key with more than one field.
mc.ez: 只有复合主键才可能部分相关。

mc.q: STUDENT(SID, EID, SNAME, SCORE), PK = SID+EID, with SID → SNAME. The table is
o: not in 2NF due to partial dependency
mc.e: SNAME depends on SID only, part of the key.
mc.ez: SNAME 只依赖 SID → 部分相关。

mc.q: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH), PK = SID, with CLASS → CTEACH. The highest normal form is
mc.e: Single-field key → no partial dependency (2NF), but CLASS → CTEACH is transitive (not 3NF).
mc.ez: 单一主键 → 2NF；有传递相关 → 非 3NF。

mc.q: A transitive functional dependency is when
o: a non-key attribute depends on part of the primary key
a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute
mc.e: Non-key → non-key is transitive.
mc.ez: 非主键依赖另一非主键。

mc.q: 3NF requires
o: all 2NF rules and no transitive dependency
mc.e: 3NF = 2NF + no transitive dependency.

mc.q: FILM(FID, FNAME, GENRE) is in 3NF. Adding GDESC (description of the genre) makes it
o: not in 3NF, due to FID → GENRE → GDESC
not in 2NF, due to partial dependency
mc.e: GDESC depends on GENRE, a non-key attribute: transitive.
mc.ez: GDESC 依赖非主键 GENRE → 传递。

mc.q: Normalising STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH) to 3NF gives
o: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS) and CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH)
mc.e: Keep CLASS in STUDENT as a foreign key; move CTEACH to CLASSLIST.
mc.ez: STUDENT 保留 CLASS 作外键，CTEACH 移到 CLASSLIST。

mc.q: ENROL(SID, CID1, CID2, CID3). Someone claims it is in 3NF because there is no transitive dependency. The claim is wrong because
o: it has repeating attributes, so it is not in 1NF
mc.e: CID1–CID3 are repeating attributes; a non-1NF table cannot be 3NF.
mc.ez: 重复属性 → 非 1NF → 不可能 3NF。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Chapter Exercise Q2(b) (p.306), adapted

mc.q: Denormalisation is
o: an intentional way to improve the performance of data retrieval
mc.e: Redundancy is added on purpose to speed up reads.
mc.ez: 有意加冗余以加快读取。

mc.q: Which is an advantage of denormalisation?
mc.e: Fewer joins → simpler and faster queries.
mc.ez: 少 join → SQL 更简单。

mc.q: Which situation suits denormalisation best?
o: Last year's archived exam results that are only read
A booking system with frequent inserts
mc.e: Rarely updated, mainly read data.

mc.q: Given 3NF tables STUDENT(SID,SNAME,CLASS), CLASSLIST(CLASS,CTEACH), ENROL(SID,EID,SCORE), ELECTIVE(EID,ENAME,ETEACH), how many join conditions are needed in WHERE to combine all four?
mc.e: Four tables in a chain need three join conditions.
mc.ez: 4 个表需 3 个 join 条件。

mc.q:
Given
STUDENT: (1,'Ada','3A'),(2,'Clem','3B'),(3,'Eva','3B')
CLASSLIST: ('3A','Mrs Au'),('3B','Mr Bao')
ENROL(SID,EID,SCORE): (1,2,0),(2,1,78),(2,2,98),(3,1,83)
How many rows does SELECT * FROM STUDENT s, CLASSLIST c, ENROL e WHERE s.CLASS=c.CLASS AND s.SID=e.SID AND c.CTEACH='Mr Bao' return?
mc.e: Mr Bao's class 3B: Clem has 2 enrolments, Eva 1 → 3 rows.

mc.q: Which SQLite statement copies a query result into an existing table STUDENTDE?
o: INSERT INTO STUDENTDE VALUES (SELECT * FROM S)
INSERT INTO STUDENTDE SELECT * FROM S
mc.e: INSERT INTO table SELECT ... (the book writes the SELECT in brackets in MySQL).

mc.q: Which two principles should be followed when handling personal data?
o: Encrypt it and back it up
Use it for its original purposes only, and do not disclose it to unauthorised people
Store it in 3NF and use views
Delete it after one year and use passwords
mc.e: These are the two principles of data privacy in the book.
mc.ez: 只用于原来目的；不泄露给未授权者。

mc.q: A doctor uses students' medical data for targeted advertising of medical services. This
o: is fine because the doctor collected it
violates data privacy because the data is not used for its original purpose
mc.e: Using data for another purpose violates data privacy.
mc.ez: 用作别的用途违反私隐。

mc.q: Access rights are
o: permissions granted to a user to perform certain operations on specific data
mc.e: Definition from the book.
mc.ez: 授予用户对特定数据进行某些操作的权限。

mc.q: A researcher may only search for and export data. Which right should be granted?
mc.e: Searching and exporting need SELECT only.

mc.q: A participant may edit their own personal data. Which right is needed?
mc.e: Editing existing records needs UPDATE.

mc.q: Which SQL commands belong to database schema design?
mc.e: Schema design changes table structures.

mc.q: How does a view help protect data privacy?
o: It limits which rows and columns a user can access
mc.e: A view can restrict rows (WHERE) and columns (field list).
mc.ez: 视图限制可见的行和列。

mc.q:
Given 
ACCOUNT(AID, ATYPE): (1,0),(2,1),(3,2),(4,1),(5,3)
CREATE VIEW AFILM AS SELECT * FROM ACCOUNT WHERE ATYPE IN (0,1);
What does SELECT COUNT(*) FROM AFILM return?
mc.e: ATYPE 0 or 1: AIDs 1, 2, 4 → 3.
mc.ez: ATYPE 为 0 或 1 的有 3 个。

mc.q: For a statistical study of students' growth, which view is most appropriate?
o: SELECT SID, SNAME, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT
SELECT SEX, AGE, WEIGHT, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT
mc.e: Remove fields that identify a person.
mc.ez: 去掉可识别身份的字段。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Checkpoint 5.7 Q1(c) (p.302), adapted

mc.q:
Given
P(PNUM, TNUM, PNAME): ('313',2,'Connor'),('579',2,'Kara'),
('684',2,'Alice'),('500',2,'Markus'),('101',1,'Ivy')
How many rows does SELECT PNAME FROM P WHERE TNUM = (SELECT TNUM FROM P WHERE PNUM = '579') return?
mc.e: Kara is in team 2, which has 4 members including Kara.
mc.ez: Kara 在第 2 队，共 4 人（含她自己）。

sq.q:
A clinic stores patients' medical records in one table RECORD(PID, PNAME, SEX, AGE, DID, DNAME, DOA, DIAG), where DID/DNAME are the doctor's ID and name, DOA the date of appointment and DIAG the diagnosis.
PIDPNAMESEXAGEDIDDNAMEDOADIAG
123KaiM2702Mia2023-03-01Diarrhoea
124AvaF4202Mia2023-03-01Flu
125LeoM1802Mia2023-03-02Flu
123KaiM2701Ben2023-02-28Allergies

parts.q: Give an example to illustrate deletion anomaly from the table RECORD.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Deleting the record of Kai's appointment on 2023-02-28 (the only record of doctor 01) [1]
will also remove the data of doctor Ben (DID 01, DNAME Ben) [1]

parts.q: (i) Which attribute does SEX depend on? (ii) Which attribute does DNAME depend on?
parts.ms:
(i) PID [1]
(ii) DID [1]

parts.q: Normalise the table RECORD into third normal form. Write down the database schema of all tables. Underline all primary keys and identify all foreign keys.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
PATIENT(PID, PNAME, SEX, AGE) [1]
DOCTOR(DID, DNAME) [1]
APPOINTMENT(PID, DID, DOA, DIAG), PID and DID are foreign keys referencing PATIENT and DOCTOR [1]
(Accept a surrogate key such as AID for APPOINTMENT with PID, DID as FKs.)

parts.q: Wilson suggests storing the date of birth instead of the age of the patient. Why?
parts.ms:
Age changes every year, so stored ages become out of date / must be updated regularly [1]
Date of birth never changes, and the age can be calculated from it when needed [1]

sq.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Chapter Exercise Q1 (p.305-306)

sq.q: A university stores course enrolment in three tables: STUDENT(SID, FNAME, LNAME, EMAIL), COURSE(CID, CNAME, CREDIT) and ENROL(SID, CID1, CID2, CID3), where CID1 is NOT NULL and CID2, CID3 may be NULL.

parts.q: Each student can enrol in 0 to 3 courses. Draw an ER diagram for the database design. You may omit the attributes.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Entity types Student and Course with a relationship (e.g. Enrol in) [1]
Cardinality M:N (a student takes many courses; a course has many students) [1]
Participation: student side optional (0 courses possible), course side optional/reasonable [1]

parts.q: Daniel claims that the tables are in third normal form as there is no transitive functional dependency. Explain why he is wrong.
parts.ms:
CID1, CID2, CID3 are repeating attributes [1]
so ENROL is not in 1NF, and therefore cannot be in 3NF [1]

parts.q: Normalise the tables into third normal form. Write down the database schema of all tables. Underline all primary keys and identify all foreign keys.
parts.ms:
STUDENT(SID, FNAME, LNAME, EMAIL) [1]
COURSE(CID, CNAME, CREDIT) [1]
ENROL(SID, CID), SID and CID are foreign keys referencing STUDENT and COURSE [1]

parts.q: Each course now belongs to exactly one faculty, and each faculty can have multiple courses. Draw an ER diagram for COURSE and FACULTY.
parts.ms:
Faculty 1 — Have — M Course [1]
Course side: each course must belong to exactly one faculty (mandatory, 1 next to Faculty); faculty has one or more courses [1]

sq.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Chapter Exercise Q2 (p.306)

sq.q:
A teacher stores exam question information in QUESTION(YEAR, QUESTION, MARK, TCODE, TOTALMARK) and TOPIC(TCODE, TNAME).
YEARQUESTIONMARKTCODETOTALMARK
2020110A21
2020211B21
202119B19
2021210C19

parts.q: What are the primary keys of QUESTION and TOPIC respectively?
parts.ms:
QUESTION: YEAR + QUESTION [1]
TOPIC: TCODE [1]

parts.q: The teacher usually searches for questions by topic code. To speed up data retrieval without changing the table structure, what should he do?
parts.ms:
Create an index [1] on TCODE of QUESTION [1]
CREATE INDEX QTCODE ON QUESTION (TCODE);

parts.q: He claims the tables are in 3NF as there is no transitive functional dependency. Explain briefly why he is wrong.
parts.ms:
TOTALMARK depends on YEAR only, which is part of the primary key [1]
This is a partial functional dependency, so QUESTION is not in 2NF and hence not in 3NF [1]

parts.q: Normalise the tables into 3NF. Write down the schemas of all tables, underline all primary keys and identify all foreign keys.
parts.ms:
PAPER(YEAR, TOTALMARK) [1]
QUESTION(YEAR, QUESTION, MARK, TCODE), YEAR is FK referencing PAPER, TCODE is FK referencing TOPIC [1]
TOPIC(TCODE, TNAME) [1]

sq.src: Textbook EA Ch5 Chapter Exercise Q3 (p.307)

sq.q:
A retail chain uses PROD(PID, CAT, PNAME, SID, PRICE, STOCK, SNAME, SLOCAT, SKNAME) to manage products, where SID identifies the shop and SKNAME is the shopkeeper. The primary key is PID+SID.
PIDPNAMESIDPRICESNAMESLOCATSKNAME
1T-shirt179.9HomeZoneTuen MunCadan
2Coffee Maker1400HomeZoneTuen MunCadan
4Smartphone32580FastTechShatinKen
5Board game2156HappyToyTsing YiTom
7Toy gun254.5HappyToyTsing YiTom

parts.q: The shopkeeper of HomeZone changes from Cadan to Abby and only one record is updated. Will there be an anomaly? If yes, name it and explain.
parts.ms:
Yes, update anomaly [1]
Cadan is stored in more than one record; the other record(s) still show Cadan, so the data becomes inconsistent [1]

parts.q: The price of the board game at HappyToy changes and one record is updated. Will there be an anomaly? Explain.
parts.ms:
No [1]
The price depends on PID+SID and is stored in only one record [1]

parts.q: The removal of which product will cause the loss of a shop's data? Name the anomaly.
parts.ms:
Smartphone (PID 4) [1]
Deletion anomaly [1]

parts.q: Give an example of a situation where an insertion anomaly occurs.
parts.ms: Adding a new shop that sells no products yet / a new product not yet sold by any shop (part of the PK would be NULL) [1]

parts.q: Normalise PROD into 3NF. Write the schemas and underline the primary keys.
parts.ms:
PRODUCT(PID, CAT, PNAME) [1]
SHOP(SID, SNAME, SLOCAT, SKNAME) [1]
STOCKLIST(PID, SID, PRICE, STOCK), PID and SID are foreign keys [1]

sq.q: A bookshop chain database has the following ER diagram description: Store (Store ID, Store name, Location) M — Sell — N Book (ISBN, Book name, Publication date); the relationship Sell has attributes Stock and Price. sq.q: A school stores data in one table STUDENTDE(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH, EID, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE) with primary key SID+EID. The data is used to produce a printed annual report and is never changed after the report is made.

CLASS → CTEACH [1]

parts.q: The database designer says this denormalised table is a good choice here. Give two reasons to support the designer.

Faster data retrieval since no joins are needed [1]
Simpler SQL statements; anomalies are not a concern because the data is not updated [1]

parts.q: State two disadvantages of denormalisation in general.
parts.ms:
More storage space required / lower flexibility [1]
Higher risk of update, insertion or deletion anomalies [1]
